c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus cell wall fraction F8 vaccine
c_description: Experimental vaccine composed of a fraction of the bacterial cell-wall (F8) extracted from Brucella abortus 99. Efficacy: Level of primary immunity depended on dose, presence of oil adjuvant, and age of mouse; immunity with adjuvant continued beyond first month, peaked around fourth month, and remained stable for at least 7 months; booster injection reinforced immunity but did not increase it beyond a certain level. Immune response: Immunization with adjuvant enabled sustained immunity; booster injections enhanced existing immunity especially at low primary doses. [Ref6961:Bosseray, 1978]
c_preparation: Fraction F8 with or without oil adjuvant. [Ref6961:Bosseray, 1978]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall fraction F8 subunit vaccine
c_description: A cell wall fraction (F8) extracted by boiling sodium dodecylsulfate at 4% from Brucella abortus 99S was used as vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Protection was dose-dependent; 100 MOD of F8 gave about 35% protection (infected 46%), less effective than H38 vaccine at equivalent doses. Immune response: Recall vaccination did not improve immunity; LPS-S did not confer protection. [Ref6962:Bosseray et al, 1978]
c_preparation: F8 fraction formulated with oil adjuvant at doses equivalent to 1 x 10^9 and 1 x 10^10 bacteria, administered once or twice at 3 month intervals. [Ref6962:Bosseray et al, 1978]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis strain RM6/66 aqueous ether extract vaccine
c_description: The study examined immunogenic properties of aqueous ether extracts prepared from Brucella canis strain RM-6-66 cells. Efficacy: The aqueous ether-extracted material protected mice against Brucella suis infections. [Ref6963:Bowser et al, 1979]
c_preparation: Aqueous ether extract prepared from Brucella canis strain RM-6-66 cells grown on tryptose agar, ether removed, clarified by centrifugation. [Ref6963:Bowser et al, 1979]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella ovis vaccine with hydroxide adjuvant
c_description: Two killed vaccines were produced using four strains of Brucella ovis, differing by the adjuvant used (hydroxide or oil). Vaccination was applied twice at an interval of 20 days to rams under experimental and field conditions. Efficacy: Rams treated with the hydroxide adjuvant vaccine developed immunity; postvaccinal antibodies disappeared after three months. Immune response: Induction of antibodies detectable by serological tests; immunity considered solid though antibodies declined by three months. [Ref6964:Masalski, 1978]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) vaccine formulated with hydroxide adjuvant. [Ref6964:Masalski, 1978]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella ovis saline-in-oil vaccine
c_description:
Two killed vaccines were produced using four strains of Brucella ovis, differing by the adjuvant used (hydroxide or oil). Vaccination was applied twice at an interval of 20 days to rams under experimental and field conditions. Efficacy: Rams treated with the oil adjuvant vaccine built up solid immunity. Immune response: Induction of antibodies detectable by serological tests; postvaccinal antibodies disappeared after three months. [Ref6964:Masalski, 1978]
The vaccine was administered to adult ewes and rams by intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes to study local tissue reactions. Immune response: Local granulomatous inflammation around oily vaccine droplets; diffuse peritonitis observed in most animals; extraperitoneal inflammatory response at injection site noted; peritonitis persisted in approximately 20% of animals six months after intraperitoneal vaccination. [Ref7072:Bailey et al, 1988]
The study compared four vaccination methods using the inactivated Brucella ovis saline in-oil vaccine in rams. Efficacy: Two spaced doses given subcutaneously induced a more consistent, persistent, and higher magnitude serological response than a single dose or intraperitoneal administration. Immune response: The serological titre rose more rapidly and reached higher levels with two subcutaneous injections ten weeks apart; single intraperitoneal injection was least effective. [Ref7071:Bailey et al, 1987]
c_preparation:
Killed (inactivated) vaccine formulated with oil adjuvant. [Ref6964:Masalski, 1978]
Inactivated Brucella ovis formulated as a saline-in-oil emulsion. [Ref7072:Bailey et al, 1988]
Inactivated Brucella ovis vaccine formulated in saline in-oil adjuvant. [Ref7071:Bailey et al, 1987]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis phenol insoluble fractions subunit vaccine
c_description: Mouse inoculation with three different phenol-insoluble fractions extracted from Brucella melitensis was performed to study immune protection. Efficacy: Inoculation with fractions accelerated blood clearance of live Brucella and reduced bacterial multiplication in spleen; immune serum conferred good specific protection to non-immunized hosts. Immune response: Protective activity involved antibodies and other serum constituents, suggesting roles for both humoral and cellular immunity. [Ref6965:Bascoul et al, 1978]
c_preparation: Phenol-insoluble fractions 'PI', '4A', and '5' extracted from Brucella melitensis. [Ref6965:Bascoul et al, 1978]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 ribosomal fraction subunit vaccine
c_description: Ribosome preparations derived from Brucella abortus strain 19 cells were examined for immunizing activity. Efficacy: Immunity to challenge by virulent Brucella abortus 544 organisms was at least as effective as live strain 19 vaccine in mice and guinea pigs. Immune response: Development of agglutinating and complement-fixing antibodies, precipitins, and delayed hypersensitivity to Brucella abortus antigens in mice, guinea pigs, and rabbits. Ribosome preparations elicited delayed hypersensitivity reactions in chronically infected guinea pigs. [Ref6966:Corbel, 1976]
c_preparation: Ribosome preparations incorporated in Freund's incomplete adjuvant. [Ref6966:Corbel, 1976]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strains 19 and 45/20 ribosomal protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Ribosomes were isolated from Brucella abortus strains 19 and 45/20 and studied for their immunological properties. Efficacy: Ribosomes from Brucella abortus S19 induced agglutinins reacting with smooth Brucella strains; those from strain 45/20 induced agglutinins reacting with rough Brucella strains; cattle vaccinated with S19 or 45/20 vaccines developed precipitins to ribosomal components early in the immune response. Immune response: Ribosomal preparations elicited intradermal delayed hypersensitivity reactions in animals infected with Brucella abortus, Brucella melitensis, or Brucella suis; antigenic in rabbits, guinea pigs, and mice; cross-reacted with antisera to multiple Brucella species. [Ref6967:Corbel, 1976a]
c_preparation: Ribosomal preparations free of detectable lipopolysaccharide-protein agglutinogen, containing 2-3 immunodiffusion-reactive components. [Ref6967:Corbel, 1976a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 544 vaccine
c_description: Mice were infected intravenously with small numbers of live CO2-dependent Brucella abortus 544 used as vaccinal strain. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed accelerated decrease in bacterial counts preventing multiplication of challenge strain in spleens and livers compared to normal mice. Immune response: Vaccination induced acquired resistance characterized by an accelerated decreasing phase of bacterial counts after challenge, with near elimination of bacteria in spleen and liver by day six post-challenge. [Ref6968:Pardon et al, 1976]
c_preparation: Live CO2-dependent Brucella abortus 544 bacteria. [Ref6968:Pardon et al, 1976]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis fraction I subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated vaccination with a soluble antigen (fraction I) of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Vaccinated monkeys were protected against subsequent challenge with a virulent strain of Brucella melitensis. Immune response: Both fraction I and Rev. I induced significant antibody titers to Brucella melitensis; transient bacteremia observed in some monkeys. [Ref6969:Chen et al, 1976]
c_preparation: Purified soluble antigen (fraction I) of Brucella melitensis. [Ref6969:Chen et al, 1976]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine
c_description: The inactivated antigen was prepared and used to immunize guinea pigs to study immunity and macrophage migration inhibition. Efficacy: An association between macrophage migration inhibition and resistance to infection was demonstrated Immune response: Macrophage migration inhibition and agglutinin response were observed following immunization [Ref6970:Cameron et al, 1976]
c_preparation: Soluble protein antigen prepared from Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1, inactivated [Ref6970:Cameron et al, 1976]
c_antigen: soluble protein antigen from Brucella melitensis Rev I

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 vaccine with emulsion adjuvant
c_description: Mice were immunized subcutaneously with a heat-inactivated Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 vaccine incorporated into a water-in-oil emulsion. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed a decrease in challenge bacteria in the spleen during the first two days post-challenge, followed by an increase that remained lower than in unvaccinated controls; spleen weights were lower in vaccinated animals. [Ref6971:Pardon et al, 1976a]
c_preparation: Heat-inactivated Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 incorporated into a water-in-oil emulsion adjuvant. [Ref6971:Pardon et al, 1976a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis PI fraction vaccine
c_description: The PI fraction, a phenol-extracted fraction from Brucella melitensis, has been used for years in the laboratory for vaccination of laboratory and agricultural workers considered at risk. Immune response: Correlation observed between lymphocyte stimulation index, humoral antibodies to Brucella, and cutaneous response to PI in vaccinated subjects. [Ref6972:Bascoul et al, 1976]
c_preparation: Phenol-extracted fraction (PI); another phenol-extracted and peptidoglycan containing fraction (4A) was also used in vitro. [Ref6972:Bascoul et al, 1976]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain B19 phenol-insoluble fraction subunit vaccine
c_description: This prospective phase IV study involved vaccination of professionally exposed subjects who were negative to an intradermal test for previous contamination. Efficacy: Clinical effectiveness could not be accurately evaluated due to insufficient subject numbers; seropositivity reached 80% after primary vaccination but decreased after 18 months. Immune response: Booster injections restored seropositivity with a thymo-independent type response; no detectable hypersensitivity was observed; local pain occurred after 45.2% of injections and moderate systemic reactions after 5%. [Ref6973:Strady et al, 1992]
c_preparation: Vaccine composed of the phenol-insoluble fraction of Brucella abortus biotype 1 (B19 strain). [Ref6973:Strady et al, 1992]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 delta 31K vaccine
c_description:
Genetic mutant derived from strain 19 with 31K deletion was inoculated subcutaneously in calves to study bacterial survival and immune response. Efficacy: Cleared bacteria from lymph nodes more rapidly than virulent strain 2308; less lymphoid destruction; antibody titers did not persist for 16 weeks. Immune response: Induced serum antibody titers that did not persist for 16 weeks; less lymphoid destruction compared to virulent strain; no reappearance of bacteria or increase in antibody titers after dexamethasone treatment. [Ref6974:Cheville et al, 1992]
Twenty-four 10-month-old Polled Hereford heifers were inoculated subcutaneously with live cells of the mutant strain. Efficacy: All vaccinated heifers were protected; none aborted and none had Brucella abortus isolated from tissues after parturition; calves born were free of Brucella abortus. Immune response: Heifers developed antibody responses to Brucella abortus and cutaneous reactions to brucellin; antibody responses after challenge exposure indicated immunity. [Ref7021:Cheville et al, 1993]
Isogenic deletion mutant of the vaccine strain S19A with mglA gene deletion used to study macrophage response. Efficacy: Not directly reported; mutant showed higher bacterial load at 24 and 48 hours post infection compared to parental strain. Immune response: Mutant induced stronger pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine gene expression than parental strain, including IL-1α, IL-1β, TNF-α, IL6, CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCL10, CCL2, CCL5, CCL7, CCL17, CD40, ICAM1; IFNγ stimulation further increased expression of IFNß1, IL12ß, MIP1α/β, NOS2, SOD2, and FAS. [Ref7220:Jacob et al, 2016]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated vaccine derived from strain 19 with 31K gene deletion. [Ref6974:Cheville et al, 1992]
Live mutant strain S19 delta 31K [Ref7021:Cheville et al, 1993]
Live attenuated isogenic ΔmglA deletion mutant strain S19A used for in vitro infection. [Ref7220:Jacob et al, 2016]
c_model_host: Bos taurus (calves and heifers); Mus musculus splenic macrophage cell line CRL 2471 (I-13.35)

c_vaccine_name: proteinase-K-treated Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study assessed the effect of MPL and TDM adjuvants on protective responses of the proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced spleen weights and Brucella CFU compared to controls; MPL did not enhance suppression of splenic infection with this vaccine; TDM increased mean CFU when combined with proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide. Immune response: Serum IgG and IgM specific for vaccine antigens were measured; no conclusive alteration in spleen cell interleukin-1 production was observed due to wide variation. [Ref6975:Tabatabai et al, 1992]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A; trehalose dimycolate
c_preparation: Proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide given alone or combined with MPL or TDM adjuvants. [Ref6975:Tabatabai et al, 1992]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus salt-extractable protein vaccine
c_description:
The study evaluated the effect of monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) and trehalose dimycolate (TDM) as adjuvants on the protective responses of the salt-extractable protein vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination with salt-extractable protein reduced spleen weights and Brucella CFU compared to controls; MPL enhanced suppression of splenic infection when combined with salt-extractable protein; TDM had no effect on CFU with salt-extractable protein. Immune response: Serum IgG and IgM specific for vaccine antigens were measured; no conclusive alteration in spleen cell interleukin-1 production was observed due to wide variation. [Ref6975:Tabatabai et al, 1992]
The vaccine was introduced as salt-extractable proteins from Brucella abortus, evaluated for immunogenicity. Efficacy: Vaccination with as little as 0.1 microgram of CSP suppressed splenic infection, reducing viable Brucella by 5-6 logs compared to controls; protein fractions were generally effective in reducing splenic infection. [Ref6987:Tabatabai et al, 1989]
Vaccination of crossbred beef heifers with Brucella abortus salt-extractable proteins was performed to induce specific immunoglobulin isotype responses. Efficacy: Vaccinated heifers had higher antibody responses than baseline for at least 31 weeks post-vaccination; however, after challenge exposure, no significant differences in antibody responses were detected between vaccinated and nonvaccinated heifers; vaginal antibody responses did not correlate with protection; serotests could distinguish baseline titers from those of heifers that aborted and were culture-positive but could not consistently distinguish vaccinates from challenge-exposed cattle or differentiate aborted from non-aborted challenge-exposed heifers. Immune response: Vaccination induced Brucella-specific IgG and other immunoglobulin isotypes in serum and vaginal mucus; vaginal IgM was detected only at abortion; vaginal IgA was specific for virulent infection and was effective in distinguishing vaccinated from challenge-exposed heifers and aborted from non-aborted heifers; serum IgA was detected up to 13 weeks after abortion. [Ref6990:Hall et al, 1989]
Soluble salt-extractable protein antigens from Brucella abortus, mainly from the periplasmic space and nonporin outer membrane proteins, were isolated using mild extraction methods. Efficacy: Immunization with dodecanoyl-modified proteins decreased humoral antibody levels without loss of protective activity in lemmings. Immune response: Protein preparations were antigenic in guinea pigs, rabbits, and cattle, and immunogenic in lemmings, guinea pigs, and cattle; chemical modification enhanced immunogenicity while reducing humoral antibody levels. [Ref7006:Tabatabai et al, 1984]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A; trehalose dimycolate | no
c_preparation:
Salt-extractable protein given alone or combined with MPL or TDM adjuvants. [Ref6975:Tabatabai et al, 1992]
Vaccines contained salt-extractable proteins (CSP); chemically modified dodecanoyl-CSP vaccines were also tested but showed no additional advantage. [Ref6987:Tabatabai et al, 1989]
Soluble protein preparations, including chemically modified proteins with dodecanoyl anhydride to enhance immunogenicity. [Ref7006:Tabatabai et al, 1984]

c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); Dicrostonyx rubricatus (lemmings); lemmings; guinea pigs; rabbits; Cattle

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutants of Brucella abortus S19, a vaccine strain, were generated by gene replacement to study their survival and pathogenicity. Efficacy: The S19 Cu-Zn SOD mutant showed approximately 10-fold lower splenic levels than the parental strain through 26 days postinfection in mice, indicating reduced survival; infection declined sharply thereafter with no organisms detected by 105 days. [Ref6976:Tatum et al, 1992]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 with Cu-Zn SOD gene deletion replaced by a kanamycin resistance marker. [Ref6976:Tatum et al, 1992]
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (Cu-Zn SOD) deletion mutant
c_model_host: HeLa cells; J774 mouse macrophagelike cell line; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain S2308 Cu-Zn SOD deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutants of Brucella abortus S2308, a virulent strain, were generated by gene replacement to analyze survival and pathogenicity. Efficacy: The S2308 Cu-Zn SOD mutant showed lower splenic levels and reduced spleen weights in infected mice compared to wild-type S2308, indicating reduced survival and pathogenicity. [Ref6976:Tatum et al, 1992]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain S2308 with Cu-Zn SOD gene deletion replaced by a kanamycin resistance marker. [Ref6976:Tatum et al, 1992]
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (Cu-Zn SOD) deletion mutant
c_model_host: HeLa cells; J774 mouse macrophagelike cell line; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: B. abortus vaccine strain 19-BA with multiresistance
c_description: The study showed the possibility of preparing a Brucella abortus vaccine strain 19-BA with multiresistance to antibiotics by spontaneous induction of rifampicin resistance and transformation with a nonconjugative hybrid plasmid pOVI conferring resistance to multiple antibiotics. Efficacy: Immunization with the multiresistant vaccine strain GSA1 and the initial strain 19-BA was demonstrated in guinea pigs. [Ref6977:Gorelov et al, 1991]
c_preparation: Live vaccine strain 19-BA with induced multiresistance to rifampicin, tetracycline, doxycycline, ampicillin, and streptomycin. [Ref6977:Gorelov et al, 1991]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis O-polysaccharide conjugate subunit vaccine
c_description: A conjugate vaccine was synthesized by covalently coupling the O-polysaccharide from Brucella melitensis 16M to bovine serum albumin (BSA). Efficacy: Immunization with 10 micrograms of conjugate conferred significant protection against virulent challenge with B. melitensis H38, similar to the reference vaccine H38. Immune response: Induced production of antibodies; boosting was efficient when administered after 10 weeks. [Ref6978:Jacques et al, 1991]
c_preparation: Conjugate of Brucella melitensis O-polysaccharide and bovine serum albumin (BSA). [Ref6978:Jacques et al, 1991]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 soluble protein extract subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the adjuvant effects of DDA alone or combined with TDM or MDP on immune responses to a soluble protein extract of gamma irradiated Brucella abortus strain 19. Efficacy: The highest and most sustained antibody responses were elicited by the S19 vaccine; among SPEBA groups, SPEBA with DDA + TDM induced higher antibody levels and stronger delayed-type hypersensitivity responses than other adjuvant combinations. Immune response: Minimal humoral responses were induced by SPEBA alone; SPEBA with DDA + TDM induced higher antibody levels, notable delayed-type hypersensitivity, and increased IL-2 production; S19 vaccine induced the greatest IL-2 production and antibody responses; results indicate DDA + TDM combination best potentiated immune responses to the soluble antigen. [Ref6979:Dzata et al, 1991]
c_adjuvant: yes; dimethyl dioctadecyl ammonium bromide (DDA); trehalose dimycolate (TDM); muramyl dipeptide (MDP)
c_preparation: Soluble protein extract of gamma irradiated Brucella abortus strain 19 (2 mg protein per dose) administered subcutaneously with adjuvants DDA alone, DDA + TDM, or DDA + MDP. [Ref6979:Dzata et al, 1991]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus BCSP31 Salmonella chi 4064 vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
An attenuated Salmonella typhimurium chi 4064 mutant was used as a carrier for a recombinant plasmid pBA31-R7 coding for the Brucella abortus 31-kDa protein (BCSP31) to orally immunize swine. Efficacy: Orally immunized swine developed serum and intestinal antibody responses to BCSP31 and salmonella endotoxin; however, they did not develop delayed-type hypersensitivity or blastogenic responses to BCSP31. Parenteral immunization with BCSP31 plus Freund incomplete adjuvant did induce delayed-type hypersensitivity. Immune response: Effective stimulation of mucosal and systemic antibody-mediated immunity was observed after oral immunization with recombinant S. typhimurium expressing BCSP31, but no antigen-specific delayed-type hypersensitivity or blastogenic response was induced by this route. [Ref6980:Stabel et al, 1991]
An attenuated Salmonella typhimurium chi 4064 mutant was used as a carrier for a plasmid coding for the Brucella abortus 31-kDa protein (BCSP31). Efficacy: The vaccine induced serum and intestinal antibody responses to BCSP31 and Salmonella endotoxin but did not induce delayed-type hypersensitivity or strong cell-mediated immunity. Immune response: Effective stimulation of antibody-mediated immunity; poor induction of cell-mediated immune response to BCSP31 in BALB/cByJ mice. [Ref6984:Stabel et al, 1990]
c_preparation:
Oral administration of S. typhimurium chi 4064 carrying plasmid pBA31-R7 expressing BCSP31 protein; no adjuvant used. [Ref6980:Stabel et al, 1991]
Recombinant plasmid pBA31-R7 expressing BCSP31 was introduced into attenuated Salmonella typhimurium chi 4064 (delta cya delta crp mutant). [Ref6984:Stabel et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus BCSP31 deletion vaccine
c_description: The BCSP31 gene encoding a 31-kDa salt-extractable immunogenic protein was deleted from Brucella abortus strains by replacement with an antibiotic resistance marker gene. [Ref6981:Halling et al, 1991]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strains with BCSP31 gene deletion constructed by electroporation and recombination; antibiotic-resistant transformants isolated. [Ref6981:Halling et al, 1991]
c_model_host: Mus musculus macrophagelike cell line J774; HeLa cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis-vitamin E adjuvant vaccine
c_description: Rams vaccinated at 6-8 months of age with a water-in-oil Brucella ovis-vitamin E adjuvant vaccine. Efficacy: Rams vaccinated with the vitamin E adjuvant vaccine had significantly higher serum antibody levels than those vaccinated with commercial B. ovis bacterin or B. melitensis Rev. 1; higher antibody levels persisted two years post-vaccination. Immune response: Elevated and sustained serum antibody levels indicating a strong serological response, likely boosted by natural infection. [Ref6982:Tengerdy et al, 1991]
c_preparation: Water-in-oil emulsion with vitamin E as adjuvant. [Ref6982:Tengerdy et al, 1991]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus polyclonal anti-idiotype antibody subunit vaccine
c_description: Polyclonal goat anti-idiotypic antibodies mimicking Brucella abortus antigens were generated from rabbit polyclonal idiotypes specific for a partially purified extract of B. abortus (PX III). Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed greater than 90% reduction of bacteria in the spleen compared to unvaccinated controls after challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308. Immune response: Vaccinated mice developed high serum titers of antibodies specific for Brucella abortus; immunoblotting distinguished vaccinated mice from naturally infected mice. [Ref6983:Beauclair et al, 1990]
c_preparation: Purified anti-idiotypic antibodies obtained by two-step immunoaffinity column chromatography. [Ref6983:Beauclair et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 proteinase K-treated lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Lipopolysaccharide extracted from Brucella abortus strain 2308 and treated with proteinase K. Efficacy: PKLPS was immunogenic and protective, reducing splenic bacterial load and weight. Immune response: Induced serologic responses; protective immune response comparable or superior to recombinant proteins. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]
c_preparation: PKLPS used alone or combined with other proteins. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is derived from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface proteins. Efficacy: BCSP was immunogenic and protective in mice, showing reduced splenic bacterial load and weight compared to controls. Immune response: Induced serologic responses detected by ELISA; BCSP induced a protective immune response superior to recombinant proteins. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]
c_preparation: Extracted Brucella cell surface protein (BCSP) used alone or in combination with other proteins or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP20 subunit vaccine
c_description: Subcomponent protein recovered from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface. Efficacy: BCSP20 was immunogenic and partially protective; protection thought to be due to associated immunogenic BCSP fraction. Immune response: Induced serologic responses but recombinant BCSP20 did not induce protection comparable to BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]
c_preparation: BCSP20 used alone or combined with other proteins or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Subcomponent protein recovered from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface. Efficacy: BCSP31 was immunogenic and partially protective; protection attributed to associated immunogenic BCSP fraction. Immune response: Induced serologic responses; recombinant BCSP31 did not induce protection comparable to BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]
c_preparation: BCSP31 used alone or combined with other proteins or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]

Recombinant form of BCSP20 protein. Efficacy: Recombinant BCSP20 did not consistently induce protection comparable to BCSP or PKLPS. Immune response: Induced immune responses but not protective comparable to native BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref6985:Pugh et al, 1990]
Mice vaccinated with recombinant protein rBCSP20 alone or combined with proteinase K-treated lipopolysaccharide. Efficacy: Recombinant protein rBCSP20 alone did not provide protection; combined with lipopolysaccharide provided protection. [Ref6988:Pugh et al, 1989a]

Mice vaccinated with recombinant protein rBCSP45 alone or combined with proteinase K-treated lipopolysaccharide. Efficacy: Recombinant protein rBCSP45 alone did not provide protection; combined with lipopolysaccharide provided protection. [Ref6988:Pugh et al, 1989a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus rough-strain outer membrane–peptidoglycan complex subunit vaccine
c_description: The OM-PG from rough strains of Brucella abortus was tested for its ability to induce lymphocyte responsiveness in cattle. Efficacy: Frequency of lymphocyte responsiveness increased with dose and with two inoculations compared to single inoculations; OM-PG from a rough transposon mutant induced comparable responsiveness to that from a spontaneous rough mutant; differences in lymphocyte specificity compared to strain 19 vaccine. Immune response: Induction of lymphocyte proliferation responses in cattle; lymphocytes stimulated by OM-PG had different specificities than those stimulated by strain 19 vaccination. [Ref6986:Smith et al, 1990]
c_preparation: OM-PG preparations emulsified in a commercial adjuvant; doses ranged from 400 to 8000 micrograms; administered in single or two inoculations. [Ref6986:Smith et al, 1990]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description:
The study investigated whether antibody alone could prevent infection with Brucella abortus by using monoclonal antibodies specific to the O polysaccharide. Efficacy: 82% of mice infected with 100 CFU of B. abortus preincubated with IgG2a MAb were free of infection up to 6 weeks; higher challenge doses reduced efficacy; IgG1 MAb and convalescent serum diminished but did not prevent infection. Immune response: Antibodies of appropriate specificity and isotype (IgG2a) were effective in opsonizing B. abortus and facilitating killing by activated macrophages; killing required activated macrophages and endotoxin presence in medium. [Ref6989:Winter et al, 1989]
Purified OPS from Brucella abortus 1119-3 and Brucella suis 1330 were evaluated as vaccines in field trials in Venezuela for protection of swine against Brucella suis challenge. Efficacy: Gilts vaccinated with OPS showed no serologic reactions, no abortions (100% protection), and litter sizes of 10 to 12 pigs. Immune response: No serologic reactions detected in vaccinated gilts, indicating effective protection without detectable antibody response by the assays used. [Ref7035:Lord et al, 1998]
c_preparation:
Passive administration of O polysaccharide-specific IgG2a and IgG1 monoclonal antibodies and convalescent-phase serum. [Ref6989:Winter et al, 1989]
Purified O-polysaccharide at doses of 100 to 500 micrograms; administered intramuscularly or orally; one or three doses. [Ref7035:Lord et al, 1998]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (CD-1 outbred mice); mouse peritoneal macrophages

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMPs subunit vaccine
c_description: Proteins extracted by hot saline or released into outer membrane blebs from field strains of Brucella melitensis were analyzed and found to be antigenically related to those of B. ovis. Efficacy: Not directly reported; antigenic similarity and conservation suggest potential for subcellular vaccine development. Immune response: Cross-reactions among strains indicate antigenic relatedness; immunogenic proteins conserved in infected animals. [Ref6991:Gamazo et al, 1989]
c_preparation: Subcellular proteins present in hot saline extracts and outer membrane blebs, similar in profile to B. ovis proteins. [Ref6991:Gamazo et al, 1989]
c_antigen: proteins of 43 kDa; group A (25.5 to 32.0 kDa); group B (21.5 to 22.5 kDa); group C (18.0 to 19.5 kDa); group D (13.0 to 15.5 kDa)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis strain S105 vaccine
c_description: A mutant strain S105 was selected from Brucella suis strain 2 after chemical mutagenesis with diethyl sulphate (DES) to reduce residual virulence. Efficacy: Strain S105 was as effective as the parent strain 2 in stimulating protective immunity to Brucella melitensis in sheep. Immune response: Not reported explicitly; implied protective immunity stimulation in sheep. [Ref6992:Zhao et al, 1989]
c_preparation: Oral vaccine formulation of the mutant strain S105. [Ref6992:Zhao et al, 1989]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus strain 2308 cell envelope vaccine
c_description: Cell envelopes from virulent strain 2308 were used as nonliving vaccine antigens administered with various adjuvants. Efficacy: Equivalent protection at 1 week post-infection regardless of adjuvant used. Immune response: Early protection largely due to O antibodies; T cell-mediated immunity had a subsidiary role. [Ref414:Montaraz et al., 1986]
c_adjuvant: yes; phosphate-buffered saline, incomplete Freund adjuvant, or trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Cell envelopes administered in phosphate-buffered saline, incomplete Freund adjuvant, or TDM and MDP adjuvant. [Ref414:Montaraz et al., 1986]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall fraction PG subunit vaccine
c_description: Mice were vaccinated intravenously with a cell-wall fraction (PG) from Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Immune serum and splenic cells from vaccinated mice strongly reduced splenic infection over time; combined transfer showed additive effect only transiently at 2-3 weeks post-challenge when serum was injected after challenge; no additive or antagonistic effect after 21 days; liver infection not notably modified until 21 days when both helped reduce infection. Immune response: Protection mediated by both humoral (immune serum) and cellular (splenic lymphocytes) immunity; combined effects not additive beyond early time points; serum reduced initial spleen colonization when injected before challenge. [Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]
c_preparation: Cell-wall fraction (PG) from Brucella abortus used as vaccine antigen; no adjuvant mentioned. [Ref6993:Plommet et al, 1986]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 chemically modified salt-extractable protein (dCSP) subunit vaccine
c_description: Beef heifers were vaccinated on Day 0 with chemically modified salt-extractable protein (dCSP) from Brucella abortus Strain 19 in Freund's complete adjuvant; a booster was given six weeks later with either homologous or heterologous vaccine. Efficacy: No significant protection observed; 60 to 83% of vaccinated heifers aborted and 70-83% were culture positive after challenge, similar to controls Immune response: Vaccination stimulated marked antibody responses and increased cell-mediated immune response measured by lymphocyte blast transformation; antibody responses increased rapidly after challenge and were higher in heifers that aborted; LBT responses were higher in vaccinates but not significantly different from controls [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_preparation: dCSP formulated with Freund's complete adjuvant [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 31-kDa protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 31-kDa protein, thought to be localized at or near the bacterial cell surface, was previously shown to protect against experimental brucellosis in rodents. The gene coding for this protein has been cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli, allowing production of the protein free of Brucella contaminants. Efficacy: Preliminary evidence showed protection against experimental brucellosis in rodents by the purified 31-kDa protein. [Ref6995:Mayfield et al, 1988]
c_preparation: Recombinant 31-kDa protein expressed in E. coli from its native promoter; purified protein free of Brucella contaminants. [Ref6995:Mayfield et al, 1988]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus native cell envelope subunit vaccine
c_description: Vaccines composed of native cell envelopes or outer membrane proteins of smooth strain 2308 were compared to a vaccine composed of the insoluble residue (PG) of strain 2308 cell envelopes extracted with hot sodium dodecyl sulfate. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with native cell envelopes displayed protective immunity equivalent to PG vaccine; in cattle, native cell envelope antigens induced significantly higher titers of whole cell agglutinins over 3 months than PG. Immune response: Both native and PG vaccines stimulated lymphocyte blastogenesis and delayed hypersensitivity to porin and group 3 proteins with no significant difference; native cell envelope vaccine induced higher antibody responses including antibodies to O polysaccharide. [Ref6996:Winter et al, 1988]
c_adjuvant: yes; oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Vaccines were given by injection in an oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide or without adjuvant. [Ref6996:Winter et al, 1988]
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins; porin; group 3 proteins; O polysaccharide

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 hot-SDS-insoluble cell-envelope fraction (PG) subunit vaccine
c_description: A vaccine (PG) composed of the insoluble residue of strain 2308 cell envelopes extracted with hot sodium dodecyl sulfate was compared to native cell envelope vaccines. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with PG showed protective immunity equivalent to native cell envelope vaccine; in cattle, PG without adjuvant induced negligible immune responses; revaccination with PG in adjuvant enhanced antibody production. Immune response: Both native and PG vaccines stimulated lymphocyte blastogenesis and delayed hypersensitivity to porin and group 3 proteins with no significant difference; PG induced lower antibody responses in cattle unless given with adjuvant. [Ref6996:Winter et al, 1988]
c_adjuvant: yes; oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Vaccines were administered by injection in an oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide or without adjuvant. [Ref6996:Winter et al, 1988]
c_antigen: insoluble residue of cell envelopes; porin; group 3 proteins; O polysaccharide

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fraction subunit vaccine
c_description: A protein-bound peptidoglycan fraction (PG) was used to immunize mice intravenously or subcutaneously. Efficacy: Transferred lymph node and spleen cells conferred immunity reducing Brucella counts; lymph node cells were more efficient; immunity increased for about 21 days post-transfer; immunity was partially abrogated by anti-Thy serum treatment; genetic background influenced response. Immune response: Cell-mediated immunity involving both T-enriched and B-enriched cells; immunity could be adoptively transferred; two cell-mediated immune mechanisms may be involved; expression of immunity may be genetically determined. [Ref6997:Plommet et al, 1987]
c_preparation: Protein-bound peptidoglycan fraction derived from Brucella abortus cell wall; administered intravenously or subcutaneously. [Ref6997:Plommet et al, 1987]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (DBA/2, CBA, DBA/2 x CBA F1 mice)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 BA lipopolysaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study compared different lipopolysaccharide (LPS) preparations from Brucella abortus vaccine strain 19-BA on hematopoiesis in mice. Efficacy: LPS from B. abortus vaccine strain 19-BA had a less pronounced disturbing effect on hematopoiesis than LPS from B. melitensis virulent strain 565; none stimulated formation of transitory endogenous colonies in mouse spleen. Immune response: Lipid A at doses 0.1-10 micrograms produced no activating effect on hematopoiesis characteristics studied. [Ref6998:Malikov et al, 1985]
c_preparation: LPS preparations obtained by Boivin's technique, Westphal's technique, and mild alkaline hydrolysis of Boivin's active complex. [Ref6998:Malikov et al, 1985]

c_vaccine_name: killed Brucella melitensis cells vaccine
c_description: The vaccine consisted of killed Brucella melitensis cells suspended in incomplete adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced B. abortus live cells in spleen; tetramisole treatment increased protection 3.5-fold compared to vaccine alone. Immune response: Tetramisole stimulation of vaccination was not accompanied by increases in specific antibodies as measured by three serological tests. [Ref6999:Renoux et al, 1973]
c_preparation: Killed Brucella melitensis cells formulated with incomplete adjuvant. [Ref6999:Renoux et al, 1973]

c_vaccine_name: purified killed Brucella abortus vaccine from smooth strain 544
c_description: A purified killed vaccine developed for use in man from the smooth strain 544 and previously tested in mice. Efficacy: Highly active and immunizing in mice and guinea-pigs; immunization in guinea-pigs without adjuvant; activity enhanced by water-in-oil emulsions. Immune response: Produced delayed hypersensitivity in guinea-pigs; highly agglutinogenic compared to rough strain vaccine. [Ref7000:Keppie et al, 1972]
c_preparation: Whole-culture extract; activity enhanced by water-in-oil emulsions; no adjuvant required for immunization in guinea-pigs. [Ref7000:Keppie et al, 1972]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus purified killed vaccine
c_description: A purified killed vaccine was developed for potential immunization of humans against brucellosis. Efficacy: The purified whole-culture vaccine immunized mice better than crude killed organisms, extracted washed organisms, or extracted culture supernatant vaccines. Immune response: The vaccine was less allergenic in infected guinea pigs and less toxic to mice compared to crude killed Brucella abortus suspensions. [Ref7001:Keppie et al, 1971]
c_preparation: Prepared by adding sodium dodecyl sulphate to intact cultures of virulent Brucella abortus grown in a defined medium containing erythritol; bacterial debris removed; immunogen precipitated with ethanol and redissolved in buffer. [Ref7001:Keppie et al, 1971]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 non-agglutinogenic extract subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immunisation using non-agglutinogenic extracts derived from Brucella abortus strain 45-20. [Ref7002:Sterne et al, 1971]
c_preparation: Non-agglutinogenic extracts of Brucella abortus strain 45-20 were used as the vaccine formulation. [Ref7002:Sterne et al, 1971]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus strain 45/20 outer membrane protein vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated nonliving vaccines derived from Brucella abortus rough strain 45/20 containing porin and other outer membrane protein antigens combined with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants. Efficacy: Outer membrane proteins induced highest antibody titers; increasing mineral oil improved antibody responses; immune responses sustained longer than 3 months after two vaccinations; no ill effects observed. Immune response: Strong blastogenesis responses to porin, highest antibody titers to porin-lipopolysaccharide complex with outer membrane proteins; delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions observed; immune responses exceeded those after natural or experimental infection. [Ref7003:Winter et al, 1983]
c_adjuvant: yes; trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide (N-acetylmuramyl-L-alpha-aminobutyryl-D-isoglutamine)
c_preparation: Vaccines contained trehalose dimycolate and a derivative of muramyl dipeptide at fixed doses; antigen types included whole cell, outer membrane, and detergent-extracted outer membrane proteins; mineral oil quantity was varied. [Ref7003:Winter et al, 1983]
c_antigen: porin; outer membrane proteins; outer membrane; whole cell (rough strain 45/20)

c_vaccine_name: polysaccharide cross-reacting Yersinia immune serum vaccine
c_description: Immune sera cross-reacting with Yersinia polysaccharide reduced dissemination of Brucella abortus 544 infection and caused a shift of bacteria from spleen to liver when injected simultaneously with intravenous challenge. Efficacy: Induced early effect of reduced bacterial numbers in spleen due to shift to liver but did not induce late clearance effect. Immune response: Immune sera to polysaccharide cross-reacting with Yersinia induced early reduction in splenic infection but did not promote late clearance of bacteria. [Ref7004:Plommet et al, 1983]
c_preparation: Polysaccharide antigen cross-reacting with Yersinia used to generate immune serum. [Ref7004:Plommet et al, 1983]

c_vaccine_name: protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan Brucella fraction vaccine
c_description: Mice vaccinated with a protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan Brucella fraction produced immune sera that completely stopped dissemination of Brucella abortus 544 infection to the spleen. Efficacy: Immune serum prevented dissemination of infection to the spleen and helped destroy intracellular bacteria, leading to nearly complete clearance by day 49 postchallenge. Immune response: Immune sera to protein antigens induced both early reduction of bacterial numbers in spleen (due to shift to liver) and late reduction in spleen and liver with clearance; protein antigen immune serum helped destroy intracellular bacteria. [Ref7004:Plommet et al, 1983]
c_preparation: Protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fraction of Brucella used to generate immune serum. [Ref7004:Plommet et al, 1983]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus protein-bound peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: Vaccination one month before pregnancy decreased frequency of placental colonization and number of brucella per infected placenta and per spleen in pregnant mice. Efficacy: PG fractions protected mice as well as H38 killed and B19 attenuated living vaccines. Immune response: Immunity transferred by immune serum protected against placental colonization; anti-LPS, anti-PG, and anti-killed brucella sera protected mice as effectively as vaccination. [Ref7005:Bosseray, 1983]
c_preparation: Protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fractions extracted from Brucella abortus [Ref7005:Bosseray, 1983]

c_vaccine_name: live brucellosis vaccine prepared from Br. abortus 82
c_description: The study investigated the combined use of a live Brucella abortus strain 82 vaccine and a homologous lysed antigen (glucopeptide) to enhance immune response. Efficacy: The combined administration increased the number of immune animals by 1.5-2 times compared to animals receiving only one preparation. Immune response: Synergistic effect observed on antibacterial immunity index with sequential injection of glucopeptide and live vaccine. [Ref7007:Rementsova et al, 1980]
c_preparation: Live brucellosis vaccine from Brucella abortus strain 82 combined sequentially with a lysed low-molecular Brucella component (glucopeptide). [Ref7007:Rementsova et al, 1980]

c_vaccine_name: H.38 B. melitensis killed vaccine
c_description: Mice were immunized 36 days before pregnancy with the vaccine. Efficacy: Immunized mice were protected against placental colonization by Brucella abortus challenge. [Ref7008:Bosseray, 1980]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) vaccine of Brucella melitensis strain H-38. [Ref7008:Bosseray, 1980]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus strain 45/20 whole-cell vaccine with immunoadjuvants
c_description: Whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 were combined with trehalose dimycolate or muramyl dipeptide as immunoadjuvants. Efficacy: Oil emulsions of whole cells with muramyl dipeptide reduced mean splenic Brucella by 95.1%; oil emulsions with trehalose dimycolate reduced mean splenic Brucella by 99.3% compared to controls; saline suspensions were not significantly effective. Immune response: Effective immunogenic response observed with oil emulsion formulations containing adjuvants; saline suspensions showed no significant reduction in infection. [Ref7009:Woodard et al, 1980]
c_preparation: Whole cells combined with trehalose dimycolate or muramyl dipeptide in oil emulsions; also tested as saline suspensions. [Ref7009:Woodard et al, 1980]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus strain 45/20 vaccine with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants
c_description: The study evaluated killed Brucella abortus strain 45/20 cells combined with immunopotentiators as a vaccine. Efficacy: Protection induced by bacterins containing 50 to 1,000 microgram of TDM or TDM-MDP was comparable to that of live strain 19 vaccine; bacterins with MDP alone were less effective. Immune response: Immunopotentiation was enhanced by TDM; addition of MDP to TDM-containing bacterins did not further enhance immunogenicity. [Ref7010:Woodard et al, 1981]
c_preparation: 300 microgram of killed strain 45/20 cells in 1% oil emulsion with TDM, MDP, or both. [Ref7010:Woodard et al, 1981]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PG-F8 cell wall peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: The cell wall peptidoglycan fraction (PG-F8) extracted from Brucella abortus was tested as a unique antigen. Efficacy: PG-F8 conferred good dose-dependent immunity in mice. Immune response: Immunity was dose-dependent and not affected by the presence of oil adjuvant. [Ref7011:Bosseray et al, 1980]
c_preparation: Purified cell wall peptidoglycan fraction with or without oil adjuvant. [Ref7011:Bosseray et al, 1980]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis cell wall peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: The cell wall peptidoglycan fraction (PG-F7) extracted from Brucella melitensis was tested as a unique antigen. Efficacy: PG-F7 conferred good dose-dependent immunity in mice. Immune response: Immunity was dose-dependent and not affected by the presence of oil adjuvant. [Ref7011:Bosseray et al, 1980]
c_preparation: Purified cell wall peptidoglycan fraction with or without oil adjuvant. [Ref7011:Bosseray et al, 1980]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-polysaccharide and core oligosaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Immune response: Sera from infected and vaccinated bovines recognized multiple LPS determinants; monoclonal antibodies identified nine different LPS epitope specificities; antibodies against rough B. abortus LPS epitopes cross-reacted with smooth LPS; findings relate to the structure and epitopic density of B. abortus LPS [Ref7012:Rojas et al, 1994]
c_antigen: lipopolysaccharide (LPS) epitopes including O-polysaccharide (A and C), core oligosaccharide (R1 and R2), lipid A (LA1, LA2, LA3), lipid A-associated outer membrane protein (LAOmp3-1 and LAOmp3-2)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase synthetic peptide vaccine
c_description: Three synthetic peptides based on the amino acid sequence of Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase were selected for their predicted hydrophilicity, flexibility, and antigenicity and used as vaccines singly or in combination with or without monophosphoryl lipid A adjuvant. Efficacy: Peptide 3 plus monophosphoryl lipid A afforded a 2 log reduction in bacterial load; peptide 3 without adjuvant afforded 1 log reduction; peptides 1 and 2 and recombinant SOD vaccine afforded no protection; salt-extractable proteins vaccine afforded 3 log reduction. Immune response: Peptide-specific IgG antibodies were induced and enhanced by monophosphoryl lipid A; superoxide dismutase-specific IgG antibodies were only present when salt-extractable proteins were included; peptide 3 likely stimulates cellular immune responses modulating splenic infection. [Ref7013:Tabatabai et al, 1994]
c_preparation: Peptides 1, 2, and 3 administered singly or combined, with or without monophosphoryl lipid A adjuvant. [Ref7013:Tabatabai et al, 1994]
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase synthetic peptides (peptide 1, peptide 2, peptide 3)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Omp and rough lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify protective antigens of Brucella ovis to develop a safe, specific subcellular vaccine for ram epididymitis. Efficacy: Mixtures of MAbs against specific OMPs and anti-R-LPS MAb alone conferred significant protection compared to controls; combination of OMP MAbs with anti-R-LPS MAb was strongly protective. Immune response: Protective antibodies targeted B. ovis outer membrane proteins and rough lipopolysaccharide, indicating these antigens as candidates for subcellular vaccines. [Ref7014:Bowden et al, 1995]
c_preparation: Monoclonal antibodies directed against multiple outer membrane proteins and rough lipopolysaccharide were tested individually and in combination. [Ref7014:Bowden et al, 1995]
c_antigen: outer-membrane proteins (16.5-, 25-27-, 31-34- and 36-38-kDa OMPs); rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 54-kDa HtrA homologue recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Genes encoding a 54 kDa E. coli HtrA homologue were cloned into shuttle plasmids and transfected into vaccinia virus to develop recombinant vSB54. Efficacy: vSB54 induced a humoral immune response recognizing the 54 kDa HtrA homologue. Immune response: Mice inoculated with vSB54 produced antibodies against the 54 kDa HtrA homologue protein and vaccinia virus. [Ref7015:Toth et al, 1995]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing a 54 kDa protein corresponding to the HtrA homologue. [Ref7015:Toth et al, 1995]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD recombinant vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
Genes encoding B. abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase were cloned into shuttle plasmids and transfected into vaccinia virus to develop recombinant vUBSOD. Efficacy: vUBSOD did not induce a humoral immune response against B. abortus proteins. Immune response: Mice inoculated with vUBSOD responded with antibodies to vaccinia virus but not to B. abortus Cu/Zn-SOD protein. [Ref7015:Toth et al, 1995]
Vaccination of mice with live Escherichia coli expressing Brucella Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase induced protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge. Efficacy: Induced a significant level of protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge, though less than that of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. Immune response: Induced antibodies to Cu/Zn SOD and a strong proliferative response of splenocytes stimulated with thioredoxin-Cu/Zn SOD fusion protein. [Ref7037:Oñate et al, 1999]
Immunization with Escherichia coli DH5alpha expressing Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase induces a protective immune response in mice. Efficacy: Induction of protective immune response previously reported; current study shows induction of specific cytotoxic T cells. Immune response: Vaccine induced specific cytotoxic T cells mainly from CD8+ subpopulation and IFN-gamma-producing cells mainly from CD4+ subpopulation. [Ref7085:Andrews et al, 2006]
This study evaluated the immunogenicity of a recombinant Semliki Forest virus (SFV) vector vaccine encoding Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) in cattle. Efficacy: Did not induce SOD IgG1 or IgG2 antibodies but induced specific T-cell activation. Immune response: Induced specific T-cell activation; non-significant secretion of gamma interferon; no induction of IL-4 or TNF-alpha. [Ref7088:Sáez et al, 2008]
The study identifies Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) as a key virulence factor in Brucella abortus, contributing to bacterial survival by detoxifying host-generated superoxide radicals. The research provides structural and functional insights into BaSOD, including its monomeric structure and immunogenic peptide epitopes, suggesting potential targets for vaccine development. Efficacy: Not directly reported for Brucella abortus; protective effect demonstrated for antibody against Neisseria meningitidis SOD in mice, implying potential for BaSOD-targeted vaccines. Immune response: The study highlights exposed epitopes on BaSOD that could extend immunogenic peptide design; passive immunization against related SOD in Neisseria meningitidis showed protection, suggesting immune targeting of SOD is a viable strategy. [Ref7204:Pratt et al, 2015]
c_preparation:
Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing the 28 kDa protein composed of B. abortus Cu/Zn-SOD and a portion of vaccinia virus TK gene. [Ref7015:Toth et al, 1995]
Live Escherichia coli expressing Brucella Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) fusion protein. [Ref7037:Oñate et al, 1999]
Live Escherichia coli DH5alpha expressing Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase gene. [Ref7085:Andrews et al, 2006]
Recombinant Semliki Forest virus particles carrying recombinant RNA encoding SOD (SFV-SOD) administered by intraperitoneal injection. [Ref7088:Sáez et al, 2008]
c_antigen: Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) | Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase | Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) | Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD)
c_model_host: Mus musculus (Balb/C mice); J774.A1 cells; Mus musculus; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M purE deletion vaccine
c_description: A defined purine-auxotrophic mutant of Brucella melitensis 16M was constructed by chromosomal gene replacement deleting part of purE and purK genes. Efficacy: The purE deletion mutant failed to grow in human monocyte-derived macrophages, whereas wild-type and complemented strains grew by nearly two logs, indicating attenuation. [Ref706:Drazek et al., 1995]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with purE gene deletion requiring exogenous purines for growth. [Ref706:Drazek et al., 1995]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella soluble proteins subunit vaccine
c_description: Immunization with soluble Brucella proteins (SBP) was used to study T cell responses compared to live Brucella infection. Efficacy: IL-4-producing CD4+ T cells from SBP-immunized mice failed to mediate resistance against challenge infection, unlike IFN-gamma-producing CD4+ T cells from infected mice which conferred protection. Immune response: SBP immunization induced CD4+ T cells producing IL-2 and IL-4 but no detectable IFN-gamma, indicating a Th2-type response; live Brucella infection induced CD4+ T cells producing IFN-gamma and IL-2 but not IL-4, indicating a Th1-type response associated with protective immunity. [Ref7016:Zhan et al, 1995]
c_preparation: Soluble protein antigen extracts from Brucella were used for immunization. [Ref7016:Zhan et al, 1995]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 ribosomal protein subunit vaccine
c_description:
Ribosomal preparations have been used as vaccines against several pathogens including B. abortus, conferring a high degree of protection. Efficacy: Not directly reported; inferred protection based on induction of Th1 response. Immune response: Induced antigen-specific proliferation of CD4+ T cells with a Th1 cytokine profile characterized by IL-2 and IFN-gamma transcripts and secretion of IFN-gamma, but not IL-4. [Ref7017:Oliveira et al, 1994]
The Brucella abortus L7/L12 ribosomal gene was amplified and expressed as a fusion protein in E. coli, purified, and confirmed by Western blot. Immune response: Recombinant L7/L12 protein induced proliferation of T lymphocytes, with an increased percentage of CD4+ T cells compared to control cultures. [Ref7018:Oliveira et al, 1994a]
The study explores the immunogenic potential of PLGA (poly lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticles entrapping rL7/L12 protein, an immunodominant antigen of Brucella abortus, as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant reduction in splenic bacterial load (log CFU) in vaccinated mice compared to controls after Brucella abortus 544 infection. Immune response: High IgG antibody titers with predominant IgG1 subclass indicating mixed Th1/Th2 response; strong Th1 cytokine (IFN-γ) production; increased lymphocyte proliferation indicating enhanced cellular immunity. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]
c_preparation:
Recombinant L7/L12 ribosomal protein [Ref7017:Oliveira et al, 1994]
Recombinant L7/L12 fusion protein purified by affinity chromatography. [Ref7018:Oliveira et al, 1994a]
PLGA (85:15) biodegradable and biocompatible polymer nanoparticles entrapping recombinant L7/L12 protein. [Ref7203:Singh et al, 2015a]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); Bos taurus peripheral blood mononuclear cells; Escherichia coli DH5 alpha; Mus musculus

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 19 salt-extractable proteins (BCSP) vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the effect of covalent chemical modification of Brucella abortus 19 salt-extractable proteins on immune responses. Efficacy: Acylation decreased immune responses but reduced spleen CFU and splenomegaly, indicating altered protection; monophosphoryl lipid A enhanced immunogenicity. Immune response: Acylation increased IgG antibodies and altered serologic responses; monophosphoryl lipid A markedly enhanced immunogenicity of BCSP 0-70. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]
c_preparation: Salt-extractable proteins BCSP 0-70 and BCSP 70-100 were chemically modified with acetoacetic anhydride; monophosphoryl lipid A was used as an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity of BCSP 0-70. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant BCSP20 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant proteins rBCSP20, rBCSP31, and rBCSP45 were chemically modified to assess modulation of immune responses. Efficacy: Chemical modification had no effect on protection induced by recombinant proteins. Immune response: IgG serologic responses to homologous and heterologous proteins were altered by chemical modification. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins were modified with succinic and dodecanoyl anhydrides. [Ref7019:Pugh et al, 1994]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis L7/L12 ribosomal protein vaccine
c_description: The study identified and sequenced the gene encoding the Brucella melitensis L7/L12 ribosomal protein, which is an immunodominant antigen and may explain the activity of ribosomal vaccines. Immune response: The ribosomal protein L7/L12 of Brucella is an immunodominant antigen. [Ref7020:Bachrach et al, 1994]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline extract subunit vaccine
c_description:
Vaccination with hot saline extract (HS) conferred good protection against Brucella ovis infection, with protection greatly enhanced by incorporation of QS-21 or other adjuvants. Efficacy: HS-QS-21 vaccine afforded protection against B. ovis challenge as good as that developed after primary infection and as good as or better than that provided by attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. Immune response: Protection mediated by both T lymphocytes and antibodies, with antibodies playing a substantially greater role; antibodies specific for HS proteins were predominantly IgG2a and IgG3 isotypes; immune responses targeted protein moieties of HS; rough lipopolysaccharide component was poorly immunogenic in BALB/c mice. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]
The antigenic extract Hot Saline from Brucella ovis was microencapsulated by spray-drying with different polyesters to develop microparticles smaller than 5 micrometers as a vaccine delivery system. Efficacy: Not reported (no in vivo efficacy data provided) Immune response: Formulations with higher PEC content showed higher uptake by macrophages and increased respiratory burst (oxygen peroxide release), indicating potential for immune activation. [Ref7054:Murillo et al, 2002a]
c_preparation:
Subcellular vaccine consisting of hot saline extract proteins; adjuvanted formulations included QS-21 or other adjuvants. [Ref7022:Jiménez et al, 1994]
Microparticles prepared by spray-drying using poly-lactide-co-glycolide RG502H (PLGA) and blends with poly-epsilon-caprolactone (PEC) with varying ratios; formulations with higher PEC showed better macrophage uptake and less acidification. [Ref7054:Murillo et al, 2002a]
c_antigen: protein moieties of hot saline extract | Hot Saline antigenic extract

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus BCSP31 Salmonella chi 3781 vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: An attenuated Salmonella choleraesuis strain chi 3781 mutant [delta cya-12 delta(crp-cdt)19] was engineered to express the 31-kDa protein (BCSP31) from Brucella abortus via plasmid pBA31-R7 for oral immunization. Efficacy: The recombinant Salmonella choleraesuis vaccine colonized gut mucosa and deep tissues in mice and swine; mice developed serum antibodies to BCSP31 and Salmonella endotoxin, while swine showed strong DTH responses to BCSP31 and Salmonella antigens but no significant antibody responses. Immune response: Mice developed serum antibodies to BCSP31 and Salmonella endotoxin and local intestinal antibody response to Salmonella endotoxin but not BCSP31; no DTH response to BCSP31 but positive to Salmonella antigen. Swine showed strong DTH responses to both BCSP31 and Salmonella soluble antigen, indicating cell-mediated immunity, confirmed by histology, but lacked significant antibody responses. [Ref7023:Stabel et al, 1993]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella choleraesuis chi 3781 mutant carrying recombinant plasmid pBA31-R7 expressing Brucella abortus BCSP31 protein. [Ref7023:Stabel et al, 1993]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus TNP-conjugated lipopolysaccharide carrier vaccine
c_description: The study investigates the carrier nature of lipopolysaccharide from Brucella abortus (LPS-BA) in evoking humoral immune responses, suggesting that LPS-BA can substitute for whole Brucella abortus organisms in vaccine development. Efficacy: TNP-LPS-BA generated anti-TNP antibody responses in various mouse strains including immunodeficient mice, with higher titers of IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG2b antibodies in C3H/HeJ mice compared to TNP-LPS from E. coli; LPS-BA stimulated B cells more effectively than LPS-EC in C3H/HeJ mice. Immune response: LPS from Brucella abortus acts as a T-cell-independent type 1 (TI-1) carrier antigen, eliciting humoral immune responses including IgG subclass antibodies even in T-cell deficient mice, indicating its ability to directly stimulate B cells. [Ref7024:Betts et al, 1993]
c_preparation: Trinitrophenyl (TNP)-conjugated LPS from Brucella abortus (TNP-LPS-BA) was used to immunize mice. [Ref7024:Betts et al, 1993]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c, athymic BALB/c nu/nu, CBA/N, C3H/HeJ mice)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella 18-kDa outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 18 kD outer membrane protein (OMP) was synthesized in Escherichia coli cells and used as a preparation to study its influence on protection against brucellosis. Efficacy: The 18 kD OMP protected 66.7% of experimental animals against brucellosis, compared to 78.0% protection by the commercial live vaccine. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]
c_preparation: OMP preparation obtained by genetic engineering technique expressed in E. coli. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella 38-kDa outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 38 kD outer membrane protein (OMP) was synthesized in Escherichia coli cells and used as a preparation to study its influence on protection against brucellosis. Efficacy: The 38 kD OMP did not provide protective activity; the infectivity index and colony forming units in spleen were higher in vaccinated animals than controls. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]
c_preparation: OMP preparation obtained by genetic engineering technique expressed in E. coli. [Ref7025:Seliutina et al, 1993]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 salt-extractable protein subunit vaccine
c_description:
The study evaluated immune and protective responses induced by vaccination with six salt-extractable periplasmic protein fractions from Brucella abortus strain 19. Efficacy: Vaccines prepared from BCSP70 and BCSP100 were moderately protective and immunogenic; subfractions BCSP100-A through BCSP100-D were not protective without MPL; MPL enhanced protection or was neutral with BCSP70, BCSP100, BCSP100-C, and BCSP100-D; some subfractions increased bacterial survival and splenomegaly. Immune response: MPL modulated immunoglobulin G responses induced by BCSP70, BCSP100, and BCSP100-B vaccines; overall, certain protein fractions may act as virulence or survival factors in infection. [Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]
Beef heifers were vaccinated on Day 0 with salt-extractable protein (CSP) from Brucella abortus Strain 19 in Freund's complete adjuvant; a booster was given six weeks later with either homologous or heterologous vaccine. Efficacy: No significant protection observed; 60 to 83% of vaccinated heifers aborted and 70-83% were culture positive after challenge, similar to controls Immune response: Vaccination stimulated marked antibody responses and increased cell-mediated immune response measured by lymphocyte blast transformation; antibody responses increased rapidly after challenge and were higher in heifers that aborted; LBT responses were higher in vaccinates but not significantly different from controls [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) from Salmonella typhimurium Re mutant strain | yes; Freund's complete adjuvant
c_preparation:
Vaccines were prepared from BCSP70 and BCSP100 protein fractions and four subfractions (BCSP100-A through BCSP100-D) purified by anion-exchange HPLC; some formulations included monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) as an immune response modifier. [Ref7026:Pugh et al, 1996]
CSP formulated with Freund's complete adjuvant [Ref6994:Confer et al, 1987]
c_antigen: salt-extractable periplasmic proteins (BCSP70, BCSP100, and subfractions BCSP100-A, BCSP100-B, BCSP100-C, BCSP100-D) | salt-extractable protein (CSP)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis purE deletion vaccine
c_description: A purE mutant (delta purE201) of Brucella melitensis 16M was previously shown to be attenuated in cultured human monocytes and was evaluated here for attenuation in mice. Efficacy: The delta purE201 mutant showed significantly reduced bacterial counts in spleen, liver, and lungs compared to wild-type 16M; it was essentially eliminated from mice by 8 weeks postinfection, whereas 16M persisted at high levels; mice infected with delta purE201 had only mild, transient splenomegaly and no serum interleukin-6 production. Immune response: Mice infected with delta purE201 showed mild transient splenomegaly and no serum interleukin-6; CD4- and CD8-positive lymphocytes declined initially in both groups; MAC-1-positive cells increased transiently with delta purE201 infection but returned to normal by 4 weeks, unlike sustained increase with 16M infection. [Ref1799:Crawford et al., 1996]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M with purE gene deletion (delta purE201). [Ref1799:Crawford et al., 1996]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); cultured human monocytes

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis purE deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: Young goats were inoculated subcutaneously with the purE deletion mutant to evaluate host responses. Efficacy: The purE mutant was cleared from visceral tissues by PID 84, with no bacteria detected in mammary lymph nodes or spleen at necropsy; it produced immune responses and less severe pathologic changes compared to the virulent parental strain. Immune response: Serum antibody titers peaked at PID 14; marked germinal center formation and medullary plasmacytosis by PID 28; brucellar antigens detected in capsular granulomas; bacteria found mainly in macrophages and small lymphocytes. [Ref7027:Cheville et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Genetic deletion mutant (deltapurE201) of Brucella melitensis strain 16M. [Ref7027:Cheville et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp28 vaccine
c_description: The study cloned and characterized a 28-kDa outer membrane protein (Omp28) from Brucella melitensis, recognized by the humoral immune response in human brucellosis, suggesting its potential use as a vaccine antigen. Immune response: Omp28 was recognized by antibodies from human patients infected with B. abortus and B. suis, rabbit antisera against killed B. abortus, and sera from mice and goats infected with smooth B. melitensis strains, indicating immunogenicity and cross-reactivity. [Ref7028:Lindler et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 htrA gene deletion vaccine
c_description: An htrA deletion mutant was created in the bovine vaccine strain Brucella abortus S19 by replacing most of the htrA gene with a kanamycin resistance gene. Efficacy: The htrA mutant showed significantly reduced spleen colonization at 1 week and enhanced clearance at 4 and 7 weeks post-infection compared to parental strain; colonization was equivalent at 2 and 3 weeks. Immune response: The mutant elicited equivalent delayed type hypersensitivity and antibody responses compared to the parental strain in BALB/c mice. [Ref7029:Robertson et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 with htrA gene deletion; kanamycin-resistant, ampicillin-sensitive. [Ref7029:Robertson et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BP26 protein vaccine
c_description: A 26-kDa periplasmic protein (BP26) was cloned from Brucella abortus strain 19 genome and characterized; it is a novel protein with no similarity to previously sequenced genes. Immune response: BP26 protein allowed differentiation between vaccinated and infected bovines and detection of infected rams; sera from human patients with active brucellosis were positive, while sera from chronic or asymptomatic patients were nonreactive, indicating potential diagnostic value. [Ref7030:Rossetti et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus heat-vaccine
c_description: The study investigates heat-inactivated Brucella abortus as a potential vaccine candidate capable of inducing a strong cellular immune response associated with IFN-gamma production and cytotoxic T-cell development. Efficacy: Heat-inactivated B. abortus induced IL-12 secretion by monocytes, which enhanced IFN-gamma mRNA expression in T cells and increased NK cell cytolytic activity, indicating potential for directing immune response towards Th1-Tc1 differentiation. Immune response: B. abortus stimulation led to IL-12 p40 mRNA and protein secretion, upregulation of costimulatory molecules B7.1, B7.2, and intercellular adhesion molecule 1 on monocytes, increased IFN-gamma expression in T cells, and enhanced NK cytolytic activity, supporting activation of cellular immunity. [Ref7031:Zaitseva et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Heat-inactivated whole Brucella abortus bacteria were used to stimulate human monocytes. [Ref7031:Zaitseva et al, 1996]
c_model_host: human elutriated monocytes; T cells; NK cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Neisseria meningitidis GBOMP adjuvant
c_description: A mucosal vaccine against brucellosis was developed consisting of Brucella melitensis LPS complexed with Neisseria meningitidis GBOMP as a mucosal adjuvant. Efficacy: The complex vaccine induced higher levels of IgG and IgA antibodies specific for B. melitensis LPS in lung lavages and antibody-secreting cells in lungs, spleen, and cervical nodes compared to LPS alone; serum antibodies cross-reacted with B. abortus LPS. Immune response: The vaccine stimulated strong mucosal IgA and IgG responses in lungs of mice and guinea pigs; mice showed a prominent serum IgG1 response suggesting a Th2 type response; LPS alone induced mostly IgM in mice and lower antibody levels in guinea pigs. [Ref7032:Van et al, 1996]
c_adjuvant: yes; outer membrane protein (GBOMP) of Neisseria meningitidis
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated as a complex of Brucella melitensis LPS with the outer membrane protein GBOMP from group B Neisseria meningitidis. [Ref7032:Van et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus GroEL protein produced and purified for evaluation as a vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Not directly reported; induced Th1-type immune responses and DTH reactions. Immune response: Induced CD4+ T cell proliferation and secretion of IL-2 and IFN-gamma, consistent with Th1 immunity. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroES subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus GroES protein produced and purified for evaluation as a vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Not directly reported; induced Th1-type immune responses and DTH reactions. Immune response: Induced CD4+ T cell proliferation and secretion of IL-2 and IFN-gamma, consistent with Th1 immunity. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus UvrA subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus proteins UvrA, GroES, and GroEL were produced as fusion proteins in E. coli and purified for evaluation as potential vaccine antigens. Efficacy: Not directly reported; proteins induced T cell proliferation and Th1 cytokine secretion, and elicited DTH responses, suggesting potential protective capacity. Immune response: CD4+ T cells proliferated in response to rUvrA, rGroES, and rGroEL with secretion of IL-2 and IFN-gamma but not IL-4, indicating a Th1-type immune response. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion proteins expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography. [Ref7033:Oliveira et al, 1996]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain M-1 BP26-deficient vaccine
c_description: A genetically engineered Brucella abortus mutant strain M-1 lacking BP26 expression was evaluated for protective properties compared to the parental S19 vaccine strain. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with M-1 were similarly protected as those vaccinated with S19 against challenge. Immune response: Mice vaccinated with M-1 did not develop antibodies against BP26, but protective immune response was maintained. [Ref7034:Boschiroli et al, 1997]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain M-1 mutant vaccine deficient in BP26 protein. [Ref7034:Boschiroli et al, 1997]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study tested nucleic acid vaccination using the Brucella abortus ribosomal L7/L12 gene expressed in muscle cells of mice. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with pcDNA3-encoded L7/L12 gene showed significant protection against B. abortus S2308 infection; p6-L7/L12 did not confer significant protection compared to positive controls. Immune response: The vaccine induced specific antibody and T-cell responses directed against the L7/L12 protein, demonstrating antigen-specific immunity. [Ref2290:Kurar and Splitter, 1997]
c_preparation: The L7/L12 gene was delivered via eukaryotic expression plasmids pcDNA3 (human CMV promoter) and p6 (bovine MHC 1 promoter) by single intramuscular injection. [Ref2290:Kurar and Splitter, 1997]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified OPS from Brucella abortus 1119-3 and Brucella suis 1330 were evaluated as vaccines in field trials in Venezuela for protection of swine against Brucella suis challenge. Efficacy: Gilts vaccinated with OPS showed no serologic reactions, no abortions (100% protection), and litter sizes of 10 to 12 pigs.
