Immune response: No serologic reactions detected in vaccinated gilts, indicating effective protection without detectable antibody response by the assays used. [Ref7035:Lord et al, 1998]
c_preparation: Purified O-polysaccharide at doses of 100 to 500 micrograms; administered intramuscularly or orally; one or three doses. [Ref7035:Lord et al, 1998]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 Trypanosoma cruzi CRA recombinant vaccine
c_description: A vector was developed to express foreign antigens in the Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine by cloning regulatory sequences and signal peptide of the bcsp31 gene into a broad-host-range plasmid, enabling expression of a Trypanosoma cruzi repetitive antigen. Efficacy: The recombinant antigen induced a good antibody response against the Trypanosoma cruzi antigen; expression did not alter bacterial growth or cause toxicity. Immune response: Induction of a good antibody response against the Trypanosoma cruzi repetitive antigen was observed. [Ref7036:Comerci et al, 1998]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed and secreted into the Brucella periplasmic space using plasmid pBEV in the live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19. [Ref7036:Comerci et al, 1998]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant Escherichia coli expressing the omp31 gene of Brucella melitensis, coding for a major outer membrane protein. Efficacy: No significant protection against challenge with smooth Brucella melitensis H38S was observed. Immune response: Induction of specific antibodies to Brucella melitensis in serum, increased after boosting; significant specific proliferative response of spleen cells 5 weeks after first immunization, but response did not persist. [Ref7038:Guilloteau et al, 1999]
Current Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine has many disadvantages prompting development of alternative vaccines and delivery systems. Efficacy: Invasive E. coli vaccine expressing Omp31 induced significant protection against B. melitensis challenge in mice. Immune response: E. coli delivery system is non-pathogenic and delivers antigens to antigen-presenting cells promoting cellular immune responses; natural adjuvant properties suggested. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]
Since Brucella infection mostly occurs through mucosal surfaces, a vaccine delivered via mucosal route can enhance immune response to control brucellosis. Omp31 is a major outer membrane protein and protective antigen of Brucella. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant increases in sIgA, serum IgA, IgM, and total IgG antibodies with live vaccine; killed vaccine induced significant increases in serum IgM and total IgG; IgG2a subtype response was higher than IgG1 in both groups. Immune response: Elevated IFN-γ and IL-10 levels observed in mice immunized with recombinant L. lactis; no change in IL-4 levels; indicating induction of both humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7322:Shirdast et al, 2021]
c_preparation:
Recombinant Escherichia coli expressing the omp31 gene; boosting with a dose ten times lower than the first. [Ref7038:Guilloteau et al, 1999]
Escherichia coli DH5α engineered to express inv gene from Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and hly gene from Listeria monocytogenes, carrying plasmid expressing B. melitensis Omp31. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]
Recombinant Lactococcus lactis displaying Omp31 antigen was constructed by fusing omp31 gene with usp45 signal peptide and M6 cell wall anchor in pNZ7021 expression vector; live and killed forms of recombinant L. lactis were used for oral and intraperitoneal immunization, respectively. [Ref7322:Shirdast et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 18-kDa Omp recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A recombinant vaccinia virus expressing an 18-kDa outer membrane protein of Brucella abortus was constructed using shuttle vector pMCO2 and vaccinia virus wild-type WR strain. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with the recombinant virus were not protected against challenge with virulent B. abortus 2308. Immune response: Inoculated mice produced 18-kDa protein-specific antibodies predominantly of IgG2a isotype; splenocytes showed lymphocyte proliferation and gamma interferon production upon stimulation with purified maltose binding protein-18-kDa fusion protein. [Ref7039:Vemulapalli et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing the 18-kDa outer membrane protein. [Ref7039:Vemulapalli et al, 2000]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 22.9-kDa protein vaccine
c_description: Two novel proteins from Brucella abortus strain RB51 were isolated and characterized for immunological properties. Efficacy: The 22.9-kDa protein was as effective as the live Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in protection studies. Immune response: The 22.9-kDa protein induced a strong in vitro blast transformation in lymphoid cells from previously sensitized mice. [Ref7040:Cespedes et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Purified 22.9-kDa protein used as protective immunogen. [Ref7040:Cespedes et al, 2000]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 32.2-kDa protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Two novel proteins from Brucella abortus strain RB51 were isolated and characterized for immunological properties. Efficacy: The 32.2-kDa protein had a poor protective effect under similar conditions. Immune response: The 32.2-kDa protein induced a strong in vitro blast transformation in lymphoid cells from previously sensitized mice. [Ref7040:Cespedes et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Purified 32.2-kDa protein used as immunogen. [Ref7040:Cespedes et al, 2000]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 beta-galactosidase live virulent vaccine
c_description: Recombinant strain RB51 constructed to express E. coli beta-galactosidase under Brucella groE or sodC promoters. Efficacy: Recombinant RB51 expressing beta-galactosidase maintained attenuation and protective efficacy against B. abortus 2308 challenge. Immune response: Induced specific IgG2a antibodies and IFN-gamma secretion without IL-4, indicating a Th1 type immune response to beta-galactosidase. [Ref7041:Vemulapalli et al, 2000a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain RB51 bacteria transformed with plasmids expressing beta-galactosidase. [Ref7041:Vemulapalli et al, 2000a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 HSP65 live virulent vaccine
c_description: Recombinant strain RB51 constructed to express M. bovis HSP65 under Brucella groE promoter. Efficacy: Expression of HSP65 did not alter attenuation or vaccine efficacy of strain RB51 against B. abortus 2308 challenge. Immune response: Induced specific IgG2a antibodies and IFN-gamma secretion without IL-4, indicating a Th1 type immune response to HSP65. [Ref7041:Vemulapalli et al, 2000a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain RB51 bacteria transformed with plasmids expressing HSP65. [Ref7041:Vemulapalli et al, 2000a]
c_antigen: 65-kDa heat shock protein (HSP65) of Mycobacterium bovis

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Omp16 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify protective outer membrane proteins (OMPs) of Brucella ovis as vaccine candidates by testing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against these antigens for protection in mice. Efficacy: Monoclonal antibodies to Omp16, Omp19, and Omp31 provided significant protection against B. ovis challenge, reducing spleen infection and preventing splenomegaly; mAbs to Omp31 maintained protection even in mixtures with nonprotective mAbs. Immune response: Protective immunity was mediated by antibodies targeting surface-exposed epitopes of OMPs and R-LPS, confirming the protective role of these antigens and identifying Omp31 as a promising subunit vaccine candidate against ram epididymitis. [Ref7042:Bowden et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Monoclonal antibodies against individual or combinations of OMPs and rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS) were used for passive immunization; a mouse serum raised against B. ovis hot-saline extract containing antibodies to both OMPs and R-LPS was used as a positive control. [Ref7042:Bowden et al, 2000]
c_antigen: Omp16; Omp19; Omp31; Omp10; Omp25; Omp2b; Omp1; rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL baculovirus recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_model_host: Trichoplusia ni cells; Spodoptera frugiperda (Sf9) cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroES recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_model_host: Trichoplusia ni cells; Spodoptera frugiperda (Sf9) cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HtrA baculovirus recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression. [Ref7043:Bae et al, 2000]
c_model_host: Trichoplusia ni cells; Spodoptera frugiperda (Sf9) cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL vaccinia recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The groEL gene encoding the antigenic heat shock protein GroEL from Brucella abortus was subcloned into vaccinia virus via homologous recombination and expression was confirmed by Western blotting. Efficacy: No significant level of protection was demonstrable despite induction of specific antibodies. Immune response: Mice produced GroEL and vaccinia virus specific antibodies after inoculation with the recombinant vaccine. [Ref7044:Baloglu et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing Brucella abortus GroEL protein. [Ref7044:Baloglu et al, 2000]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 18-kDa protein DNA vaccine
c_description: A single intrasplenic injection of plasmid DNA encoding the 18-kDa protein from Brucella abortus was used to induce immune responses for monoclonal antibody production. Efficacy: The technique resulted in early, strong monoclonal antibody production, with hybridomas generated up to 25 days after a single injection, indicating persistent expression of the antigen gene. Immune response: Monoclonal antibodies of IgG (IgG2b and IgG1 subtypes) and IgM isotypes were produced; antibodies recognized native and some heat-denatured recombinant 18-kDa protein; ELISA and immunoblotting confirmed strong specific antibody responses. [Ref7045:Velikovsky et al, 2000]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA containing the expression vector for the 18-kDa protein in saline; administered by intrasplenic injection. [Ref7045:Velikovsky et al, 2000]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; NS-0 myeloma cell line

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus wboA deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study investigates rough wboA mutants derived from Brucella abortus 2308 and Brucella melitensis 16M, which lack O polysaccharide due to deletion of the wboA gene essential for O chain synthesis. Efficacy: Rough B. abortus wboA mutants were more sensitive to bactericidal action of serum than rough B. melitensis mutants; OPS-deficient B. melitensis mutants were more resistant than B. abortus mutants; complement deposition and killing occurred via classical and MBL-mediated pathways. Immune response: Activation of classical and mannose-binding lectin complement pathways leading to complement deposition (iC3b, C5b-9) and bacterial killing; alternative pathway not activated. [Ref7046:Fernandez-Prada et al, 2001]
c_preparation: Rough mutants of Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis with wboA gene deletion. [Ref7046:Fernandez-Prada et al, 2001]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase mutant vaccine
c_description: A cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase mutant was generated from the Brucella abortus attenuated vaccinal strain 19 (S19) to investigate its role in virulence and vaccine efficacy. Efficacy: The mutant was completely cleared from mouse spleens after 4 weeks but retained full protective ability against virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308 challenge. Immune response: The mutant induced equivalent spleen gamma interferon mRNA and IgG2a anti-LPS antibody levels compared to parental S19 strain, but lower IgG1 anti-LPS antibody titers, suggesting a relatively exclusive Th1 immune response. [Ref7047:Briones et al, 2001]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase gene. [Ref7047:Briones et al, 2001]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline extract poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticle subunit vaccine
c_description: A hot saline antigenic extract from Brucella ovis was encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles to create a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Subcutaneous or oral administration of HS-PEC protected mice against B. ovis infection with protection similar to the Rev. 1 vaccine; subcutaneous vaccination with HS-PEC was as effective as Rev. 1 in protecting against B. abortus infection; free HS or empty PEC microparticles did not confer protection. Immune response: Subcutaneous administration of HS-PEC induced high levels of IFN-gamma and IL-2 and low levels of IL-4, indicating a combined Th1/Th2 cellular immune response; oral administration did not induce this cytokine profile. [Ref7048:Murillo et al, 2001]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of the hot saline antigenic extract encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles (HS-PEC). [Ref7048:Murillo et al, 2001]
c_antigen: hot saline antigenic extract (HS) from Brucella ovis

c_vaccine_name: DNA vaccine encoding bacterioferritin of Brucella spp
c_description: Eukaryotic expression vector pCIBFR encoding bacterioferritin constructed and verified for protein expression in COS-7 cells. Efficacy: Induced a strong and long-lived memory immune response lasting at least 3 months; elicited a typical T-helper 1-dominated immune response; did not induce moderate protection against B. abortus 544 challenge. Immune response: Induced T-cell proliferative response, strong gamma interferon production upon restimulation, and Th1-dominated cytokine and IgG isotype profile. [Ref2291:Al-Mariri et al., 2001]
c_preparation: Intramuscular injection of plasmid DNA vector pCIBFR, administered three times at 3-week intervals. [Ref2291:Al-Mariri et al., 2001]

c_vaccine_name: DNA vaccine encoding P39 of Brucella spp
c_description: Eukaryotic expression vector pCIP39 encoding P39 constructed and verified for protein expression in COS-7 cells. Efficacy: Induced higher antibody responses than bacterioferritin vaccine; elicited a strong and long-lived memory immune response lasting at least 3 months; induced a typical T-helper 1-dominated immune response; induced moderate protection against B. abortus 544 challenge. Immune response: Induced T-cell proliferative response, strong gamma interferon production upon restimulation, and Th1-dominated cytokine and IgG isotype profile. [Ref2291:Al-Mariri et al., 2001]
c_preparation: Intramuscular injection of plasmid DNA vector pCIP39, administered three times at 3-week intervals. [Ref2291:Al-Mariri et al., 2001]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL DNA vaccine
c_description: The GroEL gene from Brucella abortus was amplified and cloned into mammalian expression vectors pCMV-link and pCMV-tPA to create DNA vaccines. Efficacy: Neither immunisation route with the GroEL DNA vaccine induced significant protective immunity against Brucella abortus. Immune response: Intramuscular injection induced a predominantly Th1 response with IgG2a antibodies and high IFN-gamma production; gene gun immunisation induced a mixed Th0 response with high IgG1/IgG2a ratio and production of IL-4 and IFN-gamma. [Ref2292:Leclerq et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Two constructs were made: pCMV-link encoding a non-secreted form of GroEL and pCMV-tPA encoding a secreted form; the pCMV-link construct produced higher protein levels. [Ref2292:Leclerq et al., 2002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Lactococcus lactis recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
The study introduces the concept of using food-grade lactic acid bacteria (Lactococcus lactis) as a carrier for the Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L7/L12 antigen to develop oral live vaccines against brucellosis. [Ref7049:Ribeiro et al, 2002]
A recombinant Lactococcus lactis strain producing Brucella abortus L7/L12 antigen under a nisin inducible promoter was orally administered. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed partial protective immunity against Brucella abortus virulent strain S2308. Immune response: Induced local humoral immune response evidenced by significant anti-L7/L12 specific IgA in feces; no systemic anti-L7/L12 antibodies detected in serum. [Ref7065:Pontes et al, 2003]
c_preparation:
The L7/L12 gene was expressed in Lactococcus lactis under a nisin-inducible promoter, producing the antigen in cytoplasmic, secreted, and cell-wall-anchored forms using different signal peptides and fusion constructs to enhance yield and targeting. [Ref7049:Ribeiro et al, 2002]
Live recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing L7/L12 antigen. [Ref7065:Pontes et al, 2003]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus bacterioferritin DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was delivered using live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica serotypes O:3 and O:9 as vectors to improve protection and evaluate the role of anti-LPS antibodies. Efficacy: Induced antigen-specific Th1-type immune responses; however, only O:9 vector strains (which induce anti-LPS antibodies) conferred significant protection against B. abortus 544 infection. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific serum immunoglobulin and Th1-type responses including lymphocyte proliferation and gamma interferon production; anti-LPS antibodies detected only in O:9-immunized mice. [Ref1270:Al-Mariri et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Naked-DNA plasmids encoding bacterioferritin delivered by live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica O:3 or O:9 strains via intragastric immunization. [Ref1270:Al-Mariri et al., 2002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 Yersinia recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was delivered using live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica serotypes O:3 and O:9 as vectors to improve protection and evaluate the role of anti-LPS antibodies. Efficacy: Induced antigen-specific Th1-type immune responses; the O:9 vector carrying pCIP39 conferred the best and highly significant protection against B. abortus 544 infection. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific serum immunoglobulin and Th1-type responses including lymphocyte proliferation and gamma interferon production; anti-LPS antibodies detected only in O:9-immunized mice. [Ref1270:Al-Mariri et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Naked-DNA plasmids encoding P39 delivered by live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica O:3 or O:9 strains via intragastric immunization. [Ref1270:Al-Mariri et al., 2002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Intranasal immunization of mice with purified Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide as a noncovalent complex with Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein was performed. Efficacy: Vaccination significantly reduced bacterial dissemination to spleen and liver compared to controls at 8 weeks postchallenge (P < 0.0001 for spleen, P = 0.005 for liver). No effect was observed on lung infection. Immune response: Immunization elicited a high-titer systemic anti-LPS IgG antibody response predominantly of the IgG1 subtype, with some IgG2a, IgG2b, and IgG3. A significant mucosal antibody response was also observed. Antibody titers remained high for 16 weeks postimmunization. [Ref703:Bhattacharjee et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Purified Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide formulated as a noncovalent complex with Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein. [Ref703:Bhattacharjee et al., 2002]
c_antigen: lipopolysaccharide; group B outer membrane protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis antigenic complex HS subunit vaccine
c_description: Microparticles containing an antigenic complex from Brucella ovis (HS) were prepared by double emulsion solvent evaporation using two different polyesters for vaccine purposes against brucellosis. Efficacy: Not directly reported; however, HS-PEC microparticles showed antigen release in boosters and enhanced phagocytosis, suggesting potential effectiveness. Immune response: Not directly reported; increased phagocytosis by macrophages observed with PEC microparticles indicating potential for improved immune activation. [Ref7050:Murillo et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Antigenic complex HS encapsulated in polyester microparticles made from poly-lactide-co-glycolide acid (75:25; RG 756) or poly-epsilon-caprolactone (PEC), forming smooth spherical sub-5 micrometer particles with ~30% antigen encapsulation. [Ref7050:Murillo et al, 2002]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis Omp25 deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis mutant BM 25 lacks the major 25 kDa outer membrane protein Omp25 and was previously found attenuated in the murine model. This study evaluated its pathogenicity and protective capacity in pregnant goats. Efficacy: Vaccination with BM 25 prior to breeding resulted in 100% protection against abortion following challenge with virulent strain 16M, comparable to protection by strain Rev. 1. Immune response: Not reported explicitly; inferred protective immunity as evidenced by prevention of abortion and colonization without causing abortions. [Ref7051:Edmonds et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant BM 25 with deletion of Omp25 protein. [Ref7051:Edmonds et al, 2002]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus INTA2 vaccine
c_description:
Brucella abortus INTA2 is a novel mutant strain constructed by inactivation of two B. abortus strain 19 genes, bp26 and bmp18, replacing bp26 with the luciferase gene as a marker, aiming to reduce residual virulence and allow differentiation from field strains. Efficacy: INTA2 showed significantly reduced bacterial load in spleens during early infection and no splenomegaly, indicating reduced residual virulence; provided similar protection levels against virulent challenge as strain 19. Immune response: INTA2 induced O-side antibodies but did not express BP26, enabling differentiation of vaccinated animals from those infected with field strains by measuring anti-BP26 antibodies via agglutination test or ELISA. [Ref7052:Campos et al, 2002]
Brucella abortus M1-luc is a mutant strain derived from strain 19 vaccine in which most of bp26 sequence has been replaced by the luciferase coding gene. Efficacy: Protection against abortion was 81.8% in heifers vaccinated with M1-luc, comparable to 78.6% protection with S19 vaccine. [Ref7090:Fiorentino et al, 2008]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated double mutant strain with bp26 replaced by luciferase gene and partial deletion of bmp18, lacking drug resistance markers. [Ref7052:Campos et al, 2002]
Live attenuated mutant strain with bp26 replaced by luciferase gene. [Ref7090:Fiorentino et al, 2008]
c_antigen: bp26; bmp18; luc (marker gene) | bp26 gene replaced by luciferase coding gene
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); BALB/c mice; Bos taurus (heifers)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL/GroES/HtrA baculovirus-expressing insect-cell subunit vaccine
c_description: Baculovirus recombinants expressing individual, divalent or trivalent B. abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and/or HtrA were used as immunogens. Efficacy: No protection against B. abortus virulent strain 2308 challenge was observed. Immune response: Antibodies were detected against GroEL and HtrA but not GroES; cellular immune response evidenced by significant IFN-gamma release in mice immunized with purified HtrA-Ribi adjuvant combination. [Ref7053:Bae et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Protein-expressing whole insect cells combined with complete Freund's adjuvant. [Ref7053:Bae et al, 2002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus purified recombinant GroEL/GroES/HtrA subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified recombinant B. abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and/or HtrA were administered. Efficacy: No protection against B. abortus virulent strain 2308 challenge was observed. Immune response: Antibodies against GroEL and HtrA but not GroES; significant IFN-gamma release observed with HtrA-Ribi adjuvant immunization. [Ref7053:Bae et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Purified proteins combined with Ribi adjuvant. [Ref7053:Bae et al, 2002]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis delta Omp25 vaccine
c_description: Omp25 was examined as a potential vaccine candidate by creating a mutant strain with disruption of the omp25 gene. Efficacy: Vaccination with BM25 resulted in more than a 2 log10 reduction in bacterial load following challenge with virulent B. melitensis (P<0.01). [Ref1946:Edmonds et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain with omp25 gene disruption (BM25). [Ref1946:Edmonds et al., 2002]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis Delta Omp25 vaccine
c_description: Omp25 was examined as a potential vaccine candidate by creating a mutant strain with disruption of the omp25 gene. Efficacy: Vaccination with BO25 resulted in clearance of the challenge strain and provided 2.5 log10 greater protection against virulent B. ovis than vaccine strain Rev. 1. [Ref1946:Edmonds et al., 2002]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis strain with omp25 gene disruption (BO25). [Ref1946:Edmonds et al., 2002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate-dehydrogenase DNA vaccine
c_description: The study identified and characterized the Brucella abortus GAPDH gene and expressed it as a recombinant protein. The GAPDH gene was shown to be a single copy in the genome and functionally complemented E. coli gap mutants. Efficacy: Partial protection was induced in mice against experimental Brucella abortus infection when the GAPDH DNA vaccine was co-administered with IL-12 plasmid. Immune response: Vaccination induced gamma-interferon and tumor necrosis factor-alpha production but not interleukin-4, indicating a Th1-type cellular immune response; sera from naturally infected animals showed antibody reactivity against recombinant GAPDH. [Ref1484:Rosinha et al., 2002b]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine formulation co-administered with a murine interleukin-12-expressing plasmid. [Ref1484:Rosinha et al., 2002b]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine expressing ESAT-6 fusion protein
c_description: A recombinant RB51 strain expressing ESAT-6, a protective protein of Mycobacterium bovis, as a fusion protein with the signal sequence and additional amino terminal amino acids of SOD. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with RB51ESAT showed significantly enhanced protection against Brucella challenge compared to strain RB51 alone. Immune response: Vaccinated mice developed specific immune responses to the mycobacterial ESAT-6 protein and a strong Th1 type immune response. [Ref7056:Vemulapalli et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 strain genetically modified to express ESAT-6 fusion protein. [Ref7056:Vemulapalli et al, 2002]
c_antigen: ESAT-6 (Mycobacterium bovis protective protein); Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase signal sequence fusion

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 overexpressing SodC and Ag85A vaccine
c_description: A recombinant RB51 strain engineered to overexpress Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and simultaneously express 85A, a protective protein of Mycobacterium spp. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with RB51SOD/85A showed significantly enhanced protection against Brucella challenge compared to strain RB51 alone. Immune response: Vaccinated mice developed specific immune responses to the mycobacterial 85A protein and a strong Th1 type immune response. [Ref7056:Vemulapalli et al, 2002]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 strain genetically modified to overexpress SOD and express 85A protein. [Ref7056:Vemulapalli et al, 2002]
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); 85A (Mycobacterium spp. protective protein)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 Cu-Zn SOD HtrA two-component systems subunit vaccine
c_description: Early vaccine development studies included a subunit vaccine prepared by salt extraction of B. abortus. Efficacy: Antigenicity was not predictive of subunit vaccine effectiveness; no clear correlation with protection. [Ref7057:Halling, 2002]
c_preparation: Subunit vaccine containing proteins cloned from salt extract and antigenic or virulence-related proteins. [Ref7057:Halling, 2002]
c_antigen: BCSP31; Cu-Zn SOD; HtrA; two-component systems
c_model_host: HeLa cells; macrophage-related cell lines; Mus musculus

c_vaccine_name: manB(core) mutant vaccine
c_description: The manB(core) mutant was tested as a rough vaccine candidate in mice. Efficacy: Ineffective as a vaccine against Brucella abortus in mice. Immune response: Induced antibodies to rough LPS and outer membrane proteins but did not confer effective protection. [Ref7058:Monreal et al, 2003]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough lipopolysaccharide mutant with manB(core) gene disruption. [Ref7058:Monreal et al, 2003]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus per mutant vaccine
c_description: The per mutant was evaluated as a rough vaccine candidate in mice. Efficacy: Induced protection against Brucella abortus but less than the standard smooth vaccine strain 19; afforded similar protection to strain 19 against Brucella ovis. Immune response: Induced antibodies to rough LPS and outer membrane proteins; protection attributed largely to anti O-polysaccharide antibodies. [Ref7058:Monreal et al, 2003]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough lipopolysaccharide mutant with per gene disruption. [Ref7058:Monreal et al, 2003]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD DNA vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA vaccine encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase. Efficacy: The DNA vaccine induced a strong, significant level of protection against challenge with B. abortus strain 2308, comparable to protection induced by B. abortus vaccine strain RB51. Immune response: Induced SOD-specific antibodies with IgG2a dominance over IgG1; elicited T-cell proliferative response; induced gamma interferon production but not IL-10 or IL-4, indicating a T-helper-1-dominated immune response. [Ref564:Onate et al., 2003]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the SOD gene (pcDNA-SOD) administered by intramuscular injection. [Ref564:Onate et al., 2003]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis streptomycin dependent mutant vaccine
c_description:
The study investigates immunity induced by a streptomycin-dependent mutant of Brucella melitensis. [Ref7059:ELBERG et al, 1955]
The study investigated immunization against Brucella infection using viable and nonviable suspensions of a streptomycin-dependent mutant of Brucella melitensis. [Ref7061:HERZBERG et al, 1955]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated streptomycin-dependent mutant strain of Brucella melitensis. [Ref7059:ELBERG et al, 1955]
Viable (live) and nonviable (inactivated) suspensions of the streptomycin-dependent mutant were used. [Ref7061:HERZBERG et al, 1955]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain streptomycin non dependent vaccine
c_description: The vaccine strain was isolated and its properties and behavior studied to evaluate its ability to immunize goats against brucella infection and prevent abortion. Efficacy: Demonstrated immunization of goats against brucella infection and protection against abortion; efficacy differed between heat-killed and living cell vaccines. Immune response: Included investigation of cross-immunity between tubercle bacilli and brucellae infections using monocytes from vaccinated and unvaccinated rabbits. [Ref7060:ELBERG et al, 1958]
c_preparation: Both heat-killed and living cells of the strain were used as vaccine formulations. [Ref7060:ELBERG et al, 1958]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
c_description: The immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (rBLS) was evaluated in mice. Efficacy: Immunization with rBLS protected mice against challenge with B. abortus 544; protection levels in the spleen were similar across all adjuvants, while only BLS-Al and BLS-IFA were effective in the liver. Immune response: rBLS induced a vigorous IgG response with high titers of IgG1 and IgG2; adjuvants increased this response, with BLS-IFA being most effective. Spleen cells from immunized mice proliferated and produced IL-2, IFN-gamma, IL-10, and IL-4, indicating a mixed Th1-Th2 response. [Ref7062:Velikovsky et al, 2003]
c_adjuvant: yes; aluminum hydroxide gel; monophosphoryl lipid A; incomplete Freund's adjuvant
c_preparation: rBLS was administered alone or with aluminum hydroxide gel (BLS-Al), monophosphoryl lipid A (BLS-MPA), or incomplete Freund's adjuvant (BLS-IFA). [Ref7062:Velikovsky et al, 2003]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus 2308 delta pgm vaccine
c_description: The deltapgm strain is a phosphoglucomutase gene deletion mutant of Brucella abortus S2308 that synthesizes an incomplete O antigen resulting in a rough lipopolysaccharide phenotype. It was developed to overcome disadvantages of the S19 vaccine such as virulence in humans and interference with immune screening. Efficacy: Vaccination with the deltapgm strain induced protection levels comparable to those induced by the S19 vaccine. Immune response: The vaccine generated a proliferative splenocyte response and a cytokine profile typical of a Th1 response; no specific anti-O-antigen antibody response was detected by fluorescence polarization assay. [Ref1909:Ugalde et al., 2003]
c_preparation: Live rough-phenotype mutant strain with inability to assemble complete O side chain in LPS. [Ref1909:Ugalde et al., 2003]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus T150R1-adjuvanted vaccine
c_description: Chickens were injected subcutaneously at one day of age with oil-in-water emulsions containing the nonionic block polymer T150R1. Efficacy: Chickens treated with T150R1 polymer developed higher IgM antibody titers to sheep erythrocytes and killed Brucella abortus compared to untreated controls. Immune response: Increased IgM antibody response; no effect on cell-mediated immunity as measured by blastogenic responses; suggested stimulation of more rapid B cell migration to peripheral organs. [Ref7063:Ragland et al, 2004]
c_preparation: Oil-in-water emulsions of the nonionic block polymer T150R1 combined with killed Brucella abortus antigen. [Ref7063:Ragland et al, 2004]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus pncA mutant vaccine
c_description: The pncA mutant of Brucella abortus showed defective intracellular replication and reduced virulence in mice but retained the ability to confer protection against virulent B. abortus strain 544. Efficacy: The pncA mutant showed a 1.5-log reduction in bacterial load in mouse spleens after 10 weeks and fully retained protective ability against virulent B. abortus strain 544. [Ref7064:Kim et al, 2004]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
c_description:
The enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) is highly immunogenic due to its homodecameric structure and stability, making it a candidate scaffold for subunit vaccine design by displaying multiple copies of foreign peptides. Immune response: BLS is highly immunogenic, presumably due to its repetitive and organized homodecameric arrangement, which is expected to induce strong immune responses when displaying foreign peptides. [Ref486:Laplagne et al., 2004]
Lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) was evaluated as a protein carrier to improve antigen delivery of KETc1, a peptide from an anti-cysticercosis vaccine. Efficacy: KETc1 preserved its protective capacity when expressed as a recombinant chimeric protein with BLS. Immune response: KETc1 and BLS-KETc1 were not restricted by MHC H-2(d), H-2(k), or H-2(b) haplotypes, although KETc1 is preferentially presented in H-2(b); BLS is a potent delivery system improving subunit vaccine immunogenicity. [Ref7066:Sciutto et al, 2005]
The enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) is a highly immunogenic protein that forms a stable dimer of pentamers and can be engineered to present foreign peptides without disrupting folding, making it efficient to elicit systemic and oral immunity without adjuvants. Efficacy: Not directly reported; BLS induces dendritic cell activation and proinflammatory responses indicative of potential vaccine efficacy. Immune response: Up-regulation of dendritic cell costimulatory molecules and MHC class II; increased chemokine mRNA levels; induction of proinflammatory cytokine secretion; increased dendritic cell numbers and CD62L expression in lymph nodes; effects dependent on TLR4 signaling. [Ref7081:Berguer et al, 2006]
A protein nanoscaffold, lumazine synthase isolated from Brucella (BLS), was designed to facilitate cellular uptake of displayed antigens and maturation of dendritic cells, enhancing humoral immune responses. Efficacy: CHSPE-formulated vaccine provided a similar level of protection to the live attenuated vaccine and was superior to that of ISA 206. Immune response: CHSPE enhanced recruitment and activation of dendritic cells at the injection site and draining lymph nodes, induced antigen-specific antibody levels comparable to ISA 206, increased central and effector memory T cells, and promoted secretion of Th1-type cytokines. [Ref7414:Yang et al, 2024a]
c_adjuvant: no | yes; chitosan hydrochloride-stabilized Pickering emulsion (CHSPE)
c_preparation:
Chimeric proteins were engineered to display ten copies of a desired peptide (up to 27 residues) on the BLS scaffold without disrupting folding or stability; mixtures of chimeras were reassembled to control stoichiometry and spatial arrangement of different peptides. [Ref486:Laplagne et al., 2004]
Recombinant chimeric protein expressing KETc1 fused to Brucella spp. lumazine synthase. [Ref7066:Sciutto et al, 2005]
Polymeric protein (BLS) used alone without adjuvants; chimeric forms possible by insertion of foreign peptides at the N terminus. [Ref7081:Berguer et al, 2006]
The BLS nanoscaffold-based vaccine was formulated with chitosan hydrochloride-stabilized Pickering emulsion (CHSPE) as an adjuvant. [Ref7414:Yang et al, 2024a]
c_antigen: lumazine synthase (BLS); foreign peptides up to 27 residues; KETc1 | lumazine synthase; KETc1 | lumazine synthase (BLS)
c_model_host: Mus musculus (mouse) bone marrow dendritic cells; bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus virB4 mutant vaccine
c_description: The virB4 mutant is an intracellular growth-defective mutant of Brucella abortus used to study abortion induction. Efficacy: The virB4 mutant did not induce abortion in pregnant mice. Immune response: Infection with the virB4 mutant did not induce transient IFN-gamma production during placental development. [Ref7067:Kim et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus SFV-SOD recombinant vector RNA vaccine
c_description: Constructed replication-deficient Semliki Forest virus particles carrying recombinant RNA encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase. Efficacy: SFV-SOD particles induced significant protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 compared to control virus particles. Immune response: Induced T-cell proliferative response and gamma interferon secretion without SOD-specific antibodies; splenocytes showed cytotoxic T-lymphocyte activity against Brucella-infected cells; no interleukin-4 induction. [Ref7068:Oñate et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Recombinant Semliki Forest virus particles (SFV-SOD particles) expressing the SOD protein. [Ref7068:Oñate et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 vaccinia recombinant vector vaccine (WRL7/L12)
c_description: The Brucella abortus L7/L12 gene encoding ribosomal protein L7/L12 was cloned into vaccinia virus by homologous recombination to produce the WRL7/L12 recombinant. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with WRL7/L12 produced antibodies specific to vaccinia virus and L7/L12 antigens but were not protected against virulent Brucella abortus 2308 challenge. Immune response: Mice produced predominantly IgG2a isotype antibody responses indicative of a Th1 type immune response; however, no protective immunity was observed. [Ref7069:Baloglu et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing Brucella abortus L7/L12 protein. [Ref7069:Baloglu et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis OmaA-deficient vaccine
c_description: An OmaA-deficient strain of Brucella suis strain 1330 was generated by disrupting the DNA region encoding the passenger alpha-domain of the OmaA protein. The full-length OmaA gene was cloned and used to complement the deficient strain. Efficacy: Vaccination with the OmaA-deficient strain provided 3.0-3.9 log10 colony forming units protection against challenge with B. suis strain 1330 in BALB/c mice. [Ref7070:Bandara et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Live attenuated OmaA-deficient Brucella suis strain 1330 [Ref7070:Bandara et al, 2005]
c_model_host: BALB/c mice; J774 macrophage cell line

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis ctpA deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: A CtpA-deficient Brucella suis strain (1330DeltactpA) was generated by allelic exchange to study the role of the carboxyl-terminal processing protease in bacterial morphology and persistence. Efficacy: Vaccination with the ctpA-deficient strain conferred 4 to 5 log(10) CFU protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 or B. suis strain 1330 but no protection against B. melitensis strain 16 M. [Ref7073:Bandara et al, 2005a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with ctpA gene deletion. [Ref7073:Bandara et al, 2005a]
c_model_host: J774 mouse macrophage cell line; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: bp26 DNA vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis 16M genome was screened for immunogenic proteins; bp26 was identified as a protective antigen. Efficacy: bp26 DNA vaccine conferred protection against wild-type B. melitensis 16M challenge. Immune response: Induced elevated serum IgG antibodies without IgG subclass bias; stimulated gamma interferon and IL-4, IL-5, and IL-6 cytokines upon antigen restimulation. [Ref7074:Yang et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant plasmid encoding bp26 used for intramuscular DNA immunization. [Ref7074:Yang et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: trigger factor DNA vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis 16M genome was screened for immunogenic proteins; trigger factor was identified as a protective antigen. Efficacy: trigger factor DNA vaccine conferred protection against wild-type B. melitensis 16M challenge; combined with bp26, protection was significantly enhanced. Immune response: Induced elevated serum IgG antibodies without IgG subclass bias; stimulated gamma interferon but did not induce IL-4, IL-5, or IL-6 cytokines upon antigen restimulation. [Ref7074:Yang et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant plasmid encoding trigger factor used for intramuscular DNA immunization. [Ref7074:Yang et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus soluble protein extract (SPEBA) vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunization of cattle with a Brucella abortus soluble protein extract vaccine augmented by recombinant bovine IL 2. Efficacy: SPEBA vaccine alone provided limited protection; co-administration with rBoIL 2 improved antibody responses and lymphoproliferation but protection against abortion was not as strong as with S19 plus rBoIL 2. Immune response: Antibody responses were significantly higher in vaccinates receiving rBoIL 2; lymphoproliferation responses were higher in vaccinated or rBoIL 2-treated cattle; rBoIL 2 stimulated activation of macrophages with up-regulation of TNF-alpha, IL-12p40, and interferon-gamma genes. [Ref7075:Wyckoff et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Subunit vaccine consisting of 2 mg soluble protein extract administered with or without recombinant bovine IL 2. [Ref7075:Wyckoff et al, 2005]
c_antigen: soluble protein extract of Brucella abortus (SPEBA)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 48-74 peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: A synthetic peptide containing amino acids 48 to 74 of Omp31 was evaluated for immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mice. Efficacy: The peptide induced protection against B. melitensis similar to rOmp31 but less protection against B. ovis. Immune response: The peptide did not elicit a specific humoral response but induced a Th1 response mediated by CD4+ T cells. [Ref7076:Cassataro et al, 2005]
c_preparation: Synthetic peptide administered with incomplete Freund's adjuvant. [Ref7076:Cassataro et al, 2005]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description:
The recombinant 31-kDa outer membrane protein from Brucella melitensis (rOmp31) was evaluated for immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mice. Efficacy: Immunization with rOmp31 conferred protection against B. melitensis and B. ovis infection; protection against B. melitensis was mediated primarily by CD4+ T cells. Immune response: Intraperitoneal Omp31-IFA induced Th1 response; intraperitoneal TMC/Omp31 NPs induced mixed Th1-Th2 response; oral TMC/Omp31 NPs elicited mixed Th1-Th17 response; oral vaccination enhanced antigen-specific cell proliferation and Th17 response correlated with high protection. c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis outer membrane complex microparticle subunit vaccine
c_description: A safer vaccine alternative to Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 was developed using an outer membrane complex from Brucella ovis encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles. Immune response: Adequate serological response against Brucella ovis antigens induced by 800 microg HS-PEC; no positive serological reactions in Rose Bengal and Complement Fixation tests in HS-PEC vaccinated animals, unlike Rev. 1 vaccinated animals which were seropositive in these tests. [Ref7077:Muñoz et al, 2006]
c_preparation: Outer membrane complex antigen from Brucella ovis encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles prepared by a double emulsion solvent evaporation method (TROMS), with antigen loading about 13 microg HS per mg microparticles. [Ref7077:Muñoz et al, 2006]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus strain RB51 recombinant gamma-irradiated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus strain RB51 is an attenuated rough mutant used as a live vaccine against bovine brucellosis. Efficacy: Gamma-irradiated recombinant RB51 induced significant protection against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus in mice, whereas heat-killed vaccine did not. Immune response: Induction of beta-galactosidase-specific Th1-type immune responses; gamma-irradiated vaccine stimulated dendritic cell maturation with higher interleukin-12 secretion compared to heat-killed vaccine; no differences in immune responses to B. abortus-specific antigens between groups. c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus bvrS/bvrR mutant vaccine

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD DNA vaccine fused to IL-2
c_description: The study evaluated a DNA vaccine expressing a fusion protein of Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase antigen and IL-2 to enhance immune response and protection. Efficacy: Liposomal rL7/L12 vaccine showed better systemic clearance of bacterial load after challenge compared to free antigen and standard S-19 vaccine. Immune response: Liposomal rL7/L12 induced strong cell-mediated immunity (delayed type hypersensitivity, T-cell proliferation, type I cytokine upregulation) and stronger humoral immune response than free antigen, S-19 vaccine, or IFA-L7/L12 combination. c_vaccine_name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Brucella abortus combined DNA vaccine
c_description: The study examined the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a combined DNA vaccine including six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from M. tuberculosis and B. abortus. Efficacy: DNA-IL-12(+) immunized mice showed significantly reduced CFU counts in lung and spleen for M. tuberculosis and B. abortus, respectively, with better protection than combined DNA vaccine alone or positive controls. Immune response: DNA-IL-12(+) induced stronger antigen-specific IFN-gamma ELISPOT activities, higher CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cell responses, higher antigen-specific IgG titers with IgG2a skewing, increased IFN-gamma and IL-2 secretion, and decreased IL-4 and IL-10 secretion, indicating enhanced Th1-associated immune responses. [Ref2294:Yu et al., 2007]

Efficacy: Mice immunized with recombinant strains developed specific humoral immune responses predominantly IgG2a against RAP1 and specific cellular immune responses to recombinant RAP1 were elicited in vitro. Immune response: Strong humoral and cellular immune responses were induced by the recombinant B. abortus S19 strains expressing RAP1, with IgG2a as the predominant antibody isotype and lymphocyte activation in vitro. [Ref7089:Sabio et al, 2008]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD and interleukin-18 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the prophylactic potential of a liposome-based DNA vaccine co-expressing Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) against experimental murine brucellosis. Efficacy: Co-expression of IL-18 with SOD resulted in higher lymphoproliferative response and IFN-gamma production compared to immunization with free form SOD-DNA, indicating enhanced protection potential. Immune response: Induction of SOD-specific humoral and cellular immune responses with predominantly IgG2a antibody type; co-expression of IL-18 polarized antigen-specific immune responses toward Th-1 type, favorable for controlling intracellular pathogens. [Ref7091:Singha et al, 2008]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain B115 vaccine
c_description:
Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 is used as vaccine for prophylaxis in sheep and goats but induces antibodies to O-polysaccharide (O-PS) complicating differentiation of vaccinated and infected animals; B115 is a natural, attenuated, rough strain lacking surface O-PS and proposed as alternative vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with B115 conferred significant protective immunity against B. melitensis 16M and B. ovis, equivalent to that of Rev. 1 vaccine. Immune response: No interfering antibodies to O-PS detected; vaccination monitored by specific B115-based complement fixation test. [Ref7092:Adone et al, 2008]
B. melitensis strain B115 is a natural, attenuated rough strain previously shown to be highly protective against B. melitensis and B. ovis infections in mice without inducing interfering antibodies. This study tested its efficacy against B. abortus and B. suis. Efficacy: Vaccination with 10^8 CFU/mouse of B115 conferred satisfactory protection against B. abortus 2308. Single vaccination with 10^8 or 10^9 CFU/mouse provided weak protection against B. suis, but two vaccinations with 10^9 CFU/mouse significantly increased protection. Immune response: B115 showed adequate persistence in mice and induced solid humoral and cell-mediated immunity despite its rough phenotype. [Ref7116:Adone et al, 2011]
The rough strain Brucella melitensis B115 was shown to protect mice against wild Brucella strains despite lacking anti-O-PS antibodies. Efficacy: Antibodies induced by B115 conferred satisfactory protection, especially against B. abortus 2308, similar to protection conferred by S19 antiserum; RB51 antiserum was ineffective. Immune response: Antibodies induced by B115 act as opsonins targeting antigens other than O-PS, promoting efficient internalization and degradation of bacteria within phagocytes. [Ref7131:Adone et al, 2012]
c_preparation:
Live, attenuated rough strain B115 with O-PS present intracellularly but not exposed on surface. [Ref7092:Adone et al, 2008]
Live attenuated rough strain B115 administered at doses of 10^8 or 10^9 CFU per mouse. [Ref7116:Adone et al, 2011]
Live rough strain B115 of Brucella melitensis. [Ref7131:Adone et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus hsp60 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study suggests that hsp60 is a highly immunogenic heat shock protein produced by Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis, with higher production in B. abortus. The lower production of hsp60 by B. melitensis may contribute to its greater virulence. The authors propose hsp60 as a good antigenic candidate for engineering a subunit vaccine against Brucella. Immune response: Sera from brucellosis patients reacted strongly with hsp60 and other bacterial proteins, indicating the immunogenicity of hsp60. No reactivity was observed with sera from healthy individuals, suggesting a specific immune response to infection. [Ref7093:Amirmozafari et al, 2008]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis hsp60 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study indicates that hsp60 is an immunogenic heat shock protein produced by Brucella melitensis, though at lower levels than in B. abortus. This lower production may contribute to the higher virulence of B. melitensis. Hsp60 is proposed as a candidate antigen for subunit vaccine development. Immune response: Patient sera showed strong reactivity to hsp60 and other proteins, indicating an immune response specific to infection, while healthy control sera did not react. [Ref7093:Amirmozafari et al, 2008]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 bp26 and omp31 deletion vaccine

Efficacy: CGV2631 conferred significant protection against Brucella ovis but protection was significantly lower than that conferred by CGV26 and Rev. 1 vaccines. [Ref7094:Grilló et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Live attenuated deletion mutant of Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with bp26 and omp31 genes deleted; administered subcutaneously or conjunctivally. [Ref7094:Grilló et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: S19 DeltavjbR::Kan live vaccine candidate
c_description:
A vjbR knockout mutant was generated in the Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine to improve safety and efficacy. Efficacy: A single dose of the encapsulated mutant conferred higher levels of protection against wild-type challenge compared to the nonencapsulated vaccine. Immune response: The vaccine candidate elicited an anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response even when administered in encapsulated form. Safety: The vaccine was safer than the parental S19 strain, as indicated by the absence of splenomegaly in vaccinated mice. [Ref2096:Arenas-Gamboa et al., 2009]
Developed as a safer live attenuated vaccine candidate for human and animal use with demonstrated safety and protective efficacy in multiple immunocompetent animal models. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced colonization in multiple organs and reduced pathological changes after challenge with wild-type Brucella melitensis 16M. Immune response: Protection observed despite immunocompromised status, suggesting involvement of lesser-known immune mechanisms. [Ref7124:Arenas-Gamboa et al, 2012]
B. abortus S19ΔvjbR was used as a vaccine candidate to evaluate safety in the mouse model. Immune response: No significant bone changes or severe inflammatory responses were observed in mice inoculated with S19ΔvjbR. [Ref7282:Khalaf et al, 2019]
Live attenuated vaccine candidate derived from S19 with vjbR deletion, investigated for safety in pregnant swine. Efficacy: Not reported (study focused on safety; efficacy to be studied in future). Immune response: Robust anti-Brucella IgG humoral response induced, but of shorter duration (4-6 weeks post-inoculation) compared to cattle or mice. [Ref7289:Zriba et al, 2019]
The attenuated mutant S19vjbR is a derivative of strain S19 with vjbR gene deletion, studied as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: The mutant S19vjbR was progressively killed inside mature osteoclasts but induced significantly larger osteoclasts with enhanced resorptive activity. Immune response: No apoptosis or stimulation of nitric oxide or lactose dehydrogenase production was observed; osteoclasts infected with S19vjbR were larger and had enhanced resorptive activity. [Ref7299:Khalaf et al, 2020]

The vaccine was delivered either encapsulated in alginate microspheres containing vitelline protein B as a sustained-release vehicle or nonencapsulated. [Ref2096:Arenas-Gamboa et al., 2009]
Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 with vjbR gene deletion. [Ref7124:Arenas-Gamboa et al, 2012]
