c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella Escherichia coli vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study evaluates a live, non-pathogenic Escherichia coli genetically engineered to mimic Brucella infection pathways and present antigens to induce cytolytic T cell responses as a vaccine delivery system. Efficacy: The E. coli vaccine vector infected all tested cells and efficiently delivered therapeutics; elicited a Th1 cytokine profile in primary and secondary immune responses; induced specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) when delivering Brucella antigen. Immune response: Induction of Th1 cytokine profile and specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte responses, indicating cell mediated immunity against Brucella antigens. [Ref7095:Harms et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Escherichia coli modified to express Yersinia invasin and Listeria listeriolysin O (LLO) to enable infectivity and antigen release; engineered to express GFP or Brucella antigens. [Ref7095:Harms et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25c Omp31b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study discusses the potential interest of Omp25c and Omp31b as subcellular vaccines based on their occurrence in Brucella strains and antigenic relatedness with other family proteins. [Ref7096:Martín-Martín et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp31b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study discusses the potential interest of Omp25c and Omp31b as subcellular vaccines based on their occurrence in Brucella strains and antigenic relatedness with other family proteins. [Ref7096:Martín-Martín et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Semliki Forest virus (SFV) particles carrying RNA encoding Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 (IF3) were constructed as a replication-deficient vector vaccine. Efficacy: Mice immunized with SFV-IF3 showed significant resistance to challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 (P<0.01). Immune response: Induction of IF3-specific IgM antibodies by day 14 post-immunization; T-cell proliferative response and interferon gamma secretion upon in vitro stimulation with recombinant IF3 or crude Brucella protein extracts; no interleukin-4 secretion detected. [Ref7097:Cabrera et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Infectious but replication-deficient SFV particles encoding IF3 protein. [Ref7097:Cabrera et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 subunit vaccine
c_description: The infC gene encoding IF3 was cloned, sequenced, and expressed in Escherichia coli to produce recombinant protein. Efficacy: Previous reports indicated immunoprotective capacity; current study showed strong lymphocyte proliferation and gamma interferon production upon stimulation. Immune response: Immunization with recombinant IF3 induced a TH-1 polarized response characterized by gamma interferon production without IL-4 secretion or antibody production. [Ref7098:González et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant Brucella IF3 protein was used. [Ref7098:González et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 overexpressing sodC and wboA vaccine
c_description:
Investigated as a recombinant RB51 strain vaccine candidate to improve immune response and protection in bison. Efficacy: RB51+sodC,wboA vaccinated bison did not have greater protection from abortion or infection compared to nonvaccinates; less efficacious than parental RB51 strain. Immune response: Similar antibody, proliferative, and gamma interferon responses to RB51 as parental RB51 vaccine; cleared vaccine strain from lymph nodes faster than RB51. [Ref890:Olsen et al., 2009]
The vaccine was developed to protect elk from Brucella abortus infection, addressing the expanding range of infected elk in the Greater Yellowstone Area and the risk of transmission to cattle. Efficacy: The recombinant vaccine did not protect elk against brucellosis after experimental challenge. [Ref7218:Nol et al, 2016]
c_preparation:
7.4 x 10^10 CFU of RB51+sodC,wboA administered to bison. [Ref890:Olsen et al., 2009]
Recombinant live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 overexpressing superoxide dismutase and glycosyltransferase genes. [Ref7218:Nol et al, 2016]
c_antigen: superoxide dismutase (sodC), glycosyltransferase (wboA) | superoxide dismutase; glycosyltransferase

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus gonadotropin releasing hormone subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was used to immunize captive female elk to evaluate contraceptive efficacy as a method to reduce brucellosis transmission and manage elk populations. Efficacy: Both doses prevented pregnancy in elk cows for at least three years with infertility rates of 86-100% in treated groups versus 0-28% in controls (P<0.0001). Immune response: Antibody titers were measured but specific immune response details are not reported in the abstract. [Ref7099:Killian et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Single immunization of either 1,000 microg or 2,000 microg doses of GonaCon. [Ref7099:Killian et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella L7/L12 DNA vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the ability of a DNA vaccine encoding the L7/L12 protein of Brucella sp. to induce cellular and humoral immune responses. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed lower bacterial cfu compared to control groups, indicating vaccine efficiency. Immune response: High levels of IFN-gamma (3100 pg/mL) and low levels of IL-5 (300 pg/mL) were produced by splenic lymphocytes; high IgG2a isotype response with slightly lower IgG1 titers; high IgG2a/IgG1 ratio indicating activation of Th1 cell response. [Ref2102:Abtahi et al., 2008]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine encoding L7/L12 gene delivered by intramuscular injection; three vaccinations at 3 week intervals. [Ref2102:Abtahi et al., 2008]

c_vaccine_name: Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus combined DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a combined DNA vaccine containing six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from M. bovis and B. abortus. Efficacy: The combined DNA vaccine significantly reduced the number of positive lymph node and spleen cultures for both pathogens compared to unvaccinated calves; provided significantly better protection than BCG vaccine against M. bovis; protection level comparable to S19 vaccine against B. abortus. Immune response: Stronger antigen-specific IFN-gamma responses and ELISPOT activities; higher antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses than BCG or S19 groups; higher antigen-specific IgG titers; two antigens induced significant IFN-gamma responses 6 months after challenge. [Ref7100:Hu et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Combined DNA vaccine containing six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from both pathogens. [Ref7100:Hu et al, 2009]
c_antigen: six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain WRRP1 vaccine expressing wboA and Bacillus anthracis protective antigen
c_description: The study investigated simultaneous expression of a homologous antigen (wboA gene encoding mannosyltransferase for LPS O-antigen biosynthesis) and a heterologous antigen (Bacillus anthracis pag gene encoding protective antigen) in an attenuated rough Brucella melitensis strain. Efficacy: Strain WRSPA induced protection in BALB/c mice against B. melitensis 16M challenge but failed to protect A/J mice against B. anthracis Sterne strain challenge. [Ref7101:Bandara et al, 2009]
c_preparation: The wboA and pag genes were cloned into plasmid pBBR4MCS and introduced into O-antigen deficient B. melitensis strain WRRP1 to produce strain WRSPA, which expressed O-antigen and protective antigen products. [Ref7101:Bandara et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis antigenic complex subunit vaccine
c_description: This study developed a novel formulation strategy for delivering the Brucella ovis antigenic extract (HS) into ovine mucosal surfaces. [Ref7102:Da et al, 2009]
c_preparation: HS was entrapped in conventional and mannosylated poly(anhydride) nanoparticles prepared by solvent displacement method; nanoparticles were gamma-irradiated at 10 kGy or 25 kGy for sterilization suitable for ophthalmic administration. [Ref7102:Da et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella melitensis gamma irradiated vaccine
c_description: The study hypothesized that bacterial metabolism is important for antigenic and adjuvant properties needed for protective immunity; gamma-irradiation was used to inactivate Brucella melitensis while retaining metabolic activity. Efficacy: The irradiated vaccine protected mice against virulent bacterial challenge without residual virulence. Immune response: The vaccine generated antigen-specific cytotoxic T cells and persisted in macrophages, indicating induction of cellular immunity. [Ref7103:Magnani et al, 2009]
c_preparation: Gamma-irradiated Brucella melitensis bacteria that are nondividing but metabolically active. [Ref7103:Magnani et al, 2009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus D15 protein subunit vaccine
c_description:
Immune response: Antibody responses to Mdh and D15 proteins were significantly more frequent in naturally infected elk compared to vaccinated and uninfected elk, indicating these antigens as predictors of natural infection; variable cross-reactivity observed in cattle sera, suggesting common expression of AfuA and Mdh during infection in both hosts [Ref7104:Lowry et al, 2010]
Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with D15 appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. Immune response: Not reported. [Ref7119:Lowry et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Recombinant D15 protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts. [Ref7119:Lowry et al, 2011]
c_antigen: D15; malate dehydrogenase (Mdh); ion transporter (AfuA) | D15
c_model_host: Elk (Cervus elaphus); cattle (Bos taurus); Mus musculus (BALB/c mice)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 2308 znuA purE double mutant vaccine
c_description: A double mutant strain was constructed from Brucella abortus 2308 by deleting znuA and purE genes to create a new, safe live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Two doses of the double mutant conferred 0.79 log protection, similar to S19 vaccine; single dose of znuA mutant also conferred similar protection. Immune response: The double mutant was less capable of surviving in macrophages and caused significantly less inflammation in spleens of infected mice compared to wild-type strain. [Ref7105:Yang et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain of Brucella abortus 2308 with deletions in znuA and purE genes. [Ref7105:Yang et al, 2010]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp28 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the potential of CpG ODN to enhance the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant OMP28 of Brucella melitensis as a subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The rOMP28+CpG treated mice showed significant protection against B. abortus 544 challenge, but the level of protection was lower than the required level. Immune response: Vaccination induced vigorous IgG response biased towards Th1 type (IgG2a), increased T-cell proliferation, and up-regulation of type I cytokines including interferon gamma; free antigen alone suppressed IFN-gamma production in vitro. B. abortus S-19 vaccinated mice showed highest IL-4 and IFN-gamma production. [Ref7106:Kaushik et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Recombinant OMP28 protein co-administered with CpG oligonucleotides as an adjuvant. [Ref7106:Kaushik et al, 2010]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis P39 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
The study analyzed the potential of the Brucella melitensis 16 M periplasmic binding protein (P39) antigen expressed in live Escherichia coli as a vaccine against B. melitensis 16 M infection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination significantly reduced the number of Brucella melitensis strain 16 M bacteria in spleens compared to saline controls (p<0.001). Immune response: The vaccine elicited T-cell proliferative responses, induced gamma interferon production upon antigen re-stimulation, and generated strong humoral responses including IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies. [Ref7107:Al-Mariri, 2010]
BALB/c mice were immunized with live Escherichia coli expressing the p39 gene of Brucella melitensis, coding for the periplasmic binding protein, combined with CpG oligodeoxynucleotides as adjuvant. Efficacy: Mice immunized with E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 plus CpG ODN showed higher protection against B. melitensis 16M compared to those immunized with E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 alone or with non-CpG ODN; no protection observed with E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b alone or with adjuvant; Rev. 1 vaccine showed more effective protection at 4 and 8 weeks post-challenge. Immune response: Significant IFN-γ production and T-cell proliferation in response to P39 antigen; antibody responses (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a) detected only in groups receiving E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 with CpG or non-CpG ODN. [Ref7128:Al-Mariri et al, 2012]
c_preparation:
Live Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b expressing Brucella P39 protein administered intraperitoneally twice at 4-week intervals. [Ref7107:Al-Mariri, 2010]
Live Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 with CpG oligodeoxynucleotides or non-CpG ODN; control groups included E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b alone or with adjuvants. [Ref7128:Al-Mariri et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus 2308 delta pgk vaccine
c_description: A pgk deletion mutant of Brucella abortus strain 2308 was constructed to test the role of PGK in pathogenesis and as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The Delta pgk mutant strain exhibited extreme attenuation and induced protective immunity superior to that conferred by commercial strain 19 or RB51 vaccines in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised mice. Immune response: The mutant strain showed altered intracellular trafficking with retention in late endosomal/lysosomal compartments (LAMP1 positive), indicating impaired intracellular survival; induced protective immunity superior to commercial vaccines. [Ref1811:Trant et al., 2010]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus Delta pgk mutant strain. [Ref1811:Trant et al., 2010]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c, C57BL/6, 129/Sv, IRF-1 knockout mice); bone marrow-derived macrophages

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain WRR51 vaccine
c_description: Two defined nonreverting rough mutants were derived from virulent Brucella melitensis strain 16M as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: WRR51 showed better survival in hMDMs compared to WRRP1 and less attenuation in mice compared to dual mutant WRRP1. [Ref7108:Nikolich et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA deletion. [Ref7108:Nikolich et al, 2010]
c_model_host: human monocyte-derived macrophages; Mus musculus (BALB/c mice)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain WRRP1 vaccine
c_description: Two defined nonreverting rough mutants were derived from virulent Brucella melitensis strain 16M as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: WRRP1 exhibited reduced survival in hMDMs and persisted for 1 week or less in mice, showing more severe attenuation than single mutants. [Ref7108:Nikolich et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with dual deletions in wboA and purEK. [Ref7108:Nikolich et al, 2010]
c_model_host: human monocyte-derived macrophages; Mus musculus (BALB/c mice)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the immunopotentiation of the live Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine by various adjuvants. Efficacy: Adjuvants enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses, correlating with increased protection against experimental challenge; highest protection was observed with TNF-beta or polyoxidonium combined with the vaccine. Immune response: Adjuvants increased synthesis of antibodies against rough and smooth Brucella antigens, enhanced cell-mediated immunity, and improved macrophage phagocytosis. The dynamics and levels of antibody responses varied depending on the adjuvant used. [Ref7109:Denisov et al, 2010]
c_adjuvant: yes; larifan; polyoxidonium; natrium thiosulphate; TNF-beta; Ribi adjuvant system
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine combined with different adjuvants including larifan, polyoxidonium (PO), natrium thiosulphate (NT), TNF-beta, and Ribi adjuvant system (RAS). [Ref7109:Denisov et al, 2010]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus wbkC gene disruption vaccine
c_description: Rough mutants of Brucella abortus were generated by disruption of the wbkC gene, which encodes the formyltransferase enzyme involved in LPS biosynthesis. Efficacy: The wbkC mutant strains were attenuated in macrophages and mice; they induced lower protective immunity in C57BL/6 mice than the smooth vaccine strain S19 but similar protection to the rough vaccine RB51. Immune response: Mutants induced higher levels of IL-12 and TNF-alpha in macrophages compared to parental smooth strains. [Ref7110:Lacerda et al, 2010]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (C57BL/6 and interferon regulatory factor-1 knockout mice); bone marrow-derived macrophages

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine expressing Mycobacterium bovis MPB83 fusion proteins
c_description: The immunodominant MPB83 antigen from Mycobacterium bovis was expressed as chimeric fusion proteins with β-galactosidase, outer membrane lipoprotein OMP19, or periplasmic protein BP26 in Brucella abortus strain 19, driven by each gene's own promoter. Efficacy: Recombinant S19 strains induced specific INF-γ production against MPB83; fusion to BP26 resulted in weaker immune response; no effect on bacterial survival or infection pattern. Immune response: Specific cellular immune response characterized by INF-γ production against MPB83 antigen; lipid moiety association (OMP19 fusion) did not enhance immunogenicity compared to other fusions. [Ref7111:Sabio et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. abortus S19 strains carrying genes coding for MPB83 fused to β-galactosidase, OMP19, or BP26 expressed from replicative or integrative plasmids; OMP19-MPB83 processed as a lipoprotein. [Ref7111:Sabio et al, 2010]
c_antigen: MPB83; fusion partners β-galactosidase, OMP19, BP26

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HSA-L7/L12 and lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the protection of a combination of recombinant HSA-L7/L12 fusion protein with LPS in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: The combination of tHSA-L7/L12 fusion protein with LPS and B. abortus S19 induced higher protection against virulent B. abortus 544 challenge than other groups (P = 0.005). Immune response: The combination vaccine elicited significantly higher antibody titers than LPS alone and L7/L12+LPS; predominant IgG1 and IgG3 subtypes observed; strong T-cell proliferative response induced by tHSA-L7/L12 fusion protein and L7/L12, indicating cellular immunity; no significant difference in proliferative response between L7/L12 and tHSA-L7/L12 fusion protein groups. [Ref7112:Pakzad et al, 2010]
c_preparation: Recombinant HSA-L7/L12 fusion protein expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and purified by affinity chromatography; LPS extracted by n-butanol and purified by ultracentrifugation; combined for immunization. [Ref7112:Pakzad et al, 2010]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 GFP vaccine
c_description:
A prototype Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine expressing green fluorescent protein (S19-GFP) was constructed to serve as a marker vaccine. Efficacy: S19-GFP protected mice against virulent Brucella abortus challenge to the same extent as the parental S19 vaccine. Immune response: Both S19-GFP and S19 vaccines induced similar levels of antibodies against lipopolysaccharide; anti-GFP antibodies allowed discrimination between S19-GFP vaccinated and S19 vaccinated mice. [Ref7113:Chacón-Díaz et al, 2011]
The study developed a Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine constitutively expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) coded in chromosome II to allow serological differentiation of vaccinated cattle from infected animals. Efficacy: S19-GFP displayed similar biological characteristics and immunogenic and protective efficacies in mice compared to parental S19 strain; induced long-lasting anti-GFP antibodies in cattle, allowing differentiation from infected animals. Immune response: Vaccinated animals developed anti-S-LPS antibodies followed by anti-GFP antibodies; anti-GFP antibody response was higher in GFP-boosted animals; anti-GFP antibodies persisted as long or longer than anti-S-LPS antibodies, enabling serological identification of vaccinated cattle. [Ref7351:Chacón-Díaz et al, 2021]
c_preparation:
The S19-GFP vaccine maintained all biochemical characteristics of the parental S19 vaccine and expressed GFP allowing identification under ultraviolet light. [Ref7113:Chacón-Díaz et al, 2011]
Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 genetically modified to express GFP; administered at 5×10^9 CFU by subcutaneous or conjunctival routes; some animals received a GFP boost seven weeks later. [Ref7351:Chacón-Díaz et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella neotomae 26-kDa periplasmic protein gamma irradiated vaccine
c_description: Recombinant B. neotomae overexpressing a 26 kDa periplasmic protein was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent Brucella species. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific antibody and T cell responses. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella neotomae gamma irradiated vaccine
c_description:
The study aimed to evaluate Brucella neotomae, a bacterium not known to cause disease, as a vaccine platform for human brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific antibody and T cell responses. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]
The study tested oral immunization with gamma-irradiated B. neotomae to induce protection against virulent Brucella abortus 2308. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with B. neotomae showed highest resistance to B. abortus 2308 colonization in spleen and liver after intraperitoneal challenge; all tested doses conferred significant protection intraperitoneally; highest dose (10^11 CFU-equivalent) required for protection against intranasal challenge with reduced bacterial colonization in spleens and lungs. Immune response: Induction of serum and mucosal antibodies specific to smooth LPS including IgM, IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, and IgG3 isotypes; antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells secreting IFN-γ and TNF-α were elicited. [Ref7175:Dabral et al, 2014]
c_preparation:
B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]
Gamma-irradiated B. neotomae administered orally in different doses (10^9, 10^10, 10^11 CFU-equivalent). [Ref7175:Dabral et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine hydrolase subunit vaccine
c_description: Due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines, screening of Brucella-protective antigens as subunit vaccine candidates was pursued; immunoproteomic assay identified immunogenic soluble proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M, including AdoHcyase. Efficacy: Recombinant AdoHcyase induced a high level of protection against B. melitensis 16M challenge in mice. Immune response: Strong antibody response induced; polyclonal antibody recognized a 52 kDa band in soluble protein extracts from five Brucella strains; significant stimulation of interferon-γ and interleukin-2 production. [Ref7115:Yang et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Recombinant AdoHcyase protein expressed in Escherichia coli. [Ref7115:Yang et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella virB2 deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to construct Brucella vaccine strain M5-90 delta virB2 mutants as a basis for developing new attenuated vaccines. [Ref7117:Li et al, 2010]
c_preparation: A virB2 deletion mutant was created using homologous recombination with a suicide plasmid pGEM-7zf-delta virB2-sacB. [Ref7117:Li et al, 2010]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51-leuB vaccine over-expressing SOD
c_description: A recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph was engineered to over-express SOD alone to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: Significant protection compared to control; less effective than the strain over-expressing SOD and WboA. Immune response: Elicited protective immune responses against brucellosis. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid over-expressing SOD. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51-leuB vaccine over-expressing SOD and L7/L12
c_description: A recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph was engineered to over-express SOD and L7/L12 ribosomal protein to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: Significant protection compared to control; less effective than the strain over-expressing SOD and WboA. Immune response: Elicited protective immune responses against brucellosis. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid over-expressing SOD and L7/L12. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]
c_antigen: Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); L7/L12 ribosomal protein

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51-leuB vaccine over-expressing SOD and WboA
c_description: An improved recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph (strain RB51leuB) was developed to over-express homologous proteins SOD, L7/L12, and WboA to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: All vaccine groups significantly protected mice compared to controls (P<0.05); the strain RB51leuB/SOD/WboA vaccine provided significantly better protection than strains RB51leuB/SOD or RB51leuB/SOD/L7/L12. Immune response: Over-expression of Brucella antigens in strain RB51leuB elicited protective immune responses against brucellosis. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB was used as a platform with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid to construct strains over-expressing SOD alone, SOD and L7/L12, or SOD and WboA. [Ref7118:Rajasekaran et al, 2011]
c_antigen: Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); L7/L12 ribosomal protein; glycosyl-transferase (WboA)

c_preparation: Recombinant AfuA protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts. [Ref7119:Lowry et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: Escheriosome-encapsulated Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to investigate the immunogenic potential of fusogenic liposomes (escheriosomes) encapsulated recombinant Cu-Zn SOD protein alone or combined with recombinant IL-18. Efficacy: Immunization with liposome-encapsulated rSOD alone or combined with rIL-18 increased resistance in mice against challenge with B. abortus 544. Immune response: Escheriosomes encapsulated rSOD induced immune responses that were further enhanced upon co-immunization with recombinant IL-18. [Ref7120:Singha et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Recombinant Cu-Zn SOD protein encapsulated in fusogenic liposomes (escheriosomes). [Ref7120:Singha et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M delta mucR vaccine
c_description: The mucR mutant (BMEI 1364) was identified and characterized as a vaccine candidate for brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals demonstrated a statistically significant degree of protection against both intraperitoneal and aerosol challenge. Immune response: The vaccine elicited a strong protective immunity; safety was indicated by absence of Brucella-associated pathological changes including splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, or granulomatous disease. [Ref2071:Arenas-Gamboa et al., 2011]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant administered intraperitoneally at a dose of 10^5 CFU. [Ref2071:Arenas-Gamboa et al., 2011]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus bp26 and trigger factor DNA vaccine
c_description: Bison were vaccinated with eukaryotic DNA expression vectors encoding Brucella periplasmic protein bp26 and chaperone protein trigger factor (TF) to understand immune responses in wildlife where current vaccines are ineffective. Efficacy: DNA-vaccinated bison developed enhanced antibody, proliferative T cell, and IFN-γ responses compared to controls; increased percentages of CD4(+) and CD8(+) T lymphocytes observed. Immune response: Strong cellular immune responses indicated by elevated antibody production, T cell proliferation, and interferon-gamma secretion upon antigen restimulation; increased CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cell populations. [Ref7121:Clapp et al, 2011]
c_preparation: DNA vaccines encoding bp26 and TF administered intramuscularly with CpG adjuvant at weeks 0, 2, and 4. [Ref7121:Clapp et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis znuA deletion vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain with deletion of the znuA gene involved in zinc transport, developed to provide protection against inhalational infection. Efficacy: Single oral vaccination rapidly cleared from mice within 2 weeks; effectively protected mice against nasal challenge with wild-type B. melitensis 16M; 83% of vaccinated mice had no detectable brucellae in spleens; enhanced clearance from lungs; partial protection observed in IFN-γ-deficient mice. Immune response: Vaccination stimulated IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-22; protection was partially dependent on IL-17 in RB51 vaccinated mice but not explicitly for ΔznuA B. melitensis; suggests stimulation of Th1 and Th17 cell responses. [Ref7122:Clapp et al, 2011a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated ΔznuA B. melitensis administered orally. [Ref7122:Clapp et al, 2011a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis riboflavin synthase alpha chain subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified immunogenic proteins from Brucella melitensis 16 M soluble proteins using immunoproteomic assay to screen candidate antigens for subunit vaccine development. Riboflavin synthase alpha chain (RS-α) was identified as a novel vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with recombinant RS-α showed partial protection against Brucella melitensis infection. Immune response: Vaccinated mice splenocytes produced IFN-γ and IL-2 but not IL-4 or IL-10 upon in vitro stimulation with recombinant RS-α, indicating a Th1-type immune response. [Ref7123:Yang et al, 2011a]
c_preparation: Recombinant RS-α protein expressed in Escherichia coli as a His-tag fusion protein. [Ref7123:Yang et al, 2011a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M delta vjbR vaccine
c_description:
Developed as a safer live attenuated vaccine candidate for human and animal use with demonstrated safety and protective efficacy in multiple immunocompetent animal models. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced colonization in multiple organs and reduced pathological changes after challenge with wild-type Brucella melitensis 16M. Immune response: Protection observed despite immunocompromised status, suggesting involvement of lesser-known immune mechanisms. [Ref7124:Arenas-Gamboa et al, 2012]
The study investigates the safety of the Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR strain vaccine candidate in young goats over a 15-month period including vaccination, impregnation, delivery, and lactation. Efficacy: Not reported (the study focused on safety, not efficacy). Immune response: Blood samples were collected to assess humoral immune response throughout the study; specific immune response results are not detailed in the abstract. [Ref7332:Castaño-Zubieta et al, 2021]
The vjbR gene, a quorum sensing regulator involved in Brucella intracellular survival, was targeted to develop a vaccine candidate that allows differentiation between infection and vaccination. Efficacy: Vaccination with 16MΔvjbR conferred significant protective immunity against Brucella melitensis strain 16M challenge, equivalent to the licensed vaccine Rev. 1. Immune response: The vjbR deletion mutant elicited a Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response and induced secretion of gamma interferon and interleukin-10. [Ref1910:Wang et al., 2011]
Males were vaccinated using subcutaneous injection with vaccine candidate 16MΔvjbR at 10^9 CFU/100 μl. Efficacy: Vaccination resulted in a significant reduction in colonization in the mouse reproductive organs but did not correlate with decreased inflammation; efficacy varied between species and reproductive organs. Immune response: Not reported. [Ref7367:Hensel et al, 2022]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16 M with vjbR gene deletion. [Ref7124:Arenas-Gamboa et al, 2012]
A single subcutaneous dose containing 1x10^9 CFU of B. melitensis 16MΔvjbR was delivered either encapsulated in alginate microcapsules or non-encapsulated. [Ref7332:Castaño-Zubieta et al, 2021]
A vjbR mutant of Brucella melitensis strain 16M was constructed by replacing the vjbR gene with a kanamycin resistance gene. [Ref1910:Wang et al., 2011]
Live attenuated vaccine candidate 16MΔvjbR administered subcutaneously. [Ref7367:Hensel et al, 2022]
c_antigen: vjbR deletion mutant | vjbR deletion mutant; VjbR protein
c_model_host: Mus musculus (IRF-1(-/-) knockout mice); BALB/c mice; macrophage; guinea pig; Capra hircus; Mus musculus

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 vaccine
c_description: B. melitensis strain M5-90 is a live attenuated vaccine cultured from B. melitensis strain M28 and has been used as an effective tool in the control of brucellosis in goats and sheep in China. Efficacy: Not directly reported; study provides molecular insights into attenuation mechanisms that may facilitate generation of new attenuated vaccine strains with enhanced efficacy Immune response: Infection induced parallel changes in gene expression profiles in macrophages, including induction of anti-inflammatory and antiapoptotic factors; differential expression of genes involved in lysosome and MAPK pathways; apoptosis-related genes were key differentially expressed genes in significant pathways [Ref7125:Wang et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain derived from B. melitensis strain M28 [Ref7125:Wang et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus SodC Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is based on recombinant Lactococcus lactis secreting Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) used as an oral antigen delivery system. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals were protected against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308; protection was mildly improved with co-administration of IL-12 expressing L. lactis. Immune response: Induction of anti-SOD-specific IgM and IgG2a dominated IgG responses in sera; SOD-specific secretory IgA detected in nasal and bronchoalveolar lavages; T-cell proliferative responses to SOD and Brucella protein extracts observed up to 6 months post-boost, indicating long-term memory. [Ref7126:Sáez et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Oral administration of Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 transformed with pSEC derivatives encoding SOD. [Ref7126:Sáez et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus N-formylperosamine polymer AcrA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study engineered a glycoprotein by expressing Campylobacter jejuni oligosaccharyltransferase PglB and acceptor protein AcrA in Yersinia enterocolitica O9 cells, transferring a polymer of N-formylperosamine identical to Brucella abortus O polysaccharide onto AcrA. Efficacy: The glycoprotein induced an IgG response recognizing Brucella O antigen but did not confer protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice. Immune response: IgG antibody response specific to Brucella O antigen was generated in mice following glycoprotein injection. [Ref7127:Iwashkiw et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant glycoprotein consisting of N-formylperosamine polymer conjugated to AcrA protein produced in Yersinia enterocolitica O9. [Ref7127:Iwashkiw et al, 2012]
c_antigen: N-formylperosamine polymer conjugated to AcrA protein

c_vaccine_name: AsnC recombinant protein vaccine
c_description: Screening of Brucella protective antigens identified AsnC as a protein stimulating strong IFN-γ responses and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Mice immunized with AsnC plus adjuvant showed protection against virulent B. abortus infection comparable to licensed vaccine S19 and Cu-Zn SOD antigen. Immune response: AsnC induced strong antibody responses and stimulated strong IFN-γ responses in splenocytes. [Ref2099:Fu et al., 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant AsnC protein plus adjuvant [Ref2099:Fu et al., 2012]

c_vaccine_name: CobB recombinant protein vaccine
c_description: Due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines, screening of Brucella protective antigens as subunit vaccine candidates was focused on; CobB was identified as a protein stimulating strong IFN-γ responses and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Mice immunized with CobB plus adjuvant showed protection against virulent B. abortus infection comparable to licensed vaccine S19 and Cu-Zn SOD antigen. Immune response: CobB induced strong antibody responses and stimulated strong IFN-γ responses in splenocytes. [Ref2099:Fu et al., 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant CobB protein plus adjuvant [Ref2099:Fu et al., 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description:
The study evaluated the immunogenic potential of recombinant Omp25 and its protective efficacy against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in Balb/c mice. Efficacy: Intradermal immunization significantly reduced splenic colonization of Brucella abortus; protection comparable to that of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine. Immune response: Immunization induced a mixed Th1 and Th2 immune response with high IL-4, IL-12, and IFN-γ levels; post-challenge cytokine profile showed elevated IL-12 and IFN-γ but no IL-4, indicating a cell mediated immune response likely responsible for protection. [Ref7129:Goel et al, 2012]
Recombinant Omp25 protein was formulated in PC-PE liposomes and PLGA microparticles to enhance protective immunity. Efficacy: Significant protection was observed with prime and booster liposome immunization comparable to Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine; microparticle immunization failed to provide better protection. Immune response: Liposome immunized mice showed stimulation of cell mediated immune response after challenge, including cytotoxicity in CD4(+) and CD8(+) enriched lymphocytes; microparticle immunized mice showed decreased cytotoxicity and lack of cell mediated immunity after challenge. [Ref7147:Goel et al, 2013]
The study aimed to express and purify recombinant Omp25 protein from Brucella abortus biovar 3 and evaluate its immunogenicity as a vaccine candidate molecule against animal brucellosis. Efficacy: Doses of recombinant Omp25 protein greater than 0.1 μg/mL were toxic to RAW cells; doses of 1 μg/mL and lower increased inflammation via nitric oxide levels; IFN-γ production was induced at 0.05 μg/mL without affecting cell viability; IL-12 levels did not significantly change. Immune response: The recombinant Omp25 protein stimulated Th1-related cytokine IFN-γ production in macrophages, indicating a potential to induce a protective immune response relevant for vaccine development. [Ref7346:Atabey et al, 2021]
c_preparation:
Recombinant Omp25 administered via intraperitoneal and intradermal routes; dosage reduction observed with intradermal immunization. [Ref7129:Goel et al, 2012]
Omp25 protein encapsulated in PC-PE liposomes or PLGA microparticles. [Ref7147:Goel et al, 2013]
Recombinant Omp25 protein was produced using a prokaryotic expression system, purified by affinity chromatography followed by gel permeation chromatography. [Ref7346:Atabey et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella GroEL subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identifies GroEL as a Brucella immunodominant antigen using nanobody technology and MALDI-TOF-MS, suggesting its potential as a candidate antigen for next generation vaccine development. Immune response: GroEL is identified as an immunodominant antigen involved in protein folding during stress; nanobody NbBruc02 specifically recognizes GroEL, indicating its immunogenicity and potential for vaccine development. [Ref7130:Abbady et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BP26 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
Current Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine has many disadvantages prompting development of alternative vaccines and delivery systems. Efficacy: Invasive E. coli vaccine expressing BP26 induced significant protection against B. melitensis challenge in mice. Immune response: E. coli delivery system is non-pathogenic and delivers antigens to antigen-presenting cells promoting cellular immune responses; natural adjuvant properties suggested. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]
The study aimed to produce a food-grade recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Brucella melitensis BP26 protein as a potential live delivery vector vaccine. [Ref7285:Azizpour et al, 2019]
c_preparation:
Escherichia coli DH5α engineered to express inv gene from Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and hly gene from Listeria monocytogenes, carrying plasmid expressing B. melitensis BP26. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]
The bp26 gene of Brucella melitensis was cloned into the food-grade pNZ 8149 vector and expressed in Lactococcus lactis NZ 3900. [Ref7285:Azizpour et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Current Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine has many disadvantages prompting development of alternative vaccines and delivery systems. Efficacy: Invasive E. coli vaccine expressing Omp16 induced significant protection against B. melitensis challenge in mice. Immune response: E. coli delivery system is non-pathogenic and delivers antigens to antigen-presenting cells promoting cellular immune responses; natural adjuvant properties suggested. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Escherichia coli DH5α engineered to express inv gene from Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and hly gene from Listeria monocytogenes, carrying plasmid expressing B. melitensis Omp16. [Ref7132:Gupta et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 virB5 gene deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: A gene deletion mutant strain of Brucella abortus strain 19 with virB5 deletion was constructed as a molecular tag vaccine. Immune response: Recombinant VirB5 antigen could discriminate mice infected with wild-type B. abortus from those infected with the virB5 mutant strain, indicating potential as a serological marker. [Ref7133:Tan et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated induction of protective immunity in mice against brucellosis by vaccination with a combination of naloxone, alum, and heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M. Efficacy: The group receiving naloxone + alum + heat-killed Brucella melitensis showed significantly increased IFN-γ, IL-4, and IgG levels, the lowest bacterial load, and 100% survival rate in groups vaccinated with adjuvant combinations. Immune response: Enhanced immunogenicity with increased Th1-type cytokine IFN-γ, IL-4, and immunoglobulin G levels indicating a strong cellular and humoral immune response. [Ref7134:Motaharinia et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Combination of naloxone and alum as adjuvants with heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M. [Ref7134:Motaharinia et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus dihydrolipoamide succinyltransferase subunit vaccine
c_description: The recombinant dihydrolipoamide succinyltransferase (rE2o) of Brucella abortus was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli and purified by metal affinity chromatography. It is immunoreactive with brucellosis positive cattle sera. Efficacy: The rE2o vaccine provided partial protection against challenge with pathogenic Brucella abortus in BALB/c mice. Immune response: The vaccine induced high IgG antibody and its isotypes IgG1, significant production of IFN-γ, IL-10, and IL-4 cytokines, and significant lymphoproliferation of splenocytes, indicating a mixed but predominant Th2 type immune response. [Ref7135:Verma et al, 2012]
c_adjuvant: yes; Freund's adjuvant and aluminium hydroxide gel
c_preparation: Recombinant rE2o protein formulated with two different adjuvants: Freund's adjuvant and aluminium hydroxide gel. [Ref7135:Verma et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline complex subunit vaccine encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the protection offered by the hot saline complex extracted from Brucella ovis encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles when administered conjunctivally. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals showed a 3-log reduction in spleen colony forming units compared to unvaccinated controls; protection was significantly higher than that observed with the commercial Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine administered subcutaneously. Immune response: The vaccine induced a strong and prolonged mucosal IgA response superior to that induced by Rev. 1; elicited cytokines IL-2, IL-4, and gamma-IFN correlated well with protection; biodistribution showed movement of nanoparticles from the palpebral area to nasal region and gastrointestinal tract, differing from free colloids which remained at administration site. [Ref7136:Da et al, 2012]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of hot saline complex antigen encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles of approximately 300 nm size, with antigen loading close to 30 μg per mg nanoparticle; the encapsulated antigen maintained protein profile, structural integrity, and antigenicity. [Ref7136:Da et al, 2012]
c_antigen: hot saline complex extracted from Brucella ovis (HS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus FlgJ subunit vaccine
c_description: Flagellar proteins of Brucella abortus were screened for protective antigens; FlgJ was identified as a candidate inducing protective immune responses. Efficacy: Immunization with FlgJ plus adjuvant provided protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection in mice. Immune response: Induced vigorous immunoglobulin G response and stimulated splenocytes to secrete IFN-γ, indicating humoral and cell-mediated immunity. [Ref7137:Li et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant his-tagged FlgJ protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; administered with adjuvant. [Ref7137:Li et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus FliN subunit vaccine
c_description: Flagellar proteins of Brucella abortus were screened for protective antigens; FliN was identified as a candidate inducing protective immune responses. Efficacy: Immunization with FliN plus adjuvant provided protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection in mice. Immune response: Induced vigorous immunoglobulin G response and stimulated splenocytes to secrete IFN-γ, indicating humoral and cell-mediated immunity. [Ref7137:Li et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant his-tagged FliN protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; administered with adjuvant. [Ref7137:Li et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella canis virB10 mutant vaccine
c_description: A non-polar virB10 mutant was constructed in Brucella canis to reduce virulence. Efficacy: The virB10 mutant was cleared by day 21 post-infection and significantly reduced CFU recovery after challenge with wild-type B. canis at day 15, indicating protective immunity. Immune response: Similar antibody isotype levels (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, IgM) compared to wild-type; mild and constant IFN-γ response over time, unlike the rapid strong IFN-γ response induced by wild-type strain. [Ref7138:Palomares-Resendiz et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis virB10 mutant strain. [Ref7138:Palomares-Resendiz et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella canis virB11 deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: A virB11 deletion mutant was constructed in Brucella canis to reduce virulence. Efficacy: The virB11 mutant was cleared by day 21 post-infection; no significant reduction in CFU after challenge reported. Immune response: Similar antibody isotype levels (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, IgM) compared to wild-type; mild and constant IFN-γ response over time, unlike the rapid strong IFN-γ response induced by wild-type strain. [Ref7138:Palomares-Resendiz et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis virB11 deletion mutant strain. [Ref7138:Palomares-Resendiz et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp28 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and protective ability of recombinant Omp28 from Brucella abortus as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: rOmp28-immunized mice showed 20-fold higher IgG1 and IgG2a titers compared to controls; spleen proliferation and bacterial burden were approximately 1.5-fold lower than PBS-treated mice after challenge. Immune response: Induction of both humoral (IgG1) and cell-mediated (IgG2a) immune responses was observed in rOmp28-immunized mice. [Ref7139:Lim et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp28 protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; no adjuvant mentioned. [Ref7139:Lim et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: pVF263 DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a DNA vaccine encoding the BAB1_0263 open reading frame of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Not reported protective efficacy; only pVF278 showed protection against challenge. Immune response: Induced dominant IgG2a antibody response and T-cell proliferative response; significant interferon gamma (IFN-γ) production upon restimulation with recombinant 263 protein; no IL-10 or IL-4 detected, indicating a Th1-dominated immune response. [Ref2664:Sislema-Egas et al., 2012]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the BAB1_0263 gene administered by intramuscular injection. [Ref2664:Sislema-Egas et al., 2012]

c_vaccine_name: pVF278 DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a DNA vaccine encoding the BAB1_0278 open reading frame of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Induced protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308. Immune response: Induced dominant IgG2a antibody response and T-cell proliferative response; did not induce IL-10 or IL-4, indicating a Th1-dominated immune response; no significant IFN-γ detected upon restimulation with recombinant 278 protein. [Ref2664:Sislema-Egas et al., 2012]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the BAB1_0278 gene administered by intramuscular injection. [Ref2664:Sislema-Egas et al., 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase OVA(257-264) subunit vaccine
c_description: The study introduces a polymeric protein chimera based on Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) fused with the OVA(257-264) peptide, designed to induce immunity without adjuvants. Efficacy: Immunization induced rapid activation and proliferation of OVA(257-264)-specific CD8+ T cells, generation of CD8+ effector cells, and a strong peptide-specific cytotoxic response dependent on TLR4 signaling. Immune response: The vaccine induced cross presentation of the peptide antigen, activation of CD8+ lymphocytes expressing activation markers CD69 and CD44, decreased IL-7Rα expression indicating effector cell generation, and TLR4-dependent cytotoxic T lymphocyte responses without adjuvants. [Ref7140:Berguer et al, 2012]
c_preparation: A decameric BLS protein with covalently attached OVA(257-264) peptide, administered without adjuvants. [Ref7140:Berguer et al, 2012]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; dendritic cells; transgenic OT-I T cells

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella pgm mutant vaccine
c_description: The pgm mutant of Brucella was constructed and studied for its biological function and effects on human trophoblast cells. Efficacy: The pgm mutant showed reduced adhesion and infection of human trophoblast cells compared to Brucella vaccine strain M5-90; sera of mice immunized with the pgm mutant were negative by agglutination tests. Immune response: Increased activity of IL-6, TNF-alpha, and lactic dehydrogenase in human trophoblast cells infected by the pgm mutant compared to Brucella vaccine strain M5-90; no increase in IL-10. [Ref7142:Wang et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Live pgm mutant strain of Brucella. [Ref7142:Wang et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella phosphoglucomutase subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified PGM protein was used to infect human trophoblast cells to study its effects. Immune response: Increased lactic dehydrogenase activity in human trophoblast cells treated with PGM protein compared to control; decreased IL-6 and TNF-alpha compared to control. [Ref7142:Wang et al, 2012]
c_preparation: Purified PGM protein. [Ref7142:Wang et al, 2012]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella virmugen gene mutant vaccine
c_description: Live attenuated vaccines are generated by mutation of genes encoding virulence factors ("virmugens") that have been proven feasible in animal models to make live attenuated vaccines by knocking out these genes. [Ref7143:Racz et al, 2013]
c_antigen: virmugen genes related to carbohydrate or nucleotide transport and metabolism; genes involving cell membrane biogenesis

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus 2308-SB6 delta wboA vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella abortus 2308 parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Showed longer survival time in mice (11 weeks) but offered less protection against challenge compared to some other mutants. Immune response: Induced protective immunity less effective than some other mutants; survival time in vivo not directly associated with protective immunity. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19-RB6 vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella abortus strain S19 parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Shorter survival time in mice (less than 6 weeks) but offered better protection against Brucella abortus 2308 challenge than some other mutants; did not induce abortion in pregnant sheep. Immune response: Induced protective immunity not directly correlated with survival time in vivo; effective in inducing protection against homologous challenge. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain NI-NB6 vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella melitensis NI parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Showed longer survival time in mice (11 weeks) but offered less protection against challenge compared to some other mutants. Immune response: Induced protective immunity less effective than some other mutants; survival time in vivo not directly associated with protective immunity. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion. [Ref7144:Wang et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit vaccine carrying Matrix 2 extracellular domain
c_description: The study evaluated Brucella abortus lumazine synthase (BLS), a highly immunogenic decameric protein, as a carrier for the influenza Matrix 2 extracellular domain (M2e) peptide, aiming to develop a broadly protective influenza vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with BLS-4M2e plus Iscomatrix adjuvant resulted in 100% survival; with alum adjuvant, 80% survival; BLS-4M2e alone protected 60% of mice; all results statistically significant compared to controls. Immune response: Immunization elicited significant humoral immune responses; fusion of four tandem M2e copies induced similar antibody levels without adjuvant, while one M2e copy required adjuvants for significant response. [Ref7145:Alvarez et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Chimeric proteins were generated by fusing one or four tandem copies of M2e to BLS, expressed in Escherichia coli, and assembled into decameric subunits exposing M2e peptides at the N-terminal ends; formulations included adjuvants such as Iscomatrix and alum. [Ref7145:Alvarez et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus 2308 delta BAB1_0542 vaccine
c_description: The ABC transporter ATPase gene (BAB1_0542) of Brucella abortus strain 2308 was inactivated by deleting a 446-bp fragment, generating a mutant strain S2308ΔATP with a rough phenotype and attenuated virulence. Efficacy: The mutant strain S2308ΔATP showed attenuated virulence in vitro and in vivo; immunization with S2308ΔATP protected mice from challenge with virulent strain; complemented strain restored smooth phenotype and survival comparable to wild type. Immune response: Expression levels of MHC I, MHC II, and co-stimulatory molecules were investigated in mice following infection with S2308ΔATP and wild type S2308, indicating immune activation differences. [Ref7148:Zhang et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Mutant strain S2308ΔATP with ABC transporter ATPase gene deletion, exhibiting rough phenotype and altered growth rate compared to wild type. [Ref7148:Zhang et al, 2013]
c_antigen: ABC transporter ATPase gene (BAB1_0542) deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BtuB subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. Immune response: Omp22 and Hia showed high adhesin probability and conferred invasive capacity; all proteins except FlgK reacted with sera from exposed hosts; BtuB, Hia, and FlgK stimulated mixed Th1-Th2 responses in mouse splenocytes; BtuB and Hia elicited nitric oxide release from splenocytes of S19 immunized mice. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; Capra hircus; Homo sapiens; Escherichia coli

c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
