c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. Immune response: Omp22 and Hia showed high adhesin probability and conferred invasive capacity; all proteins except FlgK reacted with sera from exposed hosts; BtuB, Hia, and FlgK stimulated mixed Th1-Th2 responses in mouse splenocytes; BtuB and Hia elicited nitric oxide release from splenocytes of S19 immunized mice. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; Capra hircus; Homo sapiens; Escherichia coli

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp22 subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. Immune response: Omp22 and Hia showed high adhesin probability and conferred invasive capacity; all proteins except FlgK reacted with sera from exposed hosts; BtuB, Hia, and FlgK stimulated mixed Th1-Th2 responses in mouse splenocytes; BtuB and Hia elicited nitric oxide release from splenocytes of S19 immunized mice. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation. [Ref7149:Gomez et al, 2013]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; Capra hircus; Homo sapiens; Escherichia coli

c_vaccine_name: DNA vaccine encoding SP41 from Brucella melitensis
c_description: A plasmid construct pCISP41 was established for expression of SP41 protein in mammalian cells to evaluate its role as a DNA vaccine against Brucella spp. Efficacy: DNA-SP41 vaccination induced specific IgG and T-cell responses but provided lower protection against B. melitensis 16M challenge in mice compared to the attenuated B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine Immune response: Induction of SP41-specific serum IgG antibodies; T-cell proliferative response; production of IFN-γ but not IL-5, indicating a T-helper-1-dominated immune response important for protection against intracellular Brucella infection [Ref7150:Al-Mariri et al, 2013]
c_preparation: DNA plasmid pCISP41 encoding SP41 protein [Ref7150:Al-Mariri et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M hfq mutant vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was constructed to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines Rev. 1 and M5-90, including residual virulence and inability to differentiate infection from vaccination. Efficacy: Reduced survival of the mutant strain in macrophages and mice; strong protective immunity against virulent Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in BALB/c mice. Immune response: Induction of anti-Brucella-specific IgG1 and IgG2a subtype responses; secretion of gamma interferon and interleukin-4; Hfq antigen allows serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals. [Ref7151:Zhang et al, 2013a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M with hfq gene deletion. [Ref7151:Zhang et al, 2013a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis strain 353-1 vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the safety, immunogenicity, and clearance of the natural rough mutant of Brucella suis strain 353-1 as a vaccine in domestic swine. Efficacy: The vaccine strain was nonpathogenic, cleared from most vaccinates by 10-12 weeks, did not cause significant tissue lesions, was phenotypically stable, and was not shed to sentinel animals. Immune response: Vaccination induced significant humoral responses, peripheral blood mononuclear cell proliferation, and interferon-gamma production compared to controls. [Ref7152:Stoffregen et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Live natural rough mutant strain 353-1 administered by conjunctival or intramuscular routes at doses of 5 × 10^7 CFU or 1-2 × 10^10 CFU. [Ref7152:Stoffregen et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis HSP and TF subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to assess the immunogenicity of Brucella melitensis HSP and TF proteins. Immune response: Immunized rabbit serum showed immunogenic response to HSP and TF proteins. [Ref7153:Ghasemi et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ABC-type transporter DNA vaccine
c_description: A DNA vaccine containing an open reading frame of genomic island 3, specific for Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis, was constructed and tested. Efficacy: The vaccine induced protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus 2308. Immune response: The vaccine elicited a dominant IgG2a antibody response, T-cell proliferative response, and significant interferon gamma (IFN-γ) production upon restimulation with recombinant 278a protein; no IL-4 induction was observed, indicating a typical T-helper 1 (TH1) response. [Ref7154:Riquelme-Neira et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the open reading frame with homology to an ABC-type transporter (pV278a) administered by intramuscular injection. [Ref7154:Riquelme-Neira et al, 2013]
c_antigen: open reading frame with homology to an ABC-type transporter (genomic island 3)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp16 subunit vaccine
c_description:
U-Omp16 from Brucella spp. was delivered by the nasal route as an adjuvant to induce immune responses. Efficacy: U-Omp16 increased antigen presence in lung tissues, induced systemic IgG and Th1 responses to ovalbumin, and ameliorated hypersensitivity to cow's milk protein by reducing clinical signs and anti-CMP IgE antibodies. Immune response: Induced inflammatory immune response in lung tissues; promoted Th1 immune responses; modulated Th2 allergic response towards Th1 immunity. [Ref7155:Ibañez et al, 2013]
The study proposes the development of a protective subunit vaccine based on Brucella Outer Membrane Protein (Omp16) antigens as an alternative to live attenuated vaccines, which have disadvantages. Immune response: The predicted epitopes are hypothesized to stimulate both B-cell and T-cell mediated immune responses, indicating potential protective capacity as an immunogenic candidate for an epitope-based vaccine against brucellosis. [Ref7263:Rezaei et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Unlipidated outer membrane protein Omp16 (U-Omp16) administered intranasally, co-administered with ovalbumin as a model antigen. [Ref7155:Ibañez et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L9 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified ribosomal protein L9 from the stationary-phase exoproteome of Brucella abortus as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Recombinant L9-immunized mice were protected against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 544. Immune response: The vaccine candidate induced serum antibody response and IFN-γ release from mice spleen cells, indicating immunogenicity. [Ref7156:Jain et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Recombinant ribosomal protein L9 was produced and used for immunization. [Ref7156:Jain et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase and Shiga toxin type 2 B subunit subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel immunogen was engineered by inserting the B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2 at the amino termini of Brucella lumazine synthase, creating a chimera designed to induce strong and long-lasting neutralizing antibodies. Efficacy: Immunized mice were completely protected against intravenous Stx2 challenge; immune sera transfer conferred complete protection to weaned mice against oral EHEC challenge. Immune response: The chimera induced a strong, long-lasting humoral immune response with high-affinity antibodies possessing potent neutralizing capacity against Stx2 and its variants. [Ref7157:Mejias et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Chimera consisting of the B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2 fused to Brucella lumazine synthase, a highly stable dimer of pentamers serving as a scaffold for foreign antigen display. [Ref7157:Mejias et al, 2013]
c_antigen: B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2; brucella lumazine synthase

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus betB deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study investigated a betB deletion mutant constructed from virulent Brucella abortus 544 as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The betB mutant was predominantly cleared from mouse spleens after 2 weeks post-infection and vaccination with the live betB mutant provided effective protection against challenge with the virulent wild-type strain. Immune response: The betB mutant showed increased adherence to host cells and enhanced phosphorylation of protein kinases promoting phagocytic activity; intracellular trafficking showed elevated colocalization with LAMP-1, indicating altered phagocytic pathway engagement. [Ref7158:Lee et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Live betB deletion mutant strain of Brucella abortus. [Ref7158:Lee et al, 2014]
c_model_host: HeLa cells; RAW 264.7 macrophages; Mus musculus

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 wzm gene deletion vaccine
c_description: Allelic exchange plasmids of wzm gene were constructed and partially knocked out in Brucella abortus S19 to evaluate effects on immunity induction. Efficacy: Immunity-eliciting ability was similar to wzt mutant but reduced compared with the S19 strain. Immune response: Cytokine secretion and INF-γ induction were measured; wzm deletion mutant induced immunity but less than S19. [Ref7159:Wang et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 wzt gene deletion vaccine
c_description: Allelic exchange plasmids of wzt gene were constructed and partially knocked out in Brucella abortus S19 to evaluate effects on immunity induction. Efficacy: Immunity-eliciting ability was similar to wzm mutant but reduced compared with the S19 strain; wzt gene may be more important in immunity regulation. Immune response: Cytokine secretion and INF-γ induction were measured; wzt deletion mutant induced immunity but less than S19. [Ref7159:Wang et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description:
OMVs from Brucella melitensis have been shown to be effective vaccines against B. melitensis challenge in mice. Efficacy: No additive effect on clearance of B. melitensis; however, mice receiving OMVs with antibiotics exhibited no Brucella replication post-treatment compared to antibiotics alone; mice receiving only vaccines did not show significant clearance. Immune response: OMV vaccinated mice developed significantly higher anti-Brucella IgG antibody titers at end of treatment compared to mice receiving only antibiotics; no increased IFN-γ production by splenocytes upon stimulation. [Ref7161:Jain-Gupta et al, 2014]
Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella melitensis have been shown to provide protection similar to the live attenuated strain Rev. 1 vaccine in mice but without the associated risks of live vaccines. Efficacy: Pluronic P85 enhanced the protection provided by OMVs against Brucella melitensis challenge in mice; P85 alone also improved bacterial clearance compared to saline controls Immune response: Enhanced total IgG antibody production with OMVs plus P85; no increase in IFN-γ or IL-4 cytokine levels observed; P85 induced nonspecific protection mechanisms requiring further study [Ref7141:Jain-Gupta et al, 2012]
Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are promising acellular vaccine candidates due to their heterogeneous composition and diverse functions. Efficacy: Both vaccine regimens induced protective levels significantly higher than the Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 live vaccine. Immune response: Both vaccine regimens induced strong Th1-biased immune responses. [Ref7316:Golshani et al, 2020]
This study investigated the protective immunity conferred by outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) derived from Brucella melitensis M5 strain. Efficacy: All three immunization routes (intramuscular, subcutaneous, intranasal) showed comparable protective efficacy characterized by significantly reduced bacterial burdens and milder histopathological lesions in the spleen. Immune response: Robust humoral immunity and CD4+ T cell-mediated immune responses were elicited by all three routes of immunization; intramuscular and subcutaneous routes induced severe reactogenicity initially, whereas intranasal did not. [Ref7439:Huang et al, 2025]
c_adjuvant: yes; Pluronic P85 | yes; Poly(I:C) or CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70 VG
c_preparation:
OMVs administered twice during antibiotic therapy. [Ref7161:Jain-Gupta et al, 2014]
OMVs combined with Pluronic P85 as an adjuvant [Ref7141:Jain-Gupta et al, 2012]
OMVs formulated with either Poly(I:C) or a combination of CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70 VG adjuvants. [Ref7316:Golshani et al, 2020]
OMVs derived from Brucella melitensis M5 strain (OMVs-M5) with weak activation of innate immunity and no cytotoxicity in ex vivo assays. [Ref7439:Huang et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase Stx2 B subunit subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel immunogen was developed based on the B subunit of Shiga toxin 2 (Stx2B) and the enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) to protect against Stx2-associated damage. Efficacy: Pups born to immunized dams showed comparable anti-Stx2B antibody titers, were totally protected against lethal systemic Stx2 injection up to 2-3 months postpartum, resisted oral EHEC challenge without symptoms, and survived subsequent intravenous Stx2 challenge due to prolonged active immunity. Immune response: Maternal immunization induced anti-Stx2B neutralizing IgG antibodies transmitted through breast-feeding; pups developed active and specific immune responses after surviving EHEC infection. [Ref7162:Mejias et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Chimeric protein combining Brucella lumazine synthase and Shiga toxin 2 B subunit. [Ref7162:Mejias et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Omp16 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study presents a new candidate vector vaccine against Brucella abortus consisting of recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella L7/L12 and Omp16 proteins. Efficacy: The vaccine provided a high level of protectiveness against B. abortus infection comparable to the commercial B. abortus strain 19 vaccine and superior to the strain 19 vaccine combined with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant. Immune response: Induced strong antigen-specific T-cell immune response with high numbers of CD4(+) and CD8(+) cells, increased IFN-γ concentration, and promoted formation of IgG antibodies predominantly of isotype IgG2a against Brucella L7/L12 and Omp16 proteins. [Ref7163:Tabynov et al, 2014]
c_preparation: A bivalent vaccine formulation composed of a mixture of recombinant influenza A subtype H5N1 and H1N1 viruses expressing Brucella L7/L12 and Omp16 proteins, combined with adjuvants Montanide Gel01 or chitosan to increase effectiveness. [Ref7163:Tabynov et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain A19 delta VirB12 vaccine
c_description: The A19-delta VirB12 deletion mutant of Brucella abortus was constructed by homologous recombination technology. Efficacy: The A19-delta VirB12 mutant provided statistically significant protection against Brucella abortus 2308 challenge, comparable to the parental A19 strain. Immune response: Western blotting confirmed absence of VirB12 protein expression; the mutant elicited strong protective immunity. [Ref7164:Yi et al, 2013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with VirB12 gene deletion, administered intraperitoneally at 5.0 x 10^4 CFU dose. [Ref7164:Yi et al, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus L7/L12 influenza vector vaccine (Flu-NS1-124 construct)
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Novel candidate vaccines were generated based on recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella ribosomal protein L7/L12 from the NS1 open reading frame. Efficacy: Highest antibody response to Brucella antigen was observed with L7/L12 expressing constructs; protective efficacy in guinea pigs was comparable to commercial live B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. Immune response: Strong antibody response (ELISA GMT 242.5-735.0) induced by L7/L12 constructs; T-cell response lower than Omp16 constructs; conjunctival immunization optimal for T-cell response. [Ref7165:Tabynov et al, 2014a]
c_preparation: Four recombinant influenza A viral constructs of subtypes H5N1 or H1N1 expressing L7/L12 were produced; mono- or bivalent vaccine formulations administered via prime-boost intranasal, conjunctival, or subcutaneous immunization. [Ref7165:Tabynov et al, 2014a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Omp16 influenza A H5N1 vector vaccine (Flu-NS1-124 construct)
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
Novel candidate vaccines were generated based on recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella outer membrane protein Omp16 from the NS1 open reading frame. Efficacy: Highest T-cell immune response observed with Omp16 expressing constructs, comparable to commercial live B. abortus strain 19 vaccine; protective efficacy in guinea pigs comparable to commercial vaccine. Immune response: Strong T-cell response (ELISPOT 337 ± 52 to 651 ± 45 spots/4×10^5 cells) induced by Omp16 constructs; antibody response lower than L7/L12 constructs; conjunctival immunization optimal for T-cell response. [Ref7165:Tabynov et al, 2014a]
The recombinant strain Flu-NS1-124-Omp16 (H5N1) of influenza virus was constructed using reverse genetics technology to develop a vector anti-brucellosis vaccine. [Ref7208:Sadikaliyeva et al, 2015]
c_preparation:
Four recombinant influenza A viral constructs of subtypes H5N1 or H1N1 expressing Omp16 were produced; mono- or bivalent vaccine formulations administered via prime-boost intranasal, conjunctival, or subcutaneous immunization. [Ref7165:Tabynov et al, 2014a]
Recombinant influenza virus strain Flu-NS1-124-Omp16 (H5N1) expressing the Brucella abortus Omp16 gene. [Ref7208:Sadikaliyeva et al, 2015]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; guinea pig; chicken embryos (10-day developing)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis TF BP26 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description:
The study addresses the need for a protective subunit vaccine against Brucella melitensis due to problems with the live attenuated Rev. 1 vaccine used in ovine brucellosis prophylaxis. Efficacy: Not reported (no in vivo or in vitro efficacy data presented) Immune response: The chimeric protein is predicted to induce both B-cell and T-cell mediated immune responses based on epitope analysis. [Ref7166:Ghasemi et al, 2014]
The study used the chimeric antigen TF/Bp26/Omp31 (TBO) as a model protein candidate for stimulating protection against virulent Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Immunized mice with CaP/TBO nanoparticles showed a higher degree of protection against Brucella melitensis 16M challenge compared to IO/TBO vaccinated animals. Immune response: Both CaP/TBO and IO/TBO nanoparticle vaccines stimulated mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses as indicated by antibody levels. [Ref7420:Goudarzi et al, 2025]
c_preparation:
A synthetic chimeric gene encoding fragments of TF, BP26 (93-111), and Omp31 (48-74) proteins was designed and modeled in silico to predict the 3D structure. [Ref7166:Ghasemi et al, 2014]
Recombinant TBO protein was loaded onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles (CaP/TBO) and iron oxide nanoparticles (IO/TBO) to serve as adjuvants and delivery systems; vaccines were administered subcutaneously. [Ref7420:Goudarzi et al, 2025]
c_antigen: TF; BP26 (93-111); Omp31 (48-74) | TF/Bp26/Omp31 (TBO) chimeric antigen

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis Omp22 deletion vaccine
c_description: Two previously characterized B. ovis attenuated mutants including Δomp22 were evaluated as homologous vaccines for specific prophylaxis of B. ovis infection. Efficacy: Protective efficacy against B. ovis similar to that observed with B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine. Immune response: Induced higher levels of anti-B. ovis IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG2b antibodies than Rev 1; splenocytes secreted similar TNF-α, IL12(p40), and high IFN-γ; higher IL-1α levels than Rev 1; lower IL-10 levels than Rev 1. [Ref7167:Sancho et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis Omp25d deletion vaccine
c_description: Two previously characterized B. ovis attenuated mutants including Δomp25d were evaluated as homologous vaccines for specific prophylaxis of B. ovis infection. Efficacy: Protective efficacy against B. ovis similar to that observed with B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine. Immune response: Induced higher levels of anti-B. ovis IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG2b antibodies than Rev 1; splenocytes secreted similar TNF-α, IL12(p40), and high IFN-γ; higher IL-1α levels than Rev 1; lower IL-10 levels than Rev 1. [Ref7167:Sancho et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L9 DNA vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding ribosomal protein L9 of Brucella abortus (pVaxL9) was generated to evaluate its immunogenicity and protective efficacy. Efficacy: The L9 based DNA vaccine conferred significant protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice; groups receiving pVaxL9 priming plus recombinant L9 boosting and those immunised with electroporation showed better protection. Immune response: Induction of anti-L9 IgG antibodies of both IgG1 and IgG2a isotypes; splenocyte proliferation; Th1 type cytokine release (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2); IFN-γ production by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, especially in priming plus boosting and electroporation groups. [Ref7168:Jain et al, 2014a]
c_preparation: Intramuscular immunisation of pVaxL9 plasmid DNA; boosting with recombinant L9 protein in some groups; in vivo electroporation used in some immunisation groups. [Ref7168:Jain et al, 2014a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 Δery live vaccine
c_description: A Brucella abortus 2308 ery promoter mutant (Δery) was constructed to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines S19 and RB51, aiming for a safer and more potent vaccine that allows differentiation between natural and vaccinated infection. Efficacy: The Δery mutant showed significantly attenuated growth in macrophages and mice and induced high protective immunity in mice against virulent Brucella abortus 2308 infection. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG response; stimulated expression of interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and interleukin-4 (IL-4); expression of EryA antigen enabled serological differentiation between natural and vaccinated infection. [Ref7169:Zhang et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion in ery promoter (Δery mutant). [Ref7169:Zhang et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis HspA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the potential of recombinant HspA protein from Brucella melitensis as a subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Administration of recombinant HspA resulted in a significant reduction in bacterial load and a high degree of protection against Brucella melitensis challenge compared to control mice (p<0.001). Immune response: The vaccine elicited mixed TH1/TH2 immune responses with higher IgG1 than IgG2a titers; splenocytes showed strong recall proliferation and produced high levels of IFN-γ, IL-12, IL-10, and IL-6, with very low IL-5 and IL-4. [Ref7170:Ghasemi et al, 2014a]
c_preparation: Recombinant HspA protein was cloned in pDEST42 and used as a subunit vaccine. [Ref7170:Ghasemi et al, 2014a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis wadB mutant vaccine
c_description: The wadB mutant of Brucella ovis was generated by mutating the wadB gene, which encodes an LPS core glycosyltransferase, resulting in defects in LPS structure and outer membrane topology. Efficacy: The wadB mutant was attenuated in mice and protected them against B. ovis challenge. [Ref7171:Soler-Lloréns et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wadB mutant strain of Brucella ovis. [Ref7171:Soler-Lloréns et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis wadC mutant vaccine
c_description: The wadC mutant of Brucella ovis was generated by mutating the wadC gene, which encodes an LPS core glycosyltransferase, resulting in defects in LPS structure and outer membrane topology. Efficacy: The wadC mutant was attenuated in mice and protected them against B. ovis challenge. [Ref7171:Soler-Lloréns et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wadC mutant strain of Brucella ovis. [Ref7171:Soler-Lloréns et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus glucokinase subunit vaccine
c_description: A recombinant subunit vaccine molecule comprising the truncated region of glucokinase (r-glk) gene from Brucella abortus strain 19 was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21DE3 host to engineer a safe and effective vaccine candidate for animals and humans. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed specific antibody titer of 1:64,000 with predominant IgG2a and IgG2b isotypes indicating Th1 response; in vitro cell viability of 81.20% and 78.5% against lethal challenge of Brucella abortus 544 and Brucella melitensis 16M respectively; significantly protected mice after intraperitoneal challenge with no signs of necrosis or vacuolization in liver and spleen tissues compared to controls. Immune response: Development of Th1 directed immune responses indicated by predominant IgG2a and IgG2b isotypes; elevated splenic lymphocyte proliferation at 25 μg/ml protein concentration suggesting memory immune response; elevated B-cell response associated with Th1 immunity. [Ref7172:Vrushabhendrappa et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant glucokinase protein expressed in E. coli BL21DE3. [Ref7172:Vrushabhendrappa et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: DNA vaccine encoding Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase of Brucella abortus
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA vaccine encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase using BPPcysMPEG as an adjuvant. Efficacy: The pcDNA-SOD/BPPcysMPEG formulation induced improved protection against virulent B. abortus 2308 challenge compared to pcDNA-SOD alone. Immune response: Induced antigen-specific humoral responses (IgG2a, IgG1, secretory IgA), T-cell proliferative responses, increased gamma interferon production, and cytotoxic responses demonstrated by lysis of infected macrophages. [Ref7173:Retamal-Díaz et al, 2014]
c_preparation: Intranasal coadministration of plasmid pcDNA-SOD with the TLR2/6 agonist adjuvant BPPcysMPEG. [Ref7173:Retamal-Díaz et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Omp16 recombinant vector vaccine with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant
c_description: The study introduces a novel influenza viral vector vaccine expressing Brucella ribosomal L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins combined with the adjuvant Montanide Gel01, designed for immunization of pregnant heifers. Efficacy: The vector vaccine provided good protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection, preventing abortion and reducing infection indices in heifers and their fetuses or calves; protection was comparable to commercial vaccines Brucella abortus strain 19 and strain RB51. [Ref7174:Tabynov et al, 2014b]
c_preparation: Influenza A viral vector expressing Brucella L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins formulated with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant. [Ref7174:Tabynov et al, 2014b]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis DnaK and Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Combination of recombinant DnaK and recombinant Omp31 proteins used as a subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Combination vaccine induced protection statistically similar to that of Rev. 1 vaccine, superior to each component alone. Immune response: Not separately detailed beyond combined vaccine efficacy; implied enhanced protective immune response compared to single components. [Ref7176:Ghasemi et al, 2014b]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins DnaK and Omp31; no adjuvant mentioned. [Ref7176:Ghasemi et al, 2014b]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis DnaK subunit vaccine
c_description: The dnak gene was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli to produce recombinant DnaK protein used as a subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with DnaK showed significant protection against Brucella infection compared to controls (p<0.001), though less than protection by Rev. 1 vaccine (p<0.05). Immune response: Strong lymphocyte proliferative response; balanced IgG2a and IgG1 antibody levels; high IFN-γ, IL-12, and IL-6 production; no detectable IL-4; very low IL-10 and IL-5, indicating a Th1 dominant immune response. [Ref7176:Ghasemi et al, 2014b]
c_preparation: Recombinant DnaK protein expressed in E. coli; no adjuvant mentioned. [Ref7176:Ghasemi et al, 2014b]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis polysaccharide protein subunit vaccine
c_description: A subunit vaccine candidate was produced from Brucella suis 145 (biovar 4) expressing both the A antigen of Brucella abortus and the M antigen of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed statistically significant reduction in bacterial colonization compared to unvaccinated controls; as little as 1 ng protected mice against B. suis 145 infection; a single 1 μg injection protected mice for at least 14 months. Immune response: A single immunization induced a serum IgG response to Brucella antigens that remained elevated for up to 9 weeks. [Ref7177:Cherwonogrodzky et al, 2014]
c_preparation: The preparation consisted mostly of polysaccharide (>90% wt/wt; both cell-associated PS and exo-PS combined) and a small amount of protein (1 to 3%) with no apparent nucleic acids; the vaccine was thermostable due to heat treatment (boiling-water bath, autoclaving) and contained no added adjuvant. [Ref7177:Cherwonogrodzky et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant Brucella Omp31 antigen vaccine
c_description: Canine brucellosis caused by Brucella canis currently lacks a vaccine; this study evaluates Omp31 as a candidate antigen for vaccine development. Efficacy: Recombinant Omp31 with different adjuvants and the prime-boost strategy conferred protection against B. canis infection in mice. Immune response: Strong IgG antibody response induced; spleen cells from recombinant Omp31-immunized mice produced gamma interferon and IL-4, indicating a mixed Th1-Th2 immune response. [Ref7178:Clausse et al, 2014]
c_adjuvant: yes; incomplete Freund adjuvant; aluminum hydroxide; Quil A; Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp31 antigen formulated with various adjuvants (incomplete Freund adjuvant, aluminum hydroxide, Quil A, Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR); plasmid pCIOmp31 DNA vaccine; and a prime-boost strategy with pCIOmp31 plasmid followed by recombinant Omp31 protein boost. [Ref7178:Clausse et al, 2014]

c_vaccine_name: VirB7 protein vaccine
c_description: The vaccine targets VirB7, a component of the type IV secretion system, a key virulence factor mediating intracellular survival of Brucella spp. Efficacy: Mice immunized with VirB7 showed almost 1 log reduction in spleen bacterial load after challenge with live Brucella abortus compared to unvaccinated controls; sera from immunized dogs mediated significant bacteriolysis of B. canis in vitro. Immune response: Immunized mice splenocytes produced significant and specific IFN-γ without IL-4, indicating a Th1-type response; immunized dogs’ PBMCs produced significantly higher IFN-γ upon stimulation; positive delayed-type hypersensitivity skin test in most immunized dogs; anti-VirB7 antibodies mediated complement-dependent bacteriolysis. [Ref7179:Pollak et al, 2015]
c_preparation: VirB7 protein administered subcutaneously in three doses with QuilA adjuvant. [Ref7179:Pollak et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: VirB9 protein vaccine
c_description: The vaccine targets VirB9, a component of the type IV secretion system, a key virulence factor mediating intracellular survival of Brucella spp. Efficacy: Mice immunized with VirB9 showed almost 1 log reduction in spleen bacterial load after challenge with live Brucella abortus compared to unvaccinated controls; sera from immunized dogs mediated significant bacteriolysis of B. canis in vitro. Immune response: Immunized mice splenocytes produced significant and specific IFN-γ without IL-4, indicating a Th1-type response; immunized dogs’ PBMCs produced significantly higher IFN-γ upon stimulation; positive delayed-type hypersensitivity skin test in most immunized dogs; anti-VirB9 antibodies mediated complement-dependent bacteriolysis. [Ref7179:Pollak et al, 2015]
c_preparation: VirB9 protein administered subcutaneously in three doses with QuilA adjuvant. [Ref7179:Pollak et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 purD mutant vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon mutagenesis to create purD and purF gene mutants of the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to further attenuate the strain. Efficacy: Immunization with purD mutant protected mice against virulent B. abortus strain 544 challenge at a level similar to the parent RB51 strain; mutants showed significantly decreased intracellular survival and lowered persistence in mice. [Ref7180:Truong et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Mutants of RB51 strain with disrupted purD or purF genes were constructed and characterized. [Ref7180:Truong et al, 2015]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; murine macrophage-like RAW264.7 cells; HeLa cells

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 purF mutant vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon mutagenesis to create purF and purD gene mutants of the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to further attenuate the strain. Efficacy: Immunization with purF mutant protected mice against virulent B. abortus strain 544 challenge at a level similar to the parent RB51 strain; mutants showed significantly decreased intracellular survival and lowered persistence in mice. [Ref7180:Truong et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Mutants of RB51 strain with disrupted purF or purD genes were constructed and characterized. [Ref7180:Truong et al, 2015]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; murine macrophage-like RAW264.7 cells; HeLa cells

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus membrane fusogenic protein delta vaccine
c_description: The Δmfp::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus was evaluated as a live vaccine candidate due to its reduced virulence and persistence in mouse models. Efficacy: The Δmfp::kan strain induced greater protection than the RB51 vaccine and similar protection to the S19 vaccine in mouse models. [Ref7181:de et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Δmfp::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus. [Ref7181:de et al, 2015]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (C57BL/6 and IRF-1 knockout mice)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 19 delta vaccine
c_description: The Δomp19::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus was evaluated as a live vaccine candidate due to its attenuation and residual virulence in mouse models. Efficacy: The Δomp19::kan strain induced protection similar to that of the RB51 vaccine in mouse models. [Ref7181:de et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Δomp19::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus. [Ref7181:de et al, 2015]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (C57BL/6 and IRF-1 knockout mice)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus L7/L12 truncated Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated a fusion protein vaccine based on truncated Omp31 and L7/L12 antigens, which are immunodominant and conserved in human Brucella pathogens. Efficacy: Vaccination provided significant protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge in mice. Immune response: Induced strong specific IgG response with higher IgG2a titers, significant IFN-γ and IL-2 production, T-cell proliferation, and a persistent Th1 oriented response lasting 12 weeks after first immunization. [Ref7182:Golshani et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein combining truncated Omp31 and L7/L12 antigens. [Ref7182:Golshani et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Ndk subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective effect of recombinant protein encoded by Brucella abortus 544 ndk gene against B. abortus infection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: rNdk immunized mice showed significantly lower spleen proliferation and bacterial burden compared to control (MBP-immunized) mice after virulent B. abortus challenge (P < 0.01). Immune response: rNdk induced vigorous IgG production with higher IgG2a than IgG1 titers, strong induction of IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines (TNF, MCP1, IL-6), but low IL-10, indicating predominantly cell-mediated immune responses along with humoral immunity. [Ref7183:Hop et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant Ndk protein was cloned and expressed using a pMAL expression system and purified for immunization. [Ref7183:Hop et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus LPS-Neisseria meningitidis OMV conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop an efficacious vaccine against brucellosis using antigenic determinants of Brucella cell wall, specifically LPS, conjugated to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B OMV as a carrier protein. Efficacy: The LPS-OMV conjugate induced the highest anti-LPS IgG titers, approximately 5-fold and 1.3-fold higher than LPS alone and LPS + OMV noncovalent complex, respectively, with a 100-120-fold rise of anti-LPS IgG in mice after the third injection. Immune response: The conjugated LPS-OMV elicited significantly higher IgG antibody titers against LPS compared to other formulations, indicating strong immunogenicity. [Ref7184:Siadat et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Brucella abortus LPS was conjugated to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B outer membrane vesicle (OMV) using carbodiimide and adipic acid-mediated coupling and linking. [Ref7184:Siadat et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus LPS-Neisseria meningitidis OMV noncovalent complex subunit vaccine
c_description: A noncovalent complex of Brucella abortus LPS and Neisseria meningitidis OMV was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The LPS + OMV complex induced higher IgG titers than LPS alone but lower than the conjugated LPS-OMV vaccine. Immune response: The noncovalent LPS + OMV complex elicited increased anti-LPS IgG titers, approximately 1.3-fold lower than the conjugated vaccine. [Ref7184:Siadat et al, 2015]
c_preparation: LPS combined with OMV without covalent conjugation. [Ref7184:Siadat et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus delta pgm E. coli O157:H7 recombinant vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A bivalent vaccine was developed to prevent transmission from cattle to humans of Brucella abortus and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC). Efficacy: Mice immunized with BabΔpgm(EITH7) cleared intestinal E. coli O157:H7 infection three times faster (4 days) than mice immunized with BabΔpgm carrier strain (12 days); also elicited protective immune response against Brucella abortus infection. Immune response: Induction of anti-EITH7 IgA antibodies and protective immune response against both Brucella abortus and STEC pathogens. [Ref7185:Iannino et al, 2015]
c_preparation: A 66kDa chimeric antigen composed of EspA, Intimin, Tir, and H7 flagellin (EITH7) from STEC was constructed and expressed in Brucella abortus Δpgm vaccine strain (BabΔpgm). [Ref7185:Iannino et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 delta per vaccine
c_description:
A modified Brucella abortus strain 19 mutant (S19Δper) with intermediate rough phenotype and residual O-polysaccharide was developed by deletion of the perosamine synthetase gene to reduce residual virulence and enable DIVA capability. Efficacy: S19Δper conferred protection in mice similar to the parental S19 vaccine strain. Immune response: Immunized mice produced strong immune responses with higher levels of IFN-γ and IgG2a, indicating a Th1 cell mediated immunity bias; sera did not agglutinate with RBPT antigen, supporting DIVA capability. S19Δper showed increased susceptibility to serum complement and polymyxin B. [Ref7186:Lalsiamthara et al, 2015]
A live Brucella abortus S19 perosamine synthetase gene mutant (S19∆per) was used to explore immunological potential in mice. Efficacy: Not directly reported; transcriptome data showed activation of immune pathways suggesting immunogenic potential. Immune response: Activation of MHC-I and MHC-II antigen-processing pathways; regulation of NF-kappa B signalling, chemokine signalling, T-cell receptor pathway, apoptosis, TNF signalling, and nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor signalling pathways indicating a robust immune response. [Ref7328:Solanki et al, 2020]
Brucella abortus S19Δper is a perosamine synthetase wbkB gene deletion mutant derived from strain 19, developed to overcome safety and serodiagnostic interference drawbacks of the conventional S19 vaccine. Efficacy: All immunized buffaloes were protected against challenge with virulent B. abortus S544; lower bacterial burden in lymph nodes and absence of gross lesions observed in vaccinated animals. Immune response: S19Δper immunized animals showed significantly low anti-lipopolysaccharide antibody levels; sera exhibited moderate to weak agglutination to RBPT antigen allowing differentiation from S19 vaccinated and clinically infected animals; S19Δper was more sensitive to complement-mediated lysis than parent strain S19. [Ref7353:Chaudhuri et al, 2021]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated S19Δper mutant with intermediate rough lipopolysaccharide phenotype. [Ref7186:Lalsiamthara et al, 2015]
Live attenuated mutant strain of Brucella abortus S19 with deletion in perosamine synthetase gene. [Ref7328:Solanki et al, 2020]
Administered at normal dose (4 × 10^10 CFU/animal) and reduced dose (2 × 10^9 CFU/animal) in buffaloes; bacterial persistence assessed in buffalo calves 42 days post inoculation. [Ref7353:Chaudhuri et al, 2021]
c_antigen: perosamine synthetase gene deletion | perosamine synthetase gene mutant (S19∆per) | wbkB gene deletion (perosamine synthetase mutant)
c_model_host: Mus musculus; guinea pig; buffalo calves

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BP26 recombinant pseudorabies virus vector vaccine
c_description: The study developed and purified a recombinant pseudorabies virus with deletions in TK and gE genes carrying the bp26 gene of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: The recombinant virus elicited high titers of humoral antibodies against Brucella and pseudorabies virus, and induced strong Brucella-specific lymphocyte proliferation and interferon gamma production. Immune response: Induction of both humoral immunity (high antibody titers) and cellular immunity (lymphocyte proliferation and interferon gamma production) against Brucella and pseudorabies virus. [Ref7187:Yao et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant pseudorabies virus with ΔTK/ΔgE deletions expressing Brucella melitensis bp26 gene. [Ref7187:Yao et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: B. melitensis vaccine strain M5-90ΔwboA
c_description: A wboA mutant was derived from Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5-90 to address drawbacks of current vaccines including inability to serologically differentiate vaccinated from infected animals. Efficacy: The M5-90ΔwboA strain showed reduced survival in macrophages and mice, induced protective immunity comparable to parental M5-90 strain in mice, and elicited specific IgG and cytokine responses; in sheep, it induced IFN-γ secretion and did not cause positive results in standard serological tests. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG, secretion of IFN-γ and IL-2 in mice; IFN-γ secretion in sheep; T-cell responses (CD4+, CD8+) observed; allowed serological differentiation between natural infection and vaccination using WboA antigen probes. [Ref7188:Li et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wboA deletion mutant of B. melitensis strain M5-90. [Ref7188:Li et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant Brucella urease (rUrease) vaccine
c_description: The study examined immune response and protection elicited by recombinant Brucella urease protein as a subunit vaccine administered subcutaneously and intraperitoneally in mice. Efficacy: Subcutaneous vaccination conferred a higher degree of protection against virulent Brucella melitensis, B. abortus, and B. suis challenge compared to intraperitoneal vaccination (p ≤ 0.05). Immune response: rUrease induced mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses with high titers of specific IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies; splenocytes showed strong recall proliferation and produced high levels of IL-4, IL-12, and IFN-γ. [Ref7189:Abkar et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant urease protein cloned in pET28a vector and administered as a subunit vaccine via subcutaneous and intraperitoneal routes. [Ref7189:Abkar et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis strain delta abcBA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the Brucella ovis ΔabcBA strain as a vaccine candidate in mice to assess protection against wild-type B. ovis challenge. Efficacy: Single or multiple immunizations with non-encapsulated strain provided mild protection with reduced liver bacterial loads but not spleen; encapsulated vaccine significantly improved protection in both mouse strains and prevented lesions in spleen and liver. [Ref7190:Silva et al, 2015]
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated as an encapsulated live attenuated ΔabcBA strain; both single and multiple doses were tested, with encapsulation significantly improving protection. [Ref7190:Silva et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella L7/L12 truncated Omp31 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate and compare the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the L7/L12-TOmp31 construct administered as DNA/DNA and DNA/protein vaccine regimens. Efficacy: The DNA/Pro regimen provided higher protection levels against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge compared to the DNA/DNA regimen. Immune response: Higher IgG1 and IgG2a antibody titers and significantly increased IFN-γ production by splenocytes were observed in DNA/Pro-immunized mice compared to DNA alone. [Ref7191:Golshani et al, 2015a]
c_preparation: The vaccine was administered as a DNA priming followed by protein boosting regimen (DNA/Pro) or DNA alone (DNA/DNA). [Ref7191:Golshani et al, 2015a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Omp31 BP26 fusion subunit vaccine
c_description: The study focuses on a chimeric gene encoding fragments of trigger factor, Omp31, and BP26 from Brucella melitensis as a potential subunit vaccine candidate due to concerns about live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: Antibodies against rTOB were detected in 76.5% of sera from infected patients; vaccinated rabbit sera strongly reacted with rTOB. Immune response: The fusion protein elicited antibody responses in both vaccinated rabbits and infected human patients, indicating immunogenicity. [Ref7192:Amani et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein (rTOB) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21-DE3 and purified by Ni-NTA agarose column. [Ref7192:Amani et al, 2015]
c_antigen: trigger factor (TF), Omp31(48-74), BP26(87-111) fusion protein (TOB)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis strain 2 bacterial ghost vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was generated by cloning the lysis gene E and temperature-sensitive regulator cassette into a shuttle plasmid, which was introduced into attenuated Brucella suis live vaccine S2 bacteria to produce bacterial ghosts by inducing lysis gene E expression. Efficacy: The bacterial ghosts demonstrated protection levels against Brucella melitensis 16M challenge similar to the attenuated Brucella suis live vaccine S2. Immune response: Induced pathogen-specific serum IgG antibody response, spleen CD3(+) and CD4(+) T cell responses, and secretion of gamma interferon and interleukin-4 comparable to the attenuated live vaccine. [Ref7193:Liu et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Bacterial ghosts produced from Brucella suis strain 2 live vaccine S2 by induction of lysis gene E expression. [Ref7193:Liu et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 2308 wbkA mutant vaccine
c_description: The Brucella abortus 2308 wbkA mutant (2308ΔwbkA) was constructed to evaluate its virulence and potential as a vaccine. Efficacy: The 2308ΔwbkA mutant showed attenuated survival in macrophages and mice and induced high protective immunity against wild-type infection. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response and secretion of gamma interferon; antibodies to 2308ΔwbkA detected in mouse sera, suggesting potential for serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals. [Ref7194:Li et al, 2015a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of wbkA gene. [Ref7194:Li et al, 2015a]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; RAW 264.7 murine macrophage cell line; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: Brucella O-polysaccharide C epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: The study revisited the structural identity of the C epitope of Brucella O-polysaccharide, revealing a unique capping perosamine tetrasaccharide with specific interresidue linkages essential for the epitope. [Ref7195:Zygmunt et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Synthetic oligosaccharide glycoconjugates were used to demonstrate the structural requirements of the epitope. [Ref7195:Zygmunt et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus L7/L12 Omp16 influenza viral vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A novel influenza viral vector Brucella abortus vaccine expressing ribosomal proteins L7/L12 or Omp16 was created to provide cross-protection against Brucella melitensis in cattle. Efficacy: Provided 100% protection against abortion in vaccinated pregnant heifers and 90-100% cross-protection of heifers and their calves or fetuses after challenge with B. melitensis 16M; protection comparable to commercial B. abortus strain 19 vaccine; significant reduction in infection and colonization indices in tissues (P=0.02 to P<0.0001). [Ref7196:Tabynov et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins formulated with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant. [Ref7196:Tabynov et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus T cell peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted T cell epitopes of Brucella abortus and evaluate their vaccine potential in mice as a safer alternative to current animal vaccines that cause abortions and are pathogenic to humans. Efficacy: Mice immunized with peptide formulations showed significantly higher splenocyte proliferation and IFN-γ production and significant protection compared to PBS controls. The DNA vaccine construct also conferred significant protection (1.66 protection units) compared to PBS and empty vector controls. Immune response: Immunization induced strong IFN-γ responses and splenocyte proliferation to the selected peptides, indicating a Th1-type immune response supportive of protection. [Ref7197:Afley et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Selected peptides were co-administered either entrapped in PLG microparticles (EPLG-Pep) or adsorbed on PLG microparticles (APLG-Pep). [Ref7197:Afley et al, 2015]
c_antigen: MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted T cell peptides

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 phage lysate inactived vaccine with aluminium hydroxide gel adjuvant
c_description: The study introduces a phage lysate vaccine generated using brucellaphage 'ϕLd' lysing Brucella abortus strain 19 cultures, adsorbed on aluminium hydroxide gel as an adjuvant. Efficacy: The aluminium hydroxide gel adsorbed lysate vaccine exhibited dose-dependent protective potency, with the highest dose showing greater protection than the standard S19 vaccine. Immune response: The vaccine induced both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses, with three polypeptides (~16, 19, and 23 kDa) identified as immuno-dominant antigens responsible for the immune response. [Ref7198:Jain et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Lysate prepared from 24 h incubated Brucella abortus S19 broth cultures (~10^8 CFU/ml), adsorbed on aluminium hydroxide gel (0.1% aluminium concentration) with antigenic dose of 0.52 μg protein and 60 μg carbohydrate (CHO). [Ref7198:Jain et al, 2015]
c_antigen: immuno-dominant polypeptides of approximately 16, 19 and 23 kDa

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis delta abcBA vaccine
c_description:
This study aimed to evaluate protection induced by the vaccine candidate B. ovis ΔabcBA against experimental challenge with wild type B. ovis in rams. Efficacy: Immunization, particularly with encapsulated B. ovis ΔabcBA, prevented infection, secretion of wild type B. ovis in semen and urine, shedding of neutrophils in semen, and development of clinical changes, gross and microscopic lesions induced by wild type B. ovis. [Ref7199:Silva et al, 2015a]
Brucella ovis ∆abcBA is a live attenuated candidate vaccine strain tested for protection against Brucella melitensis infection. Efficacy: Both vaccine formulations reduced Brucella melitensis 16M counts in liver and spleen compared to nonimmunized controls, with approximately 1-log10 reduction in spleen bacterial load. Immune response: Splenocytes from mice immunized with Bo∆abcBA encapsulated with alginate plus VpB secreted IFN-γ upon stimulation with B. melitensis antigens, whereas those immunized with alginate alone did not. Spleen size was larger in mice immunized with alginate formulation compared to alginate plus VpB or controls. [Ref7327:Costa et al, 2020]
The Brucella ovis ∆abcBA strain encapsulated in alginate provides an experimental vaccine formulation that protects against Brucella spp. infection. Efficacy: The formulation with alginate and chitosan resulted in the lowest bacterial recovery in spleen and liver compared to non-vaccinated mice; Poloxamer 407 formulation did not reduce bacterial recovery significantly. Immune response: Alginate and chitosan formulation induced higher levels of Immunoglobulin G, with an increase in the IgG2b subclass, indicating a Th1 type immune response important for controlling intracellular infections; Poloxamer 407 did not induce significant humoral response. [Ref7422:Brunno et al, 2024]
c_adjuvant: no | yes; alginate; alginate plus vitelline protein B (VpB) | yes; alginate and chitosan
c_preparation:
B. ovis ΔabcBA strain encapsulated with sterile alginate or non encapsulated vaccine strain. [Ref7199:Silva et al, 2015a]
Two formulations were tested: Bo∆abcBA encapsulated with alginate alone and Bo∆abcBA encapsulated with alginate plus vitelline protein B (VpB). [Ref7327:Costa et al, 2020]
B. ovis ∆abcBA strain encapsulated by alginate with chitosan or with copolymer Poloxamer 407 as polymeric adjuvants. [Ref7422:Brunno et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 ΔcydC ΔcydD live attenuated double mutant vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. Immune response: Mutants induced a mixed but T-helper-1-biased humoral and cellular immune response in immunized mice. [Ref7200:Truong et al, 2015a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated. [Ref7200:Truong et al, 2015a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 cydC deletion vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated. [Ref7200:Truong et al, 2015a]
c_antigen: cydC deletion; cydD deletion; purD deletion; cydC cydD double deletion; cydC purD double deletion
