c_vaccine_name: rOmp31 and rTF subunit vaccines
c_description: Subunit vaccines were developed using recombinant outer membrane protein Omp31 and trigger factor chaperone protein (TF) of Brucella melitensis, administered alone or in combination, as safer alternatives to live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: The combination of rOmp31 and rTF provided protection against Brucella melitensis infection comparable to the live attenuated vaccine strain Rev. 1; combination showed a slight but not significant increase in protection compared to rTF alone. Immune response: Immunized mice showed strong antigen-specific antibody responses (IgG1 and IgG2a), robust lymphocyte proliferation, elevated cytokine production (IFN-γ, IL-12, IL-10, IL-6), and increased CD4 and CD8 T cell frequencies; combination vaccine induced slightly higher immune parameters than single antigen vaccines. [Ref7201:Ghasemi et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins rOmp31 and rTF used alone or combined as a cocktail. [Ref7201:Ghasemi et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis Omp19 subunit vaccine in N-trimethyl chitosan nanoparticles
c_description: Recombinant Omp19 protein was loaded onto N-trimethyl chitosan (TMC) nanoparticles by ionic gelation with tripolyphosphate. The vaccine was administered orally and intraperitoneally. Efficacy: Oral immunization with TMC/Omp19 nanoparticles induced a remarkably high protection level against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Immune response: Intraperitoneal immunization induced Th2 immune response; oral immunization induced mixed Th1/Th17 immune response and increased fecal IgA levels. The higher protection level with oral administration may be due to the elicited Th17 response. [Ref7202:Abkar et al, 2015a]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein encapsulated in TMC nanoparticles. [Ref7202:Abkar et al, 2015a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis Omp19 subunit vaccine with Freund's adjuvant
c_description: The omp19 gene was expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) and recombinant Omp19 purified. Omp19 was formulated with Freund's adjuvant for intraperitoneal administration. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization induced Th1 immune response and conferred protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge. Immune response: Induced Th1 immune response. [Ref7202:Abkar et al, 2015a]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein combined with Freund's incomplete adjuvant (IFA). [Ref7202:Abkar et al, 2015a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Ohr subunit vaccine
c_description: The Brucella abortus ohr gene encoding the organic hydroperoxide resistance protein was cloned, expressed as a maltose fusion protein in Escherichia coli, purified, and evaluated for immunogenicity. Efficacy: Immunization with recombinant Ohr protein induced significantly higher protection against virulent Brucella abortus infection compared to control mice immunized with maltose-binding protein. Immune response: The vaccine induced significant increases in IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies, with IgG2a predominating after booster immunizations. It also elicited high production of IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines (TNF, MCP-1, IL-12p70, IL-6) and lower IL-10, indicating a predominantly cell-mediated immune response. [Ref7205:Hop et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant Ohr protein treated with adjuvant and administered intraperitoneally. [Ref7205:Hop et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Lrp/AsnC family protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified six proteins of the Lrp/AsnC family from Brucella melitensis genome, cloned and expressed them in E. coli, and purified the recombinant proteins for immunization. Efficacy: All six Lrp/AsnC proteins induced protective immune responses against Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in mice. Immune response: Induction of antibodies against the Lrp/AsnC proteins was observed in immunized mice; antibody levels in human brucellosis sera were variable. [Ref7206:Wang et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Recombinant individual Lrp/AsnC family proteins expressed in Escherichia coli and purified. [Ref7206:Wang et al, 2015]
c_antigen: Lrp/AsnC family proteins (six individual proteins including BMEI0357)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain BA15 cydC cydD double deletion vaccine
c_description: Constructed from virulent Brucella abortus biovar 1 field isolate (BA15) by deleting genes encoding ATP-binding cassette-type transporter (cydC and cydD). Efficacy: Highly attenuated; cleared from spleens by 4 weeks post-inoculation; no splenomegaly; induced long-term protective immunity; provided significantly better protection than commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. Immune response: Induced humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in mice. [Ref7207:Truong et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live double deletion mutant without adjuvant. [Ref7207:Truong et al, 2016]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; murine macrophages; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain BA15 cydC purD double deletion vaccine
c_description: Constructed from virulent Brucella abortus biovar 1 field isolate (BA15) by deleting genes encoding ATP-binding cassette-type transporter (cydC) and phosphoribosylamine-glycine ligase (purD). Efficacy: Highly attenuated; cleared from spleens by 4 weeks post-inoculation; no splenomegaly; induced long-term protective immunity; provided significantly better protection than commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. Immune response: Induced humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in mice. [Ref7207:Truong et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live double deletion mutant without adjuvant. [Ref7207:Truong et al, 2016]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; murine macrophages; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 99 outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) were derived from Brucella abortus strain 99 using ultracentrifugation. Efficacy: OMVs showed immuno-reactivity with mice antisera and induced specific high-titer immune responses. Immune response: Specific and high-titer immune responses against antigens present in OMVs were observed, suggesting potential as a safe acellular vaccine candidate. [Ref7209:Kaur et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Isolated OMVs characterized as spherical 20-300 nm structures rich in proteins. [Ref7209:Kaur et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus OmpA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the use of Brucella abortus outer membrane protein A (OmpA) as a candidate subunit vaccine in a mouse infection model. Efficacy: Mice treated with recombinant OmpA showed significant protection compared to controls treated with MBP or PBS. Immune response: Immunization induced humoral and host cell-mediated responses, with significant increases in immunoglobulin G (IgG1 and IgG2a) and cytokines TNF-α and IL-12 compared to controls. [Ref7210:Simborio et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Recombinant OmpA protein fused to maltose binding protein (MBP) was cloned, overexpressed, and purified from Escherichia coli. [Ref7210:Simborio et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 L7/L12 recombinant influenza viral vector vaccine
c_description:
This study analyzed the duration of antigen-specific humoral and T-cell immune responses and protectiveness of a recently-developed influenza viral vector Brucella abortus vaccine expressing Omp16 and L7/L12 proteins with Montadine Gel01 adjuvant in cattle. Efficacy: Prime-boost vaccination provided significant protection against B. abortus infection at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-booster; 57.1 to 71.4% of vaccinated animals showed no signs of infection; severity and colonization rates were significantly lower in vaccinated diseased animals; good protection also observed in pregnant heifers, their fetuses, and calves; 71.4% of vaccinated heifers calved successfully versus 100% abortion in controls. Immune response: Both humoral (IgG ELISA titers with IgG2a predominance) and pronounced T-cell responses (lymphocyte stimulation index and IFN-γ production) were induced and maintained up to 12 months post-booster vaccination. [Ref7211:Tabynov et al, 2016]
The Flu-BA vaccine, a novel influenza viral vector based Brucella abortus vaccine, was introduced for use in cattle in Kazakhstan in 2019. Efficacy: Vaccine effectiveness against Brucella abortus 544 infection was 75% in calves, 60% in heifers, and 60% in adult cows; vaccinated animals showed greater protection and no clinical disease including abortion; Brucella were not isolated from calves of vaccinated cattle challenged during pregnancy. Immune response: Vaccinated animals in all age groups demonstrated increased IgG antibody responses against Brucella Omp16 and L7/L12 proteins, with calves showing the greatest increase in humoral responses; no signs of influenza infection or reduced milk production were observed; influenza viral vector was not recovered from nasal swabs or milk. [Ref7347:Ryskeldinova et al, 2021]
c_preparation:
Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus proteins Omp16 and L7/L12 combined with Montadine Gel01 adjuvant. [Ref7211:Tabynov et al, 2016]
Recombinant influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus Omp16 and L7/L12 proteins; no adjuvant reported. [Ref7347:Ryskeldinova et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis delta znuA vaccine
c_description: Nasal vaccination with the ΔznuA B. melitensis strain was used to stimulate immune protection against mucosal Brucella melitensis infection. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced spleen and lung colonization by more than 2500-fold; over 50% of vaccinated mice had no detectable brucellae; complete protection was observed in wild-type and CD4(-/-) mice but not in CD8(-/-) mice. Immune response: Induced 10-fold more Brucella-specific IFN-γ-producing CD8(+) T cells than CD4(+) T cells; CD8(+) T cells showed activated effector memory phenotype producing IFN-γ, TNF-α, perforin, and granzyme B; IFN-γ was critical for protection, IL-17 was induced but could not substitute for IFN-γ. [Ref7212:Clapp et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live attenuated ΔznuA B. melitensis strain administered via nasal route. [Ref7212:Clapp et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus L7/L12 and truncated Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: A new protein vaccine candidate against brucellosis was constructed using bioinformatics tools by designing a fusion protein of Brucella L7/L12 and truncated Omp31 antigens. Efficacy: Not reported; studies evaluating immunogenicity and cross-protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus are underway. Immune response: In silico MHC II epitope mapping indicated the fusion protein contained good MHC II binders suggesting potential immunogenicity; functional expression confirmed by Western blotting. [Ref7213:Golshani et al, 2015b]
c_preparation: The fusion protein L7/L12-TOmp31 coding sequence was cloned into pET28a vector and expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3). The recombinant protein was purified using Ni-NTA column with a yield of 40 mg/L culture. [Ref7213:Golshani et al, 2015b]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 and P39 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant proteins Omp19 and P39 from Brucella abortus, individually and as a cocktail, against B. abortus 544 and B. melitensis 16M infection in a BALB/c mouse model. Efficacy: The rOmp19+rP39 cocktail induced significantly higher protection against B. abortus 544 and B. melitensis 16M infection compared to individual proteins, with log units of protection in spleen and liver significantly greater in the cocktail group. Immune response: The cocktail induced higher antibody titers with Th1 predominant isotypes (IgG2a/2b), significant splenocyte proliferation, and increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-12). Anti-rOmp19+rP39 polysera enhanced macrophage viability against bacterial challenge more effectively than individual protein antisera. [Ref7214:Tadepalli et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins Omp19 and P39 were used individually and combined as a cocktail for intraperitoneal immunization. [Ref7214:Tadepalli et al, 2016]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; RAW 264.7 macrophage cell line

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella hfq deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The hfq gene, encoding a bacterial chaperone protein involved in stress survival and regulation of virulence genes, was deleted to create a mutant strain. Efficacy: The hfq-deletion mutant induced protective immune responses against challenge with wild-type Brucella 16M, demonstrating significant attenuation and protection. Immune response: The hfq-deletion mutant induced different cytokine profiles compared to wild-type 16M infection, suggesting modulation of host immune response and induction of protective immunity. [Ref7215:Lei et al, 2015]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella strain with hfq gene deletion. [Ref7215:Lei et al, 2015]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to analyze the secondary and tertiary structures of Brucella abortus Omp2b protein and predict T-cell and B-cell epitopes using bioinformatics tools to support its potential as a vaccine antigen. Immune response: The Omp2b protein has potential to induce both B-cell- and T-cell-mediated immune responses as predicted by bioinformatics analyses. [Ref7216:Golshani et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Cloning and expression of the short form of Omp2b (SOmp2b) was performed using pET28a expression vector in Escherichia coli BL21, followed by purification of recombinant SOmp2b protein under denaturation conditions using Ni-NTA column. [Ref7216:Golshani et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis delta pgm vaccine
c_description: A novel vaccine strain was constructed by deleting the phosphoglucomutase (pgm) gene, which is involved in polysaccharide biosynthesis. This strain lacks complete lipopolysaccharide, cannot synthesize cyclic beta glucans, and is sensitive to detergents and Polymyxin B. Efficacy: The Delta-pgm strain was completely avirulent in mice and conferred excellent protection against challenge with virulent Brucella suis. Immune response: Vaccination induced the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. [Ref7217:Czibener et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with clean deletion of the pgm gene. [Ref7217:Czibener et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 phosphoglucomutase mutant vaccine
c_description: A Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 pgm mutant (M5-90Δpgm) was constructed to overcome drawbacks of residual virulence and serological differentiation issues of existing live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: M5-90Δpgm showed significantly reduced survival in cells and mice and induced high protective immunity in BALB/c mice against wild-type challenge. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response; secretion of gamma interferon (IFN-γ) and interleukin-2 (IL-2) in mice; IFN-γ secretion in immunized sheep; allowed serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals. [Ref7219:Zhang et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of phosphoglucomutase gene. [Ref7219:Zhang et al, 2016]
c_model_host: BALB/c mice; embryonic trophoblast cells; sheep

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain IVK15 delta cydC vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked mutant by deleting cydC gene encoding ATP-binding cassette transporter protein from virulent Brucella abortus isolate IVK15 from Korean cow. Efficacy: Provided better protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 than commercial B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine in mice. Immune response: Elicited anti-Brucella specific IgG and IgG subclass responses; enhanced interferon-gamma secretion. [Ref7221:Truong et al, 2016a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain IVK15ΔcydC. [Ref7221:Truong et al, 2016a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain IVK15 delta cydD vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked mutant by deleting cydD gene encoding ATP-binding cassette transporter protein from virulent Brucella abortus isolate IVK15 from Korean cow. Efficacy: Provided better protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 than commercial B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine in mice. Immune response: Elicited anti-Brucella specific IgG and IgG subclass responses; enhanced interferon-gamma secretion. [Ref7221:Truong et al, 2016a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain IVK15ΔcydD. [Ref7221:Truong et al, 2016a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope recombinant protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Live attenuated Brucella vaccines are effective but have safety concerns; subunit vaccines are safer alternatives. This study used bioinformatics to predict B and T cell epitopes to develop a novel recombinant multi-epitope antigen for brucellosis vaccination. Efficacy: The recombinant antigen provided protection against Brucella melitensis 16 M infection comparable to vaccine strain M5-90. Immune response: Immunized mice showed mixed Th1-Th2 responses with high levels of specific IgG, increased IFN-γ and IL-6, and significantly higher frequencies of CD3, CD4, and CD8 T cells compared to controls. [Ref7222:Yin et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Recombinant multi-epitope protein antigen [Ref7222:Yin et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Live, attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vaccine candidate expressing BCSP31, Omp3b, and SOD proteins of Brucella abortus
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
A live, attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vaccine candidate was constructed to express BCSP31, Omp3b, and SOD proteins of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with the vaccine candidate significantly reduced Brucella abortus strain 544 colonization in spleen (<10^3 CFU), indicating effective protection. Immune response: Significant increases in serum IgG, TNF-α, and IFN-γ concentrations were observed in immunized groups compared to control, except for Omp3b in oral immunization group. [Ref7223:Kim et al, 2016]
Attenuated Salmonella strains expressing Brucella abortus BCSP31, Omp3b, and superoxide dismutase proteins were developed as vaccine candidates to protect against brucellosis. Efficacy: The highest dose group (1.2 × 10^6 CFU/mL) showed significantly increased immune responses and complete clearance of challenge strain from spleen, indicating effective protection. Immune response: Significantly higher serum IgG, tumor necrosis factor alpha, and interferon gamma concentrations were observed in the highest dose group compared to lower doses and control. [Ref7241:Kim et al, 2017]
This study aimed to establish proof-of-concept for protective efficacy of a Salmonella-based Brucella abortus vaccine candidate in Beagles. Efficacy: Following challenge, the vaccine reduced bacterial isolation from multiple lymph nodes and organs compared to vector control; some vaccinated Beagles showed no bacterial isolates in tested tissues, indicating partial protection. Immune response: Vaccinated Beagles showed significantly higher serum IgG, interleukin-4, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and interferon-gamma concentrations compared to controls, indicating enhanced humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7264:Kim et al, 2018]
c_preparation:
Mixture of three delivery strains of live, attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium expressing the three Brucella abortus proteins. [Ref7223:Kim et al, 2016]
A mixture of three recombinant Salmonella strains expressing the three Brucella abortus proteins was prepared at various doses for intraperitoneal immunization. [Ref7241:Kim et al, 2017]
A mixture of three live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium delivery strains, each expressing one of the recombinant Brucella abortus proteins BCSP31, Omp3b, or superoxide dismutase (SOD), was used for subcutaneous vaccination. [Ref7264:Kim et al, 2018]
c_antigen: BCSP31; Omp3b; SOD | BCSP31; Omp3b; superoxide dismutase
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); Canis lupus familiaris (Beagles)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus ghost vaccine lysed by GI24 vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus cells were lysed by the N-terminal 24-amino acid fragment (GI24) of PMAP-36 to create a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with the vaccine candidate provided significant protection against systemic infection with virulent B. abortus 544. Immune response: Increased Brucella LPS-specific serum IgG titers and elevated levels of IL-4, IL-10, TNF-α, and IFN-γ cytokines were observed in vaccinated groups compared to controls. [Ref7224:Kwon et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Vaccine candidate prepared by lysing B. abortus cells with GI24 peptide fragment. [Ref7224:Kwon et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus delta rpoE1 vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a Brucella abortus strain lacking the alternative sigma factor σ(E1) (ΔrpoE1), which is part of the general stress response system and required for persistence in mice. Efficacy: Mice immunized with ΔrpoE1 completely resisted wild-type infection and showed reduced splenomegaly and bacterial burden compared to wild-type infected mice. Immune response: Immunization elicited significantly higher Brucella-specific serum IgG, IgG2a, and IFN-γ levels compared to naïve mice, indicating a strong adaptive immune response correlating with protection. [Ref7225:Willett et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus ΔrpoE1 mutant strain without adjuvant. [Ref7225:Willett et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus delta norD delta znuA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine znBAZ was developed by deleting norD and znuA genes from Brucella abortus and inserting lacZ as a marker gene to create a highly attenuated strain. Efficacy: znBAZ was significantly more protective than the conventional RB51 vaccine by more than four orders of magnitude and was completely cleared from mouse spleens within eight weeks post-vaccination. Immune response: Vaccination with znBAZ elicited elevated numbers of IFN-γ+, TNF-α+, and polyfunctional IFN-γ+ TNF-α+ CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, indicating a diverse and potent T cell-mediated immune response compared to RB51-vaccinated mice which showed reduced proinflammatory cytokine-producing T cells. [Ref7226:Yang et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletions in norD and znuA genes and lacZ marker. [Ref7226:Yang et al, 2016]
c_antigen: norD deletion; znuA deletion; lacZ marker gene

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 Omp cationic liposome subunit vaccine (S19-OMP-liposome)
c_description: The study evaluated a vaccine formulation consisting of outer membrane protein from Brucella abortus strain S19 entrapped in a commercial cationic liposome used as an adjuvant and delivery system. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the S19-OMP-liposome showed enhanced protection compared to mice inoculated with S19 OMP alone, live B. abortus S19 vaccine, or liposome alone (P<0.05); the S19-OMP-liposome was safer than the live vaccine as indicated by spleen weight differences (P<0.01). Immune response: The immune response was Th1 cell mediated, with significantly higher IgG2a, IgG2b, and IgG3 antibody isotypes in the S19-OMP-liposome group compared to other groups at 30 days post-immunization and post-challenge (P<0.01 and P<0.05). [Ref7227:Mukherjee et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Outer membrane protein of Brucella abortus strain S19 entrapped in a commercial cationic liposome. [Ref7227:Mukherjee et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0267 DNA vaccine
c_description: Immunization with the recombinant plasmid based on BAB1_0267 ORF was evaluated for immunogenicity. Efficacy: Did not provide significant levels of protection against Brucella abortus 2308 infection. Immune response: Significantly increased IgG1 production, IFN-γ levels, and lymphoproliferative response indicating immune activation but no protective efficacy. [Ref7228:Gómez et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid DNA encoding BAB1_0267 ORF. [Ref7228:Gómez et al, 2016]
c_antigen: BAB1_0267 open reading frame (protein with SH3 domain)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0270 DNA vaccine
c_description: Immunization with the recombinant plasmid based on BAB1_0270 ORF was evaluated for immunogenicity and protection. Efficacy: Induced heightened resistance to Brucella abortus 2308 infection in mice. Immune response: Significantly increased IgG2a production, IFN-γ and TNF-α levels, and lymphoproliferative response indicating a Th1-type immune response correlated with protection. [Ref7228:Gómez et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid DNA encoding BAB1_0270 ORF. [Ref7228:Gómez et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study involved molecular cloning and expression analysis of the Omp25 gene from Iranian Brucella melitensis to design a subunit vaccine candidate. Immune response: The Omp25 gene is proposed as a candidate useful for stimulation of cell-mediated and humoral immunity in future studies. [Ref7229:Yousefi et al, 2016]
c_preparation: The Omp25 gene was amplified, cloned into pTZ57R/T vector, and expressed using pET32(a)+ vector in E. coli BL21 (DE3) strain, producing a 42 kDa protein. [Ref7229:Yousefi et al, 2016]
c_model_host: Escherichia coli (TOP10F and BL21 DE3 strains)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Flu-BA influenza vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Previously developed and evaluated in cattle; this study aimed to establish proof-of-concept efficacy in sheep and goats. Efficacy: Complete protection in 57.1% of sheep and 42.9% of goats against B. melitensis 16M challenge; significantly lower infection index and tissue colonization compared to negative controls. Immune response: No antibody response against Brucella Omp16 and L7/L12 proteins detected up to 56 days post-initial vaccination; significant antigen-specific T cell response indicated by increased lymphocyte stimulation index and enhanced IFN-γ secretion at day 56 post-vaccination. [Ref7231:Tabynov et al, 2016b]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector based Brucella abortus vaccine administered with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant. [Ref7231:Tabynov et al, 2016b]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunogenicity and protective efficacy of Brucella outer membrane protein 2b (Omp2b) using three immunization strategies: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: DNA/protein regimen conferred higher protection levels against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge compared to protein or DNA alone. Immune response: All regimens elicited strong specific IgG response with higher IgG2a over IgG1 titers indicating Th1-oriented immune response; DNA/protein regimen induced higher IFN-γ and IL-2 levels. [Ref7232:Golshani et al, 2016a]
c_preparation: Three vaccine regimens: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein using Omp2b antigen. [Ref7232:Golshani et al, 2016a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunogenicity and protective efficacy of Brucella outer membrane protein 2b (Omp2b) using three immunization strategies: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: DNA/protein regimen conferred higher protection levels against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge compared to protein or DNA alone. Immune response: All regimens elicited strong specific IgG response with higher IgG2a over IgG1 titers indicating Th1-oriented immune response; DNA/protein regimen induced higher IFN-γ and IL-2 levels. [Ref7232:Golshani et al, 2016a]
c_preparation: Three vaccine regimens: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein using Omp2b antigen. [Ref7232:Golshani et al, 2016a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus culture filtrate antigen subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine consisted of Brucella abortus culture filtrate antigen administered intraperitoneally in two doses at two-week intervals with a protein concentration of 2 mg/ml. Efficacy: The vaccine induced significant humoral and cellular immune responses as shown by increased skin thickness, higher IFN-γ levels, elevated antibody titers, and increased phagocytic ratio in immunized mice. Immune response: The vaccine elicited strong cellular immunity (delayed type hypersensitivity and IFN-γ production) and humoral immunity (antibody production), as well as enhanced phagocytic activity. [Ref7233:Salema et al, 2016]
c_preparation: Culture filtrate antigen of Brucella abortus without adjuvant. [Ref7233:Salema et al, 2016]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta NodV delta NodW vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a double deletion mutant of virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308, deleting the NodV and NodW genes encoding a two-component regulatory system on chromosome II, constructed to reduce virulence and allow serological differentiation from infected animals. Efficacy: The mutant showed significantly reduced survival in macrophages and mice, no splenomegaly in inoculated mice, and conferred high protective immunity against challenge with wild-type strain 2308 in BALB/c mice. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG antibody response; stimulated secretion of gamma interferon (IFN-γ) and interleukin-4 (IL-4), indicating activation of both Th1 and Th2 immune responses. [Ref7234:Li et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain 2308 with deletions in NodV and NodW genes; no adjuvant reported. [Ref7234:Li et al, 2017]
c_antigen: NodV and NodW (two-component regulatory system genes deleted)
c_model_host: Mus musculus; RAW 264.7 murine macrophages; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis BLSOmp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 is an immunogenic vaccine candidate that confers protection against Brucella canis in mice. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of BLSOmp31 adsorbed to aluminum hydroxide gel in Beagle dogs. Efficacy: The vaccine elicited specific antibodies 3 weeks after the first immunization; annual booster induced comparable antibody responses. Antibodies showed high complement-dependent bactericidal activity against B. canis and enhanced bacterial uptake and destruction by neutrophils. Specific IgG was detected in preputial secretions of most immunized dogs. Humoral response did not interfere with routine agglutination tests. Immune response: The antibody profile corresponded to a marked Th2 response with predominance of IgG1 over IgG2. Cellular immune response was not detected in vitro or in vivo. [Ref7235:Clausse et al, 2017]
c_preparation: BLSOmp31 antigen adsorbed to aluminum hydroxide gel (BLSOmp31-AH). [Ref7235:Clausse et al, 2017]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; Canis lupus familiaris (Beagle dogs)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella A antigen hexasaccharide and heptasaccharide conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study hypothesized that a chemically synthesized pure A antigen vaccine would allow differentiation of infected animals from vaccinated ones by using a synthetic M diagnostic antigen that does not react with antibodies generated by the vaccine. Immune response: The vaccine candidates induced anti-A antibodies that bind internal oligosaccharide sequences while minimizing antibodies directed toward the terminal nonreducing monosaccharide, thus avoiding reaction with the diagnostic M antigen. This focused antibody response addresses the challenge of creating effective brucellosis vaccines without compromising diagnosis. [Ref7236:Mandal et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Two forms of the A antigen (hexasaccharide and heptasaccharide) were chemically synthesized and conjugated to tetanus toxoid via reducing and nonreducing terminal sugars. Conjugation via the periodate oxidized terminal nonreducing monosaccharide was used to destroy terminal epitopes and focus the antibody response on internal A epitopes. [Ref7236:Mandal et al, 2017]
c_antigen: A antigen hexasaccharide; A antigen heptasaccharide

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain RM57 vaccine
c_description: A rough mutant RM57 was artificially induced from a Brucella melitensis isolate M1981 to overcome disadvantages of traditional live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: RM57 was attenuated and conferred good protection against virulent Brucella melitensis challenge, especially in the guinea pig model. [Ref7237:Feng et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Rough mutant strain RM57 with altered LPS; no significant change in LPS gene expression but increased sensitivity to polymyxin B indicating altered outer membrane integrity. [Ref7237:Feng et al, 2017]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope peptide vaccine was designed in silico targeting five immunogenic Brucella antigens (Omp31, BP26, BLS, DnaK, L7-L12) fused with helper epitopes from Tetanus toxin fragment C to induce CD4+ helper T cell responses. Efficacy: Predicted to strongly induce T cell and B cell mediated immune responses based on immunoinformatics analysis. Immune response: Designed to elicit robust T cell responses including CD4+ helper T lymphocytes and B cell mediated immunity. [Ref7238:Saadi et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Selected epitopes were linked by GPGPG linkers; cholera toxin B was linked to the N-terminal as an adjuvant using an EAAAK linker; the final construct was a 377 amino acid chimeric protein predicted to be soluble, stable, non-allergenic, and 40.59 kDa in size. [Ref7238:Saadi et al, 2017]
c_antigen: Omp31, BP26, BLS, DnaK, L7-L12, Tetanus toxin fragment C (TTFrC)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella BLS PrpA Omp19 SodC Salmonella vector vaccine with Brucella lipopolysaccharide adjuvant
c_description: A combination of four attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium live vector strains delivering heterologous Brucella antigens was developed to create a cross-protecting vaccine against multispecies brucellosis. Efficacy: Significant reduction of splenic Brucella abortus 544 colonization compared to non-immunized and Salmonella-only immunized mice; rough Salmonella variant with LPS enhanced delivery efficacy. Immune response: Increased Brucella-specific IgG and sIgA production; antigen-specific splenocyte proliferation; modulation of IL-4, IL-12, and interferon-γ production in splenocytes. [Ref7239:Lalsiamthara et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Formulations included smooth and rough variants of Salmonella delivery vectors, with or without purified Brucella lipopolysaccharide (LPS); rough Salmonella variant combined with LPS was administered intraperitoneally. [Ref7239:Lalsiamthara et al, 2017]
c_antigen: lumazine synthase; proline racemase subunit A; lipoprotein outer membrane protein-19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella rough strain vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the safety of the rough strain vaccine against brucellosis in pregnant cattle, addressing the lack of prophylactic strategies for pregnant heifers and cows in many countries. Efficacy: Vaccination with the rough strain had no adverse effect on pregnancy outcomes or calf viability at any gestational period. [Ref7240:Barbosa et al, 2017]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant DNA vaccine (pVGntR)
c_description: The recombinant DNA vaccine pVGntR was constructed based on the transcriptional regulator GntR of Brucella abortus to improve protective immunity and reduce residual virulence compared to conventional vaccines. Efficacy: pVGntR provided significantly greater protection than the conventional RB51 vaccine against wild-type Brucella abortus challenge. Immune response: Immunization with pVGntR increased immunoglobulin G (IgG) production and elevated gamma interferon (IFN-γ) and interleukin-4 (IL-4) levels, indicating enhanced humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7242:Li et al, 2017a]
c_preparation: Recombinant DNA plasmid vaccine encoding GntR [Ref7242:Li et al, 2017a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 manB mutant vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate M5-90ΔmanB was generated to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines such as residual virulence and inability to differentiate infection from vaccination. Efficacy: M5-90ΔmanB showed significantly reduced survival in macrophages and mice and conferred strong protective immunity against virulent Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in BALB/c mice. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG1 and IgG2a responses; secretion of IFN-γ and IL-4 in mice; IFN-γ secretion in goats; goats inoculated with M5-90ΔmanB were seronegative by RBPT and STAT, allowing differentiation from natural infection. [Ref7243:Zhang et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis M5-90 strain with manB gene deletion. [Ref7243:Zhang et al, 2017]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide core mutant vaccine
c_description: The study characterizes the immunomodulatory effects of Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and a modified LPS with a defective core from a wadC gene mutant strain, highlighting the potential of the wadC mutation for vaccine development targeting the Brucella core LPS structure. Efficacy: The wadC mutant LPS (Bm-wadC) efficiently potentiated mouse and human dendritic cell activation and T cell proliferation in vitro and induced high cytokine secretion in vivo, whereas wild-type LPS (Bm-wt) induced limited dendritic cell activation and cytokine response. Immune response: Bm-wt LPS selectively induced surface activation markers and cytokine secretion from Flt3-Ligand-derived dendritic cells in a TLR4-dependent manner and primed T cell proliferation in vitro; Bm-wadC LPS enhanced dendritic cell activation and T cell proliferation and promoted strong cytokine secretion in vivo. [Ref7244:Zhao et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 L7/L12 Omp19 SOD recombinant influenza viral vector vaccine
c_description:
The Flu-BA vaccine was improved by adding two additional proteins (Omp19 and SOD) and modifying the immunization method to maximize efficacy and safety. Efficacy: Prevented abortion in 66.7% of pregnant sheep and 77.8% of pregnant goats; complete protection (absence of live B. melitensis 16M) in 55.6% of sheep and 66.7% of goats; protection of fetuses in 72.7% of lambs and 90.0% of yeanlings; significantly reduced infection severity and colonization compared to controls; protection parameters comparable to commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. Immune response: Induced antigen-specific IgG antibodies predominantly of IgG2a isotype and also IgG1; strong lymphocyte recall response with IFN-γ production detected at 42 days post-vaccination. [Ref7245:Mailybayeva et al, 2017]
The study evaluated an improved commercial Brucella abortus vaccine based on influenza viral vectors expressing Brucella immunodominant proteins, with improved formulation and route of administration. Efficacy: Protection levels against B. melitensis 16M infection were 0-20% in sheep and 20-40% in goats over 6 months; infection severity and Brucella colonization significantly reduced in vaccinated animals compared to controls. Immune response: Induced antigen-specific Th1-biased antibody response (IgG2a over IgG1), T-cell and interferon γ responses lasting over 1 month post-last vaccination. [Ref7310:Mailybayeva et al, 2020]
c_adjuvant: yes; Montanide Gel01 | yes; 20% Montanide Gel01
c_preparation:
Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus proteins Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, and SOD; administered thrice at 21-day intervals with 20% Montanide Gel01 adjuvant via simultaneous subcutaneous and conjunctival routes. [Ref7245:Mailybayeva et al, 2017]
Vaccine administered thrice concurrently via subcutaneous and conjunctival routes at 21-day intervals; control group received 20% Montanide Gel01 adjuvant in phosphate-buffered saline. [Ref7310:Mailybayeva et al, 2020]
c_antigen: Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; SOD | Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta gntR vaccine
c_description: The 2308ΔgntR mutant is a Brucella abortus strain 2308 with deletion of the transcriptional regulator gene gntR, which down regulates expression of virulence-related genes and attenuates virulence. Efficacy: The 2308ΔgntR mutant induced high protective immunity in BALB/c mice challenged with wild-type B. abortus 2308. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G (IgG) response; stimulated secretion of gamma interferon (IFN-γ) and interleukin-4 (IL-4). [Ref7246:Li et al, 2017b]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with gntR gene deletion; no adjuvant reported. [Ref7246:Li et al, 2017b]
c_antigen: gntR deletion; regulated genes include omp25, virB1, vjbR, dnaK, htrA, hfq

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0273 BAB1_0278 SodC DNA vaccine
c_description: New multivalent DNA vaccines were constructed by fusion of BAB1_0273 and/or BAB1_0278 ORFs from genomic island 3 and the Brucella abortus 2308 sodC gene linked by prolines and alanines. Efficacy: Vaccines conferred low levels of protection against challenge with B. abortus 2308. Immune response: Immunization induced specific humoral and cellular immune responses, significantly increasing IgM, IgG, IgG2a antibodies, IFN-γ levels, and lymphoproliferative response of splenocytes, indicating a Th1-dominated immune response. [Ref7247:Gómez et al, 2017]
c_preparation: Fusion DNA vaccines encoding BAB1_0273 and/or BAB1_0278 antigens conjugated to sodC protein. [Ref7247:Gómez et al, 2017]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19-P39 chimeric rOP subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant chimeric protein consisting of Omp19 and P39 domains of Brucella abortus was expressed in E. coli, purified under denaturing conditions, and refolded to a dynamic form for immunization. Efficacy: Vaccination with rOP reduced bacterial CFU significantly (P<0.01) in macrophage cell lines and organs of mice after challenge with virulent Brucella species; rOP with Freund's adjuvants showed higher and faster bacterial reduction; anti-rOP antisera and antisera from rOP+adjuvant groups enhanced protection of macrophages against Brucella challenge. Immune response: rOP alone induced strong IgG response dominated by IgG2a and significant IFN-γ production by splenic T cells; rOP+FCA/IFA induced significant lymphocyte proliferation and increased Th1 cytokines IFN-γ, IL-2, and IL-12p70; antibodies recognized native Omp19 and P39 proteins; Th1-directed immune protection was observed even without adjuvant. [Ref7248:Tadepalli et al, 2017]
c_preparation: rOP alone or formulated with adjuvants Aluminum hydroxide gel, Freund's Complete Adjuvant, or Incomplete Freund's Adjuvant. [Ref7248:Tadepalli et al, 2017]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); RAW264.7 cells (macrophage cell line)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis GroEL OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the impact of GroEL in combination with recombinant outer membrane proteins OMP25 and OMP31 emulsified in chitosan nanoparticles to enhance immune responses against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Univalent vaccines (except rGroEL alone) and divalent combinations induced higher IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-4 compared to controls; individual OMP25 or OMP31 immunization showed more effective cell-mediated immunity; some rGroEL and rOMP31 combinations were more efficient than other divalent vaccines. Immune response: Induction of higher Th1-type immune response indicated by elevated IgG2a over IgG1; increased IFN-γ and lymphocyte proliferation; GroEL alone had a negative effect on TNF-α but positive trends on IFN-γ in some treatments. [Ref7249:Abbassi-Daloii et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Recombinant GroEL, OMP25, and OMP31 proteins emulsified in chitosan nanoparticles; tested as univalent and divalent formulations with different concentrations. [Ref7249:Abbassi-Daloii et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella A antigen conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study introduces a polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccine based on synthetic oligosaccharides derived from Brucella O-polysaccharide (OPS) that aims to avoid false positive serodiagnostic results caused by current vaccines. Efficacy: Immunized mice developed antibodies to the Brucella A antigen that did not react in diagnostic tests based on the M antigen, indicating potential for improved vaccine specificity. Immune response: Antibody response specific to the Brucella A antigen was elicited without generating antibodies that cause false positives in serodiagnostic tests targeting the M antigen. [Ref7250:Bundle et al, 2017]
c_preparation: A chemically synthesized polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccine targeting the Brucella A antigen, designed to not induce antibodies reactive in diagnostic tests based on the M antigen. [Ref7250:Bundle et al, 2017]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus SodC Omp19 BLS PrpA Salmonella vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: An attenuated live Salmonella Typhimurium vector delivering heterologous Brucella immunogenic proteins SOD, Omp19, BLS, and PrpA formulated with purified Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide was developed to generate a safe and effective anti-Brucella vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccinated guinea pigs showed a protective index of 1.52 based on differential splenic bacterial counts and reduced histopathological lesions compared to non-immunized controls. [Ref7251:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella proteins SOD, Omp19, BLS, and PrpA combined with purified Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide. [Ref7251:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PrpA recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector constitutively expressing heterologous Brucella abortus PrpA protein was used to investigate safety, humoral and cellular immunity, and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significantly quicker anti-Salmonella IgG responses and increased protection against Salmonella challenge compared to Salmonella vector only. Immune response: Increased IL-4 production in vitro from pulsed mice splenocytes indicating enhanced humoral immunity without major interference on cell mediated immunity. [Ref7253:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella abortus PrpA protein (ST-PrpA) [Ref7253:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella vaccine using rough Salmonella vector
c_description: An anti-Brucella vaccine candidate was developed using a rough Salmonella vector delivering Brucella antigens to mimic active intracellular Brucella infection, aiming to provide significant protection with a single dose and improved safety. Immune response: In vitro, the vaccine induced significantly lower levels of inflammatory and pyretic cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β compared to wild-type Salmonella; apoptosis, nitric oxide synthase, and cytotoxicity were comparable and not exacerbated, indicating mild induction of inflammatory cytokines and cellular changes. [Ref7254:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018b]
c_preparation: Live rough Salmonella bacterial vector delivering Brucella antigens; administered orally or subcutaneously. [Ref7254:Lalsiamthara et al, 2018b]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; THP-1 derived macrophage; Caco-2; human PBMC

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 and lumazine synthase adenovirus vector vaccine
c_description: A recombinant adenovirus vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins of Brucella abortus was constructed and evaluated. Efficacy: Single adenovirus immunization was less effective than DNA prime followed by adenovirus boost in reducing bacterial load. Immune response: Induced immune responses but less robust compared to DNA prime/adenovirus boost strategy. [Ref7255:Lin et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Recombinant adenovirus vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins. [Ref7255:Lin et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 and lumazine synthase DNA vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins of Brucella abortus was constructed and evaluated. Efficacy: Single DNA immunization was less effective than DNA prime followed by adenovirus boost in reducing bacterial load. Immune response: Induced immune responses but less robust compared to DNA prime/adenovirus boost strategy. [Ref7255:Lin et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins. [Ref7255:Lin et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 SOmp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study designed a fusion protein combining L7/L12 and SOmp2b antigens, both conserved and immunogenic in Brucella pathogens, as a potential vaccine candidate. Immune response: The fusion protein contains good MHC-II binders indicating potential to induce both B- and T-cell-mediated immune responses. [Ref7256:Golshani et al, 2018]
c_preparation: The fusion protein L7/L12-SOmp2b was cloned into pET28a vector and expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3), then purified using Ni-NTA column. [Ref7256:Golshani et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus Urease subunit vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the vaccine potential of urease antigen formulated in trimethyl chitosan (TMC) nanoparticles against brucellosis. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with TMC/Urease nanoparticles induced high specific IgG levels and resulted in a high degree of protection against virulent B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge. Immune response: Intraperitoneal TMC/Urease vaccination induced a mixed Th1-Th2 immune response with strong recall lymphocyte proliferation; oral administration induced a mixed Th1-Th17 response; urease alone induced lower IgG titers and less protection. [Ref7257:Abkar et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Urease antigen was loaded into TMC nanoparticles to create a nanoparticle formulation (TMC/Urease). [Ref7257:Abkar et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25c subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to examine the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of Omp25c, a conserved porin protein paralogous to Omp25 and Omp31, as a vaccine candidate against Brucella infections. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed protection against Brucella abortus challenge comparable to the S19 vaccine strain. Immune response: Immunization induced high IgG antibody titers with a Th2-based humoral response (IgG2a/IgG2b ratio), specific memory lymphocyte proliferation, secretion of Th1-type cytokines (IFN-γ, GM-CSF, TNF-α) and Th2-type cytokine (IL-5), and an increased CD4 T-cell subpopulation indicating a strong Th1 biased cell-mediated immunity alongside Th2 humoral immunity. [Ref7259:Paul et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Recombinant unlipidated Omp25c protein (rOmp25c) was produced and administered intraperitoneally in BALB/c mice along with Freund's adjuvant. [Ref7259:Paul et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus AspC Dps InpB Ndk subunit vaccine
c_description: The study assessed the protective efficacy of single subunit vaccines encoded by B. abortus genes aspC, dps, yaeC, and inpB, and further investigated a combined subunit vaccine consisting of purified AspC, Dps, InpB, and Ndk proteins. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccine showed superior protective effect in mice against brucellosis compared to single antigens and was comparable to the live attenuated vaccine RB51. Immune response: The vaccine induced a T-helper-1-dominated immune response characterized by dominant IgG2a over IgG1, massive production of IFN-γ and IL-2, increased blood CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proportions, and lower IL-10 production. [Ref7260:Hop et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Intraperitoneal injection of a combination of purified recombinant proteins AspC, Dps, InpB, and Ndk. [Ref7260:Hop et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: single subunit vaccines encoded by aspC, dps, yaeC, and inpB genes
c_description: Single subunit vaccines encoded by B. abortus genes aspC, dps, yaeC, and inpB were assessed for protective efficacy. Efficacy: Single antigens (except YaeC) elicited immune responses but had lower protection compared to the combined vaccine. Immune response: Immunization with AspC, Dps, and InpB elicited both humoral and cellular immune responses with dominant IgG2a over IgG1 and massive IFN-γ production with lower IL-10, indicating cell-mediated immunity. YaeC did not elicit similar responses. [Ref7260:Hop et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Immunization with individual recombinant proteins. [Ref7260:Hop et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus wbdR-inserted vaccine
c_description: The study introduced the wbdR acetyl-transferase gene from Escherichia coli O157:H7 into Brucella abortus chromosome II, generating a modified O-polysaccharide antigenic structure with N-acetyl-perosamine replacing N-formyl-perosamine. Efficacy: The wbdR constructs produced chronic infections in mice and elicited antibody responses distinguishable from wild-type strains, indicating potential for vaccine development. Immune response: The modified vaccines triggered antibodies to new immunogenic epitopes lacking the A, M, and C epitopes of wild-type strains, allowing differentiation in serological tests. [Ref7261:Martínez-Gómez et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus constructs with chromosomal insertion of wbdR gene, some with deletion of the native wbkC formyltransferase gene, producing modified lipopolysaccharide structures. [Ref7261:Martínez-Gómez et al, 2018]
c_antigen: wbdR acetyl-transferase gene; deletion of wbkC formyltransferase gene

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis vaccine with wbdR acetyl-transferase gene insertion
c_description: The wbdR acetyl-transferase gene was inserted into Brucella melitensis chromosome II, modifying the O-polysaccharide antigenic structure to include N-acetyl-perosamine and removing native epitopes. Efficacy: The modified strains caused chronic infections in mice and induced antibody responses that differ from wild-type, suggesting potential as tagged vaccines. Immune response: Antibodies were generated against new epitopes lacking the M and C epitopes, enabling serological differentiation from wild-type infections. [Ref7261:Martínez-Gómez et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Live Brucella melitensis constructs with chromosomal wbdR gene insertion and wbkC gene deletion, producing altered lipopolysaccharide antigens. [Ref7261:Martínez-Gómez et al, 2018]
c_antigen: wbdR acetyl-transferase gene; deletion of wbkC formyltransferase gene

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus BLS PrpA Omp19 SodC Salmonella Typhimurium vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study explores the efficacy of a Salmonella Typhimurium delivery-based combination vaccine expressing four heterologous Brucella antigens targeting brucellosis in goats. Efficacy: Immunized goats showed significantly higher protection demonstrated by lower bacterial loads in most tissues, reduced expression of Brucella antigens in spleen, kidney, and lung, and ameliorated histopathological lesions compared to non-immunized controls. Immune response: Significantly higher serum IgG titers against individual Brucella antigens and elevated interferon-γ production from peripheral blood mononuclear cells in vaccinated groups compared to non-immunized goats. [Ref7262:Leya et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS), proline racemase subunit A (PrpA), outer-membrane protein 19 (Omp19), and Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); administered subcutaneously at two inoculation levels (5 × 10^9 CFU/mL and 5 × 10^10 CFU/mL). [Ref7262:Leya et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy of a divalent fusion protein comprising L7/L12 and Omp25 antigens of Brucella abortus in the presence of murine IFN-gamma. Efficacy: The vaccine candidate alone provided significant protection (log protection unit 2.16, p=0.0001) against B. abortus 544; co-administration with IFN-gamma enhanced protection (log protection unit 2.4, p=0.0001). Minimal or no therapeutic effect was observed when administered with IFN-gamma post-infection. Immune response: Immunization induced dominance of IgG1 over IgG2a and upregulated cytokines IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha, and IL-10. Combination with IFN-gamma elicited stronger cell-mediated immune responses compared to the standard S19 vaccine. [Ref7265:Paul et al, 2018a]
c_preparation: A recombinant fusion protein of L7/L12 and Omp25 was used alone or in combination with recombinant murine IFN-gamma. [Ref7265:Paul et al, 2018a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis conjunctival vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was administered as a single dose conjunctival vaccination against Brucella melitensis in sheep. Efficacy: Antibody titers increased significantly at the first month post-vaccination (p < 0.001) but began to decline by the second month; the vaccine was considered safe and effective for protecting sheep from brucellosis. Immune response: Significant increase in antibody titers at one month post-vaccination; biochemical parameters showed no significant changes in glucose, AST, ALT; total protein and ALP decreased significantly; LDH and total protein levels increased significantly after vaccination. [Ref7266:Çiftci et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 vjbR deletion vaccine
c_description: The M5-90ΔvjbR mutant was constructed from the Brucella melitensis M5-90 vaccine strain to overcome safety issues and enable differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals. Efficacy: M5-90ΔvjbR showed reduced survival in macrophages and mice, induced high protective immunity in mice, and stimulated specific IgG responses and cytokine production in both mice and sheep. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG, stimulated gamma interferon (IFN-γ) and interleukin-4 (IL-4) expression in vaccinated mice and sheep; VjbR antigen enabled serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals. [Ref7267:Li et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis M5-90 strain with vjbR gene deletion. [Ref7267:Li et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to construct a DNA vaccine encoding the antigenic surface protein BCSP31 of Brucella abortus to control brucellosis, a highly contagious zoonotic disease with high prevalence in Pakistan. Efficacy: The vaccinated groups showed significantly higher IgG titers in a dose-dependent manner compared to control. The DNA vaccine provided a log unit protection of 3.02 against Brucella abortus challenge in rabbits. Immune response: The vaccine induced a significant specific IgG antibody response against BCSP31 antigen in vaccinated rabbits, indicating immunogenicity and potential protective immunity. [Ref7268:Imtiaz et al, 2018]
c_preparation: The BCSP31 gene was cloned into pTZ57 R/T vector, subcloned into pET-28a vector, expressed in E. coli BL21, and the purified protein was used for immunization. [Ref7268:Imtiaz et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella cocktail protein vaccine (rL7/L12+rTOmp31+rSOmp2b)
c_description: A cocktail protein vaccine composed of recombinant Brucella L7/L12 ribosomal protein, truncated outer membrane protein 31 (TOmp31), and SOmp2b was formulated with two different adjuvants to evaluate protective efficacy. Efficacy: Both vaccine regimens conferred protection levels comparable to live vaccines against Brucella challenge; the formulation with CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70VG induced higher protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus than the Poly (I:C) formulation. Immune response: Both vaccine regimens elicited strong specific IgG responses with higher IgG2a than IgG1 titers, indicating a Th1-oriented immune response; the CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70VG formulation induced higher antibody levels and IFN-γ/IL-2 production. [Ref7269:Golshani et al, 2018a]
c_adjuvant: yes; CpG ODN 1826 + Montanide ISA 70VG or Poly (I:C)
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated with either CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70VG adjuvants or Poly (I:C) adjuvant. [Ref7269:Golshani et al, 2018a]
c_antigen: L7/L12 ribosomal protein; truncated outer membrane protein 31 (TOmp31); SOmp2b recombinant protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 and Omp31 DNA vaccine
c_description: DNA vaccine encoding both Omp25 and Omp31 genes was constructed in the eukaryotic expression vector pcDNA3.1/Hygro (+) and confirmed by SDS-PAGE and Western blot. Efficacy: Induced significant immunoglobulin G response, T-cell proliferation, and interferon gamma production compared to controls. Immune response: Both humoral and cellular immunity were induced, with dominant IgG response and significant INF-γ production. [Ref7270:Shojaei et al, 2018]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pcDNA3.1/Hygro (+) encoding both Omp25 and Omp31 genes. [Ref7270:Shojaei et al, 2018]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BvrR DNA vaccine
c_description: A recombinant plasmid pCDNA-BvrR was constructed by inserting the BvrR gene fragment into a pCDNA3.0 vector to evaluate immunogenicity and protective efficacy. Efficacy: The DNA vaccine pCDNA-BvrR induced a significant level of protection in BALB/c mice as shown by systemic bacterial clearance after challenge with B. abortus S19. Immune response: Immunization induced a specific Th1-type immune response characterized by increased IgG with dominance of IgG2a over IgG1, significant T cell proliferation, and a typical Th1-dominated response. [Ref7271:Chen et al, 2019]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine encoding the BvrR gene; recombinant His6-tagged BvrR protein was expressed and purified for verification. [Ref7271:Chen et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: chitosan-based Brucella nasal vaccine (BNV) plus Brucella LPS
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safe and effective anti-Brucella subunit vaccine for mucosal protection against respiratory exposure. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant reduction of Brucella recovery in lungs and spleen compared to PBS control after nasal challenge. Immune response: Vaccination induced significantly higher systemic IgG and mucosal IgA responses; omp19 induced the highest IgG and IgA levels among components; splenocytes showed increased IFN-γ, lymphocyte proliferation, and CD4+ T cell responses upon re-stimulation. [Ref7272:Senevirathne et al, 2019]
c_preparation: A chitosan-based nasal vaccine formulated with Brucella immunogens sodC, omp19, BLS, PrpA plus Brucella LPS. [Ref7272:Senevirathne et al, 2019]
c_antigen: sodC, omp19, BLS, PrpA; Brucella LPS

c_vaccine_name: chitosan-based Brucella nasal vaccine (BNV)
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safe and effective anti-Brucella subunit vaccine for mucosal protection against respiratory exposure. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant reduction of Brucella recovery in lungs and spleen compared to PBS control after nasal challenge. Immune response: Vaccination induced significantly higher systemic IgG and mucosal IgA responses; omp19 induced the highest IgG and IgA levels among components; splenocytes showed increased IFN-γ, lymphocyte proliferation, and CD4+ T cell responses upon re-stimulation. [Ref7272:Senevirathne et al, 2019]
c_preparation: A chitosan-based nasal vaccine formulated with Brucella immunogens sodC, omp19, BLS, and PrpA; tested with or without Brucella LPS. [Ref7272:Senevirathne et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant SodC RibH Ndk L7/L12 MDH subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficacy of a combination of five recombinant Brucella abortus proteins cloned and expressed in a pMal vector system and purified for vaccination. Efficacy: The combination vaccine significantly reduced bacterial colonization in the spleen with a log protection unit of 1.31, comparable to protection conferred by the live attenuated vaccine RB51. Immune response: Vaccination enhanced cell-mediated immunity as indicated by significantly elevated IFN-γ and reduced IL-10 levels; both IgG1 and IgG2a antibody titers were significantly increased at three and four weeks post first immunization. [Ref7273:Arayan et al, 2019]
c_preparation: The five recombinant proteins were combined and administered intraperitoneally into BALB/c mice. [Ref7273:Arayan et al, 2019]
c_antigen: superoxide dismutase (SodC), riboflavin synthase subunit beta (RibH), nucleoside diphosphate kinase (Ndk), 50S ribosomal protein (L7/L12), malate dehydrogenase (MDH)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella suis vaccine expressing multimeric GnRH
c_description: This study reports the development of a live-attenuated Brucella suis vaccine strain that is auxotrophic for leucine and capable of expressing heterologous antigens, specifically multimeric GnRH, aimed at controlling feral swine populations and brucellosis. Efficacy: The attenuated vaccine strain provided significant protection against Brucella suis challenge in mice. Immune response: Vaccinated mice developed antibodies against the expressed multimeric GnRH antigen. [Ref7274:Smith et al, 2019]
c_preparation: The vaccine strain is leucine auxotrophic, allowing over-expression of heterologous antigens without antibiotic resistance markers. [Ref7274:Smith et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella four antigen recombinant vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A novel anti-Brucella vaccine was developed utilizing rough Salmonella delivering four Brucella antigens to overcome residual virulence and abortion issues of current live Brucella vaccines. Efficacy: Partial protection observed with 33.3% (2/6) of vaccinated midterm pregnant guinea pigs protected from abortion after challenge; lower Brucella recovery in spleen and liver and reduced histopathological burden compared to controls. Immune response: Systemic IgG against antigen components was induced by the Salmonella delivery system, indicating immune activation. [Ref7275:Lalsiamthara et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Rough Salmonella vector delivering four Brucella antigens administered intraperitoneally at 4 × 10^8 CFU. [Ref7275:Lalsiamthara et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: GI24-lysed Brucella abortus cells vaccine candidate
c_description: The study evaluated the efficacy of a vaccine candidate composed of Brucella abortus cells lysed by GI24 as a potential vaccine against brucellosis in Korean black goats. Efficacy: Three of five goats immunized with the GI24-lysed vaccine were completely protected against challenge. Group B showed significantly lower infection index and tissue colonization compared to controls. Immune response: Immunized goats showed significantly higher ELISA optical density values for B. abortus lipopolysaccharide and elevated cytokine levels (IL-4, TNF-α, IFN-γ) compared to controls, indicating a strong immune response without adverse clinical effects. [Ref7276:Kim et al, 2019]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of approximately 3 × 10^9 GI24-lysed Brucella abortus cells administered subcutaneously. [Ref7276:Kim et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles
c_description: The study compared aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: AH/Omp31 nanoparticles induced protection comparable to Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. Immune response: AH/Omp31 induced a mixed T helper type 1 (Th1) and T helper type 2 (Th2) immune response based on cytokine profiles and antibody subclasses. [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles (AH/Omp31). [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with calcium phosphate nanoparticles
c_description: The study aimed to compare calcium phosphate nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: CP/Omp31 nanoparticles elicited protection against Brucella melitensis challenge equivalent to the vaccine strain Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 and showed a low increase in protection compared to CS/Omp31 nanoparticles. Immune response: CP/Omp31 induced a mixed T helper type 1 (Th1) and T helper type 2 (Th2) immune response based on cytokine profiles and antibody subclasses. [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on calcium phosphate nanoparticles (CP/Omp31). [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with chitosan nanoparticles
c_description: The study evaluated chitosan nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: CS/Omp31 nanoparticles elicited protection against Brucella melitensis 16M, but less than CP/Omp31 nanoparticles. Immune response: CS/Omp31 induced a T helper type 1 (Th1) immune response based on cytokine profiles and antibody subclasses. [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on chitosan nanoparticles (CS/Omp31). [Ref7277:Abkar et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Mdh chitosan nanoparticle subunit vaccine (CNs-Mdh)
c_description:
This study aimed to investigate mucosal immune responses induced by Brucella abortus malate dehydrogenase antigen loaded in mucoadhesive chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally in a BALB/c mouse model. Efficacy: CNs-Mdh induced significantly higher IL-6 production in THP-1 cells compared to controls; in mice, IL-4 and IgG-secreting cells increased significantly at 4 and 6 weeks post-immunization; Mdh-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies increased with a predominant IgG1 response; mucosal IgA responses were significantly elevated in nasal washes, genital secretions, fecal extracts, and sera compared to controls. Immune response: The vaccine elicited Th2-related immune responses characterized by increased IL-4 production, predominant IgG1 antibody response, and enhanced antigen-specific mucosal IgA production, indicating effective induction of mucosal immunity through intranasal immunization. [Ref7278:Soh et al, 2019]
This study investigated the immune response elicited by recombinant malate dehydrogenase protein of Brucella abortus loaded into mucoadhesive chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1, was increased; significant production of IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines indicating mixed Th1-Th2 response; significant mucosal IgA responses detected in nasal washes and fecal excretions. Immune response: Induction of mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses with increased antigen-specific IgG1 and mucosal IgA antibodies; spleenocytes produced IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
This study investigates a subunit vaccine composed of Brucella abortus malate dehydrogenase (Mdh) loaded into chitosan nanoparticles (CNs), which act as a mucosal adjuvant to induce systemic immunity via nasal immunization. Efficacy: Intranasal immunization with CNs-Mdh induced significant production of specific IgA in fecal and genital secretions two weeks post-immunization, indicating mucosal and systemic immune activation. Immune response: The vaccine triggered early reduction in epithelial and muscle cell viability, followed by recruitment of immune cells (granulocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes) in NALT, activation of IL-6 and HMGB1 signaling pathways, and maturation of dendritic cells, leading to systemic IgG and IgA production. [Ref7305:Shim et al, 2020a]
The study investigates the immunogenicity and transport of Brucella abortus Mdh antigen loaded in chitosan nanoparticles targeting human microfold (M) cells to induce mucosal immunity via nasal or oral routes. Efficacy: CNs-Mdh induced enhanced transport of Mdh antigen in M cell model and significantly higher production of proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6 compared to Mdh alone, indicating improved antigen delivery and immune activation. Immune response: Activation of MyD88-dependent TLR2 signaling pathway leading to enhanced Th2-related responses and inflammatory cytokine production in M cells, suggesting synergistic effect of Mdh and chitosan nanoparticles in inducing mucosal immunity. [Ref7306:Shim et al, 2020b]
c_preparation:
Malate dehydrogenase antigen was loaded into mucoadhesive chitosan nanoparticles (CNs-Mdh) for intranasal immunization. [Ref7278:Soh et al, 2019]
Recombinant malate dehydrogenase protein loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
The vaccine formulation consists of malate dehydrogenase protein from Brucella abortus loaded into biocompatible and nontoxic chitosan nanoparticles designed for intranasal delivery. [Ref7305:Shim et al, 2020a]
Brucella abortus malate dehydrogenase protein loaded into chitosan nanoparticles (CNs-Mdh). [Ref7306:Shim et al, 2020b]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (BALB/c mice); THP-1 cells; human microfold (M) cells in vitro model (Caco-2 and Raji B cell co-culture); human microfold (M) cells in vitro model (Caco-2 and Raji B cell co-culture), THP-1 cells, BALB/C mice (mentioned from previous study)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: Peptides containing both T-cell and B-cell epitopes of OMP31 were synthesized and used for immunization. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significantly lower bacterial loads in lungs compared to control group after challenge. Immune response: Increased serum IgG1 and IgG2a levels; high degree of IFN-γ-producing T cells in lymphocytes from respiratory draining lymph nodes and spleen. [Ref7279:Zhang et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Peptides administered by nasal route without reported adjuvant. [Ref7279:Zhang et al, 2019]
c_antigen: OMP31 peptides containing T-cell epitope, B-cell epitope, or TB epitopes

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51WboAKF vaccine
c_description: The vaccine strain RB51WboAKF was generated by overexpressing the wbkF gene in Brucella abortus strain RB51 complemented with wboA gene (RB51WboA) to increase O-polysaccharide synthesis. Efficacy: Immunization with RB51WboAKF conferred enhanced protection against virulent B. abortus 2308, B. melitensis 16M, and B. suis 1330 challenge compared to RB51 and RB51WboA vaccine strains. Immune response: Mice vaccinated with RB51WboAKF developed increased levels of smooth LPS-specific serum antibodies (IgG2a and IgG3 isotypes), higher antigen-specific IFN-γ and TNF-α secretion by splenocytes, and increased numbers of antigen-specific IFN-γ secreting CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes compared to RB51 or RB51WboA vaccinated groups. [Ref7280:Dabral et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51WboAKF with overexpression of wbkF gene and complemented wboA gene, phenotypically rough but expressing higher levels of O-polysaccharide. [Ref7280:Dabral et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus BLS Salmonella vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen BLS, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.6 in spleen and 1.12 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. Immune response: Significant induction of Brucella-specific systemic IgG and secretory IgA; increased splenocyte proliferation upon antigen stimulation; elevated interferon-γ and interleukin-4 secretion; strong Salmonella-specific humoral and cell-mediated immune responses. [Ref7281:Senevirathne et al, 2019a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete BLS antigen. [Ref7281:Senevirathne et al, 2019a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Omp19 Salmonella vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen Omp19, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.96 in spleen and 1.14 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. Immune response: Significant induction of Brucella-specific systemic IgG and secretory IgA; increased splenocyte proliferation upon antigen stimulation; elevated interferon-γ and interleukin-4 secretion with notably high response; strong Salmonella-specific humoral and cell-mediated immune responses. [Ref7281:Senevirathne et al, 2019a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete Omp19 antigen. [Ref7281:Senevirathne et al, 2019a]
