c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to clone, express, and purify the BLS gene from Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 to design a subunit vaccine against undulant fever. [Ref7283:Akbari et al, 2019]
c_preparation: The BLS gene was amplified, inserted into pTZ57R/T vector, ligated into pET32(a)+ expression vector, and expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) induced by IPTG; the recombinant protein was confirmed by SDS-PAGE and western blotting. [Ref7283:Akbari et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella rOMP25 subunit vaccine with adjuvant
c_description: Subunit vaccines are considered as an efficient strategy against Brucellosis but are usually less immunogenic than live or killed vaccines; the study aimed to find a proper adjuvant to enhance immune response. Efficacy: CS adjuvant stimulated higher IFN-γ immunity and higher total antibody titers; rOMP25 formulated with CS, IFA, and IFA-CS induced higher IgG2a titers; cell proliferation was promoted after immunization with CS; TNF-α levels were not significantly different except for single IFA treatment. Immune response: CS adjuvant induced a stronger Th1-type immune response (higher IFN-γ and IgG2a) and lower IL-4 response compared to other adjuvants; overall, CS alone or combined with IFA improved Th1-Th2 responses. [Ref7284:Yousefi et al, 2019]
c_adjuvant: yes; Aluminum Hydroxide; Incomplete Freund; Chitosan Nanoparticle
c_preparation: Recombinant OMP25 protein formulated with different adjuvants including Aluminum Hydroxide (AH), Incomplete Freund (IFA), Chitosan Nanoparticle (CS), and combinations of CS with AH or IFA. [Ref7284:Yousefi et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis BtaF subunit vaccine
c_description: The BtaF passenger domain was engineered and expressed as a soluble trimeric protein for nasal vaccination. Efficacy: Nasal vaccination with BtaF+c-di-AMP did not protect against respiratory B. suis challenge but conferred significant protection against intragastric challenge, reducing splenic bacterial load by 3.28 log CFU. Immune response: Immunization induced increased serum IgG and IgA antibodies including mixed IgG2a/IgG1, mucosal IgA, antibodies that reduced bacterial adhesion in vitro, increased IL-2, IL-5, IL-17, and IFN-γ secretion by spleen cells, central memory CD4+ T cells in cervical lymph nodes, a BtaF-specific delayed-type hypersensitivity response, and high IFN-γ production by lung cells upon antigen stimulation. [Ref7286:Muñoz et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Nasal immunization with recombinant BtaF protein plus the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP. [Ref7286:Muñoz et al, 2019]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; A549 alveolar epithelial cells

c_vaccine_name: novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine based on FliC, 7α-HSDH, BhuA antigens
c_description: Due to safety problems with live attenuated vaccines Rev. 1 and RB51, safer and efficient vaccines are needed; this study evaluates two novel multi-peptide vaccine candidates composed of epitopes from FliC, 7α-HSDH, and BhuA proteins. Efficacy: Multi-epitope antigens with and without poly I:C provided cross protection against B. melitensis 16M and B. abortus 544 infections. Immune response: Significant induction of Th1 immunity with high levels of specific IgG (especially IgG2a), IFN-γ, and IL-2; addition of poly I:C enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7287:Sadeghi et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Multi-epitope antigens formulated with and without the adjuvant poly I:C. [Ref7287:Sadeghi et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated methanol-killed Brucella abortus strain RB51 polyanhydride VPEAR vaccine
c_description: The study reports fabrication of an implantable single dose polyanhydride-based, methanol-killed RB51 antigen containing delivery platform (VPEAR) for vaccination against bovine brucellosis. Efficacy: Initial vaccination with VPEAR did not induce measurable RB51-specific IFN-γ or IgG responses in peripheral blood; however, a subsequent booster with live RB51 induced an anamnestic response comparable in magnitude and kinetics to live RB51 vaccination alone; IgG titers were significantly higher in VPEAR vaccinated animals after booster. Immune response: VPEAR vaccination generated and sustained memory CD4+ IFN-γ-mediated T cell and humoral (IgG) responses against Brucella following booster vaccination, demonstrating the potential of killed antigen to induce protective immunity in the natural host. [Ref7288:Boggiatto et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Polyanhydride-based implantable delivery platform containing methanol-killed RB51 antigen. [Ref7288:Boggiatto et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp3b/BCSP31/SOD recombinant attenuated Salmonella vector vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to assess the protective efficacy of a novel Brucella vaccine formulation in goats using a Salmonella-based delivery system expressing recombinant Brucella abortus Omp3b, BCSP31, and SOD proteins. Efficacy: 40% of vaccinated animals were protected against B. abortus infection. The infection index and colonization of B. abortus in tested tissues were significantly lower in vaccinated goats compared to controls. Immune response: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher serum immunoglobulin G titers and interferon gamma concentrations compared to controls, indicating significant antigen-specific immune responses. [Ref7290:Kim et al, 2019a]
c_preparation: A mixture of three Brucella vaccine strains using a Salmonella-based delivery system, each expressing one of the recombinant B. abortus proteins Omp3b, BCSP31, or SOD, administered at 3.0 × 10^9 CFU/mL. [Ref7290:Kim et al, 2019a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 human interleukin 2 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study reports the construction of a recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Omp16-IL2 fusion protein as an oral Lactococcus-based vaccine, proposed as an alternative to commonly used live attenuated vaccines for future studies against brucellosis. [Ref7291:Rezaei et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Omp16-IL2 fusion gene cloned into pAMJ2008 expression vector and expressed in Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris MG1363 by electrotransformation; purified recombinant fusion protein produced. [Ref7291:Rezaei et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant cocktail protein vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated a combination vaccine of three recombinant Brucella abortus proteins (Mdh, Omp10, Omp19) loaded into chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Increased antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1; significant increase of anti-Mdh IgA but not anti-Omp IgA; spleenocytes produced significant IFN-γ and IL-4 indicating mixed Th1-Th2 response. Immune response: Induction of mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses with increased IgG1 and mucosal IgA antibodies specific to Mdh antigen; combination elicited IgG specific to each antigen type. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Cocktail of recombinant Mdh, Omp10, and Omp19 proteins loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
c_antigen: malate dehydrogenase (Mdh), outer membrane protein 10 (Omp10), outer membrane protein 19 (Omp19)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant outer membrane protein 10 vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated immune responses induced by recombinant outer membrane protein 10 of Brucella abortus loaded into chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Increased antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1; significant mucosal IgA responses detected in sera, nasal washes, genital secretions, and fecal excretions; spleenocytes did not show significant IFN-γ or IL-4 production for Omp10 alone. Immune response: Predominantly Th2-polarized immune response with increased IgG1 and mucosal IgA antibodies. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp10 protein loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant outer membrane protein 19 vaccine
c_description: This study assessed immune responses induced by recombinant outer membrane protein 19 of Brucella abortus loaded into chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Increased antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1; significant mucosal IgA responses detected in sera, nasal washes, genital secretions, and fecal excretions; spleenocytes produced significant IFN-γ and IL-4 indicating mixed Th1-Th2 response. Immune response: Induction of mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses with increased IgG1 and mucosal IgA antibodies; spleenocytes produced IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally. [Ref7292:Shim et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 epitopic region subunit vaccine fused to interleukin 2
c_description: The vaccine is a recombinant protein consisting of three repeats of a 27 amino acid immunogenic epitope derived from OMP31 antigen of Brucella melitensis fused to IL-2 as a molecular adjuvant to enhance immune stimulation. Efficacy: Treatments with chimeric proteins significantly reduced splenocyte microbial load compared to controls; 3E-IL2 treatment showed the best protection with lowest agglutination rates in Wright test. Immune response: Recombinant proteins stimulated Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2) and antibody production with higher IgG2a than IgG1 isotype; presence of both molecular (IL-2) and chemical (IFA) adjuvants enhanced immune stimulation; 3E-IL2 induced the highest levels of IFN-γ and IL-2. [Ref7293:Nazifi et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein with molecular adjuvant IL-2; chemical adjuvant incomplete Freund's adjuvant (IFA) was also used in some treatments. [Ref7293:Nazifi et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella SodC and Omp19 vaccine
c_description: The study investigated an oral live vaccine candidate using an attenuated Salmonella typhimurium strain secreting Brucella antigens SodC and Omp19, with the addition of sodium bicarbonate antacid to enhance vaccine efficacy. Efficacy: Addition of sodium bicarbonate significantly increased anti-Brucella-specific systemic IgG levels, lymphocyte proliferation, CD4+ T cell responses, and enhanced Salmonella colonization in the intestine, indicating improved protective immune response compared to vaccine without sodium bicarbonate. Immune response: Induction of a mixed Th1-Th2 response evidenced by increased systemic IgG, lymphocyte proliferation, and CD4+ T cell responses following vaccination with sodium bicarbonate-enhanced formulation. [Ref7294:Hewawaduge et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella typhimurium strain JOL1800 secreting Brucella SodC and Omp19 antigens; sodium bicarbonate (1.3% w/v) administered orally 30 minutes before and immediately after immunization as an antacid buffer. [Ref7294:Hewawaduge et al, 2020]
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SodC); outer membrane protein 19 (Omp19)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis wbkC deletion wbdR tagged vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a modified Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 strain deleted in wbkC (lipopolysaccharide formyl-transferase) and carrying wbdR (E. coli acetyl-transferase) to induce an antibody response distinguishable from wild-type strains and to avoid interference with B. melitensis serodiagnosis. Efficacy: The modified Rev. 1 vaccine was comparatively attenuated and provided protection against Brucella ovis infection in mice. Immune response: The vaccine triggered antibodies that could be differentiated from those evoked by wild-type strains, avoiding interference with serodiagnosis of B. melitensis. [Ref7295:Aragón-Aranda et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 strain with wbkC gene deletion and wbdR gene insertion. [Ref7295:Aragón-Aranda et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella neotomae wboA deletion vaccine
c_description: A rough, live-attenuated Brucella neotomae strain was generated by deleting the wboA gene encoding a glycosyltransferase, resulting in loss of the O-side chain in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) allowing serological differentiation from field-infected animals. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly higher protection against virulent Brucella suis 1330 challenge compared to controls; the rough mutant was cleared from mice within 6 weeks even at high dose (2 x 10^8 CFU). Immune response: Vaccination induced a Th1 mediated immune response evidenced by antibody titers and cytokine production by splenocytes correlating with protection. [Ref7296:Jain-Gupta et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain lacking O-side chain due to wboA gene deletion. [Ref7296:Jain-Gupta et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 rfbD deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study developed a rfbD gene deleted mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 to overcome shortcomings of the parental S19 vaccine such as residual virulence, abortion induction, and sero-diagnostic interference. Efficacy: S19ΔR showed a protective index of 1.90 against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice. Immune response: The mutant induced significantly lower anti-Brucella humoral response compared to S19, with minimal induction of Brucella specific IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, and IgG3, resulting in no apparent reactivity to RBPT antigen, indicating DIVA compatibility. [Ref7297:Lalsiamthara et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain S19ΔR exhibiting rough LPS phenotype confirmed by acriflavine dye-agglutination and LPS-SDS-PAGE analysis. [Ref7297:Lalsiamthara et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus membrane blebs subunit vaccine
c_description: Membrane blebs were obtained from Brucella abortus 2308 and analyzed by proteomics to identify proteins including known immunogens. Efficacy: Mice immunized with 2308 membrane blebs showed protective immune responses similar to the Brucella abortus RB51 vaccine control, with significant reduction in spleen CFUs after challenge (P < 0.05). Immune response: Higher IgG2a levels post-boosting compared to RB51 blebs or RB51 vaccine; increased percentage of activated B cells (CD19+CD69+) in vitro. [Ref7298:Araiza-Villanueva et al, 2019]
c_preparation: Acellular vaccine composed of membrane blebs derived from Brucella abortus 2308. [Ref7298:Araiza-Villanueva et al, 2019]
c_antigen: SodC; Omp2b; Omp2a; Omp10; Omp16; Omp19

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus delta virB2 vaccine
c_description: The attenuated mutant B. abortusΔvirB2 is a virB2 gene deletion mutant studied as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: The mutant B. abortusΔvirB2 was progressively killed inside mature osteoclasts, mimicking infection kinetics in macrophages. Immune response: No apoptosis or stimulation of nitric oxide or lactose dehydrogenase production was observed in mature osteoclasts infected with this mutant. [Ref7299:Khalaf et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain B. abortusΔvirB2. [Ref7299:Khalaf et al, 2020]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (murine bone marrow-derived macrophages and mature osteoclasts)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus double mutant znBAZ vaccine
c_description:
A newly developed Brucella abortus double mutant (znBAZ) vaccine was used with an oral prime and nasal boost regimen. Efficacy: znBAZ conferred nearly complete protection against pulmonary challenge with wild-type B. abortus 2308, with protective efficacy >2800-fold better than the RB51 vaccine; CD8+ T cells were critical for protection, while CD4+ T cells were not essential in znBAZ-vaccinated mice. Immune response: Vaccination with znBAZ potently stimulated CD8+ T cells including CD44+ CD69+ CD8+ TRM cells (both CD103+ and CD103- subsets) in the lung; these cells produced IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-17 (though IL-17 was not required for protection); RB51 vaccination induced mostly CD4+ T cells; depletion studies showed CD8+ T cells were key for protection in znBAZ vaccination. [Ref7300:Wang et al, 2020a]
The Brucella abortus double-mutant znBAZ was evaluated for protective efficacy after a single nasal dose vaccination. Efficacy: znBAZ vaccination reduced splenic and lung colonization by wild-type Brucella abortus by more than 3-4 logs; S19 reduced lung colonization by 32-fold; RB51 failed to reduce colonization. Immune response: znBAZ vaccination induced a greater than 3-fold increase in pulmonary CD8+ T cells and enhanced recruitment of polyfunctional CD8+ T cells by over 100-fold; IL-17 production by both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells was induced; IFN-γ and TNF-α production by CD4+ T cells was observed with all vaccines; protection was attributed to IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T cells as depletion abrogated protection; S19 increased only CD4+ T cells; RB51 and S19 stimulation of CD4+ T cells alone was insufficient for protection. [Ref7381:Wang et al, 2023]
c_preparation:
Live attenuated double mutant znBAZ administered mucosally (oral prime, nasal boost). [Ref7300:Wang et al, 2020a]
Live attenuated double-mutant Brucella abortus with deletions in znuA and norD genes and lacZ marker administered nasally. [Ref7381:Wang et al, 2023]
c_antigen: double mutant (znBAZ) | znuA deletion; norD deletion; lacZ marker

c_vaccine_name: combined subunit vaccine comprising BP26, Omp25 and L7/L12
c_description: The study addresses the limitations of current Brucella abortus vaccines strain 19 and RB51, which pose risks of virulence and attenuation reversal, and explores a safer alternative using a combined subunit vaccine of three B. abortus immunogens. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccinated mice showed superior protection (log10 reduction in bacterial load) against virulent B. abortus 544 compared to individual antigen vaccines, though protection was less than that conferred by B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. Immune response: CSV immunized mice exhibited heightened IgG titers specific to all three antigens, a predominant Th2 immune response indicated by IgG1/IgG2a ratios, and prominent Th1-dependent cytokine (IFN-γ) levels, suggesting a mixed Th1/Th2 immune response. [Ref7301:Gupta et al, 2019]
c_preparation: A combined subunit vaccine comprising the BP26, Omp25, and L7/L12 antigens of Brucella abortus. [Ref7301:Gupta et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Live vaccine consisting of attenuated Salmonella secreting and delivering Brucella ribosomal protein L7/L12
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study employed the Brucella abortus L7/L12 antigen cloned into a prokaryotic expression vector under a beta-lactamase secretory signal and transformed into an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain to deliver the antigen. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant reduction in Brucella colonization in spleen and liver tissues after challenge with virulent B. abortus compared to controls. Immune response: The vaccine elicited Brucella antigen-specific Th1 and Th2 immune responses significantly higher than controls, with enhanced cell-mediated immunity confirmed by splenocyte proliferation, increased CD4+ and CD8+ T cell markers, and cytokine profiling upon antigen restimulation. [Ref7302:Senevirathne et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain JOL1800 (∆lon, ∆cpxR, ∆asd, and ∆rfaL) transformed with plasmid pJHL65::L7/L12 secreting the L7/L12 antigen. [Ref7302:Senevirathne et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus FliC subunit vaccine with Mannosylated Chitosan Nanoparticles adjuvant
c_description: FliC protein, a virulence factor of Brucella, was selected as a promising antigen for vaccine development due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: Immunization with FliC and FliC-MCN conferred significant protection against Brucella melitensis 16 M and Brucella abortus 544 infections. Immune response: Both FliC and FliC-MCN induced significant specific IgG responses with higher IgG2a titers; spleen cells produced high levels of IFN-γ and IL-2 and low levels of IL-10 cytokines, indicating a Th1-biased immune response. [Ref7304:Sadeghi et al, 2020]
c_preparation: FliC protein was cloned, expressed, purified, and loaded onto Mannosylated Chitosan Nanoparticles to create a targeted vaccine delivery system. [Ref7304:Sadeghi et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 delta irr vaccine
c_description: The study constructed the M5-90Δirr mutant of Brucella melitensis to investigate the role of the irr gene in virulence and growth, suggesting its potential as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: M5-90Δirr showed attenuated adhesion and invasion but enhanced intracellular replication and resistance to hydrogen peroxide; growth was stronger under iron-limiting conditions; no significant difference in spleen bacterial load compared to parental strain at 7 and 15 days postinfection; splenic index was lower than parental strain, indicating attenuation. [Ref7307:Zhang et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion of the irr gene. [Ref7307:Zhang et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 delta rirA vaccine
c_description: The study constructed the M5-90ΔrirA mutant of Brucella melitensis to investigate the role of the rirA gene in virulence and growth. Efficacy: M5-90ΔrirA showed attenuated adhesion and invasion but enhanced intracellular replication and resistance to hydrogen peroxide; bacterial load in spleen was significantly reduced at 15 days postinfection compared to parental strain. [Ref7307:Zhang et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion of the rirA gene. [Ref7307:Zhang et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Omp25 and L7/L12 divalent recombinant vaccine
c_description: Currently used Brucella abortus strain 19 and RB51 vaccines are live attenuated strains but pose risks such as attenuation reversal and virulence; recombinant subunit vaccines are considered a safe and competent alternative. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the combined Omp25+L7/L12 vaccine exhibited superior Log10 protection against virulent Brucella abortus 544 compared to individual vaccines. Immune response: The combined vaccine induced enhanced IgG titers specific to both antigens; IgG1/IgG2a ratio indicated a predominant Th2 immune response in immunized mice. [Ref7308:Gupta et al, 2020]
c_preparation: A divalent recombinant vaccine consisting of Omp25 and L7/L12 proteins of Brucella abortus was formulated and evaluated individually and in combination. [Ref7308:Gupta et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: combination of recombinant Brucella abortus proteins Adk and SecB subunit vaccine
c_description: Combination of two recombinant proteins encoded by Brucella abortus genes Adk and SecB were cloned and expressed in E. coli and evaluated as combined subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with combined recombinant Adk and SecB proteins significantly reduced spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS control, indicating protection against B. abortus infection. Immune response: Induced strong proinflammatory cytokines TNF and IL-6; increased IFN-γ and decreased IL-10 production; enhanced blood CD4+ T cell population; significantly induced specific IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies; stimulated both humoral and T helper 1 T cell immunity. [Ref7309:Huy et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Combined recombinant Adk and SecB proteins purified after expression in Escherichia coli DH5α; administered intraperitoneally. [Ref7309:Huy et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant Brucella abortus protein Adk subunit vaccine
c_description: Two recombinant proteins encoded by Brucella abortus gene Adk were cloned and expressed in E. coli and evaluated as single subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with recombinant Adk protein significantly reduced spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS control, indicating protection against B. abortus infection. Immune response: Induced strong proinflammatory cytokines TNF and IL-6; increased IFN-γ and decreased IL-10 production; enhanced blood CD4+ T cell population; significantly induced specific IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies; stimulated both humoral and T helper 1 T cell immunity. [Ref7309:Huy et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Recombinant Adk protein purified after expression in Escherichia coli DH5α; administered intraperitoneally. [Ref7309:Huy et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 wbkA gene deletion vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to create a gene knockout mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 by deleting the wbkA gene, which encodes part of the LPS O-chain, to reduce diagnostic interference and maintain attenuation. Efficacy: The wbkA mutant induced a splenocyte proliferative response in mice comparable or superior to parental S19 and RB51 strains, indicating immunogenicity. Immune response: The mutant strain did not induce IgM antibody response detectable by ELISA, suggesting reduced interference in serological differentiation between vaccinated and infected animals. [Ref7311:Nayeri et al, 2019]
c_preparation: A wbkA gene knockout mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 was constructed to produce a strain deficient in LPS O-chain structure. [Ref7311:Nayeri et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant probiotic Lactobacillus casei vector vaccine expressing OMP19
c_description: The gene encoding OMP19 antigen was amplified and cloned into expression vector pT1NX, then transformed into Lactobacillus casei by electroporation to create a recombinant probiotic vector vaccine. Efficacy: Mice orally immunized with the recombinant vaccine showed very good protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus 544 compared to negative controls. Immune response: The vaccinated mice exhibited strong general and mucosal immune responses against Brucella abortus. [Ref7312:Mohammadi et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactobacillus casei expressing OMP19 protein. [Ref7312:Mohammadi et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-polysaccharide conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study developed a bioconjugate vaccine using an O-linked glycosylation system applied to Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9, which has O-antigen polysaccharide identical to Brucella abortus, to create a safe vaccine candidate avoiding culture of highly pathogenic B. abortus. Efficacy: The vaccine elicited B. abortus OPS-specific serum IgG, significantly reduced bacterial loads in spleen, mitigated infection, prevented severe tissue damage, and protected mice against lethal challenge with B. abortus strain A19. Immune response: Strong immune response characterized by production of B. abortus OPS-specific serum IgG antibodies. [Ref7313:Huang et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Bioconjugate vaccine produced by glycosylation of Y. enterocolitica O:9 with O-antigen polysaccharide from B. abortus. [Ref7313:Huang et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16M delta vjbR vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR was evaluated for safety and efficacy in pregnant sheep, a natural host species, to address the limitations of the current live-attenuated vaccine Rev. 1 which causes abortions in pregnant animals. Efficacy: 16MΔvjbR provided protection comparable to Rev. 1 with no statistical difference in colonization of target organs after challenge. Immune response: Not reported explicitly in the abstract. [Ref7314:Hensel et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR strain administered subcutaneously at 1 × 10^10 CFU/ml. [Ref7314:Hensel et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis RM6/66 ΔvjbR vaccine candidate
c_description: The vaccine candidate is a live attenuated strain of Brucella canis RM6/66 with a deletion in the vjbR gene developed to protect against canine brucellosis, a disease with no current vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant protection against organ colonization and histopathologic lesions after challenge; booster or adjuvant did not enhance protection. Immune response: Vaccination induced a robust humoral immune response in mice and activated canine dendritic cells in vitro. [Ref7315:Stranahan et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis RM6/66 ΔvjbR strain administered at 10^9 CFU by intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes; adjuvant addition or booster dose did not improve protection. [Ref7315:Stranahan et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine mglA deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study evaluates the effect of mglA gene deletion on oxidative stress tolerance and survival within macrophages compared to the parental strain. Efficacy: The ∆mglA 3.14 mutant exhibited increased tolerance to H2O2 but did not show improved survival inside murine macrophages compared to the parental strain. Immune response: The mutant induced cytokine production in macrophages, suggesting an enhanced immune activation relative to the parental strain. [Ref7317:Jacob et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus strain 19 with mglA gene deletion. [Ref7317:Jacob et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b protein vaccine
c_description: This study analyzed the physicochemical properties, structural characteristics, and dominant epitopes of Brucella outer membrane protein 2b (Omp2b) to provide a theoretical basis for constructing a multivalent epitope vaccine. Immune response: Identification of three linear B cell dominant epitopes, five CD8+ T cell dominant epitopes, and three CD4+ T cell dominant epitopes for Omp2b. [Ref7318:Sha et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: split-conjugated animal brucellosis vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to obtain a vaccine against animal brucellosis with high immunogenic properties by evaluating the effectiveness of a split-conjugated vaccine combined with immunomodulators fosprenil and polypeptide C. Efficacy: The split-conjugated vaccine combined with fosprenil induced higher antibody titers that persisted longer compared to the vaccine combined with polypeptide C or vaccine alone. Immune response: The vaccine with fosprenil enhanced the humoral immune response against brucellosis in calves. [Ref7319:Bouchemla et al, 2019]
c_preparation: The dry split-conjugated vaccine was dissolved in saline; fosprenil was administered intramuscularly; polypeptide C was mixed with the vaccine for subcutaneous injection in one group; another group received vaccine diluted with isotonic sodium chloride solution. [Ref7319:Bouchemla et al, 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 delta gntR bacterial ghost vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to generate Brucella abortus ghosts by homologous recombination and bacterial ghost technologies to create a safe vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The 2308ΔgntR ghost induced high protective immunity against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain S2308 in BALB/c mice. Immune response: The vaccine elicited a strong anti-Brucella-specific IgG response, induced secretion of IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines, and stimulated robust spleen CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses. [Ref7320:Wang et al, 2020b]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of bacterial ghosts derived from Brucella abortus strain 2308 with a gntR gene deletion. [Ref7320:Wang et al, 2020b]

c_vaccine_name: 7α-HSDH calcium phosphate nanoparticle-adsorbed vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using 7α-HSDH antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses and protection levels comparable to commercial vaccines B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain RB51. Immune response: Increased ratio of specific IgG2a (Th1-associated) to IgG1 (Th2-associated) antibodies; enhanced cellular and humoral immunity compared to controls. [Ref7321:Sadeghi et al, 2020a]
c_preparation: 7α-HSDH protein antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface. [Ref7321:Sadeghi et al, 2020a]

c_vaccine_name: BhuA calcium phosphate nanoparticle-adsorbed vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using BhuA antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses but did not show protection comparable to commercial vaccines. Immune response: Increased ratio of specific IgG2a (Th1-associated) to IgG1 (Th2-associated) antibodies; enhanced cellular and humoral immunity compared to controls. [Ref7321:Sadeghi et al, 2020a]
c_preparation: BhuA protein antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface. [Ref7321:Sadeghi et al, 2020a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 104M vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficacy and safety of Brucella abortus strain 104M administered by intratracheal aerosol delivery, intranasal instillation, or subcutaneous injection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed no abnormal clinical symptoms or significant body weight changes. Spleen weights post-challenge were significantly lower in immunized groups compared to controls. Bacterial loads in spleens decreased over time and were significantly lower than controls after challenge. High titers of specific antibodies were detected, peaking at week 8. Cytokine levels (IFN-γ, IL-18) were elevated pre-challenge and modulated post-challenge. No significant differences were observed among immunization routes. The vaccine showed obvious protective efficacy against aerosol challenge. Immune response: Both humoral and cellular immunity were stimulated by the vaccine. High titers of Brucella 104M-specific IgG2a antibodies were detected, higher than IgG1. Cytokines IFN-γ, IL-18, and IL-1β concentrations in serum and lung homogenate were significantly elevated in immunized groups before challenge. After challenge, serum cytokine levels decreased compared to controls, while lung cytokine levels remained elevated. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 104M delivered via three routes: intratracheal aerosol, intranasal instillation, and subcutaneous injection. [Ref7323:Wei et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus RNase E defective strain vaccine
c_description: The study generated a Brucella abortus strain encoding a defective version of RNase E lacking the C-terminal portion (rne-tnc), which was attenuated in a mouse model of infection. Efficacy: The rne-tnc strain was attenuated in the mouse model, indicating reduced virulence. [Ref7324:Sheehan et al, 2020]
c_antigen: RNase E (defective version lacking C-terminal portion)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis pyruvate phosphate dikinase deletion vaccine
c_description: The study reports the generation of a pyruvate phosphate dikinase (PpdK) deletion mutant in Brucella ovis PA strains (both CO2-dependent and CO2-independent) as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The PpdK mutant showed impaired growth in vitro, inability to multiply in infected cells, and an unusual attenuation pattern in mice with initial higher spleen colonization followed by marked decrease, indicating attenuation and potential as a vaccine candidate. [Ref7325:Vizcaíno et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strains with deletion of the PpdK gene impairing growth and virulence. [Ref7325:Vizcaíno et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 BA vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immune activation in mice vaccinated with Brucella abortus 19 BA. Efficacy: Not directly reported; the study observed antigen-specific activation of lymphocytes indicating immune response. Immune response: Statistically significant increase in CD25 expression by B cells and CD69 expression by T cells upon incubation with brucellosis polysaccharide-protein antigen; brucellin increased CD25 expression by both B and T cells; brucellin showed antigen-specific activity against CD19+CD25+ cells. The method may be promising for evaluating brucellosis immunoprophylaxis effectiveness. [Ref7326:Voitkova et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 delta per outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: The study explores outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) extracted from Brucella abortus S19Δper as an alternative subunit vaccine candidate to address safety issues associated with the live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine. Efficacy: OMVs immunized mice showed reduced splenic weight index and lower Brucella abortus strain 544 counts compared to unimmunized mice, indicating good protective efficacy; OMVs S19Δper induced higher IgG titers but conferred nearly equal protection as OMVs S19. Immune response: OMVs S19Δper elicited high IgG titers including both Th1 (IgG2a) and Th2 (IgG1) antibodies, stimulated Th1 cytokines (IL-2, TNF) and Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-6, IL-10), and induced CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, suggesting a mixed Th1 and Th2 immune response ensuring protection against virulent challenge. [Ref7329:Solanki et al, 2021]
c_preparation: OMVs derived from the LPS defective S19Δper strain, characterized by higher OMV release and more homogeneous populations compared to parent strain S19 OMVs. [Ref7329:Solanki et al, 2021]
c_antigen: LPS defective S19Δper outer membrane proteins

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella abortus strain 19 were evaluated as an alternative subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: OMVs S19 immunized mice showed reduced splenic weight index and lower bacterial counts after challenge, indicating protective efficacy similar to OMVs S19Δper. Immune response: Induced IgG including Th1 (IgG2a) and Th2 (IgG1) antibodies, stimulated Th1 and Th2 cytokines, and elicited CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, indicating a mixed Th1 and Th2 immune response. [Ref7329:Solanki et al, 2021]
c_preparation: OMVs isolated from the parent strain S19, characterized by higher polydispersity index compared to S19Δper OMVs. [Ref7329:Solanki et al, 2021]
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins and LPS of Brucella abortus strain 19

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp10 Omp28 L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Omp10-Omp28-L7/L12 proteins were expressed in Pichia pastoris and used as immunogens to evaluate immune responses. Recombinant Omp10-Omp28-L7/L12 proteins were expressed in Escherichia coli and used as immunogens to evaluate immune responses. Efficacy: The recombinant protein expressed in Pichia pastoris with TPPPS adjuvant provided the most pronounced immune effect and significantly better protection than negative controls but less protection than the B. melitensis M5 live vaccine. Efficacy: The recombinant protein expressed in Escherichia coli provided significantly better protection than negative controls; addition of TPPPS adjuvant improved protective effects; protection was less than that of the B. melitensis M5 live vaccine. Immune response: Significantly higher antibody levels, lymphocyte proliferation, T cell percentages, and cytokine secretion compared to PBS control; TPPPS adjuvant enhanced immune responses. [Ref7330:Zhu et al, 2020]
c_adjuvant: yes; Taishan Pinus massoniana pollen polysaccharides (TPPPS)
c_preparation:
Recombinant proteins expressed in Pichia pastoris combined with TPPPS adjuvant. [Ref7330:Zhu et al, 2020]
Recombinant proteins expressed in Escherichia coli combined with TPPPS adjuvant. [Ref7330:Zhu et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella suis, B. ovis, B. canis, and B. neotomae were purified and analyzed to determine their proteomic composition and antigenic proteins. Immune response: Proteins contained in the vesicles from different Brucella species were detected by anti-Brucella sera, indicating the presence of immunogenic proteins supporting the use of OMVs as acellular vaccine candidates. [Ref7333:Socorro et al, 2021]
c_preparation: OMVs purified from the outer membrane of the four Brucella species; proteomic analysis by SDS-PAGE, transmission electron microscopy, and liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry; antigenic proteins detected by western blot with anti-Brucella sera. [Ref7333:Socorro et al, 2021]
c_antigen: Omp16; Omp25; Omp31; SodC; Omp2a; BhuA

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella Omp19 Salmonella vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Oral administration of live attenuated Salmonella secreting Brucella Omp19 antigen with antacid buffers to neutralize stomach acidity and improve vaccine viability. Efficacy: Significant enhancement of antigen-specific protective immune responses against virulent Brucella challenge with antacid co-administration. Immune response: Enhanced antigen-specific protective immune responses against Brucella following oral vaccination with Salmonella delivering Omp19 antigen and antacid buffers. [Ref7334:Hewawaduge et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella vector secreting Brucella Omp19 antigen co-administered orally with sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based gastric antacid buffers. [Ref7334:Hewawaduge et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella SodC Omp19 Salmonella vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study investigated oral administration of a live attenuated Salmonella vaccine secreting Brucella antigens SodC and Omp19, combined with antacid formulations to neutralize stomach acidity and improve vaccine viability. Efficacy: Co-administration with either sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based antacid buffers significantly enhanced antigen-specific protective immune responses against virulent Brucella challenge; magnesium hydroxide buffer improved Salmonella survival and was safer. Immune response: Significant enhancement of antigen-specific protective immune responses against Brucella was observed with oral vaccination using Salmonella delivering SodC and Omp19 antigens combined with antacid buffers. [Ref7334:Hewawaduge et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella vector secreting Brucella SodC and Omp19 antigens co-administered orally with sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based gastric antacid buffers. [Ref7334:Hewawaduge et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 Omp19 Omp28 L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficiency of a combination of four recombinant Brucella abortus proteins as a combined subunit vaccine against B. abortus infection. Efficacy: CSV-treated macrophages showed increased IFN-γ and IL-12 production and decreased IL-10; enhanced nitric oxide production indicating activation of bactericidal mechanisms; immunized mice showed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, MCP-1), higher IFN-γ than IL-10, and elevated IgG2a titers compared to IgG1, suggesting effective immune activation. Immune response: Predominantly T helper 1 (Th1) immune response characterized by increased IFN-γ, IL-12, TNF-α, IL-6, MCP-1, and IgG2a antibody isotype, with decreased IL-10, indicating activation of cell-mediated immunity and macrophage bactericidal activity. [Ref7335:Huy et al, 2020a]
c_preparation: A combined subunit vaccine composed of four recombinant proteins: Omp16, Omp19, Omp28, and 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12. [Ref7335:Huy et al, 2020a]
c_model_host: RAW 264.7 cell line; Mus musculus (BALB/c mice)

c_vaccine_name: recombinant influenza viral vector vaccine expressing Brucella outer membrane proteins and Cu-Zn SOD
c_description:
A new candidate vector vaccine against human brucellosis was developed based on recombinant influenza viral vectors (rIVV) subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella outer membrane proteins Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, or Cu-Zn SOD proteins. Efficacy: Double intranasal immunization at 10^6 EID50 dose provided 80% protection of guinea pigs from B. melitensis 16M infection, comparable to the commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref7336:Bugybayeva et al, 2021]
Developed recombinant influenza viral vector subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella immunodominant proteins from NS1 open reading frame to create human brucellosis vaccine candidates. Efficacy: All vaccine formulations were safe in mice; vaccine formulations and commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine protected mice from B. melitensis 16M infection with 1.6 to 2.97 log10 unit reduction; tetravalent vaccine formulation showed significant protection in guinea pigs (0.2 ± 0.4 log10 units reduction) comparable to commercial Rev. 1 vaccine (1.2 ± 2.6 log10 units reduction). [Ref7331:Bugybayeva et al, 2020]
c_preparation:
Recombinant influenza viral vectors subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, or Cu-Zn SOD proteins; administered via conjunctival, intranasal, and sublingual routes at doses of 10^5, 10^6, and 10^7 EID50. [Ref7336:Bugybayeva et al, 2021]
Created 18 mono-, bi-, and tetravalent vaccine formulations using influenza viral vectors expressing Omp16, Omp19, L7/L12, and SOD proteins; tetravalent formulation Flu-NS1-80-Omp16+Flu-NS1-80-L7/L12+Flu-NS1-80-Omp19+Flu-NS1-80-SOD selected as lead candidate. [Ref7331:Bugybayeva et al, 2020]
c_antigen: Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; Cu-Zn SOD | Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD)
c_model_host: guinea pig; Mus musculus; Cavia porcellus

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis BLSOmp31 subunit vaccine
c_description:
This study tested a new delivery system for mucosal immunization with BLSOmp31 in a murine model to improve efficacy over previous formulations. Efficacy: BLSOmp31/CpG-ODN/Coa-ASC16 administered subcutaneously conferred significant protection against B. ovis challenge; ocular administration showed a similar degree of protection (3.66 and 3.60 logs of protection, respectively). Immune response: Subcutaneous administration stimulated a mixed Th1-Th2 immune response with highest IFN-ɣ levels; induced mixed IgG1/IgG2a antibodies; ocular route induced lower serum IgG and IgA, less IFN-ɣ and IL-4; no antibodies detected in vaginal lavages or saliva; fecal antigen-specific IgA slightly higher with subcutaneous route. [Ref7337:Moran et al, 2021]
BLSOmp31 was previously identified as a protective immunogen against Brucella ovis. In this study, it was formulated with a modified ISCOMATRIX adjuvant called ISPA and administered by subcutaneous and ocular routes. Efficacy: Both subcutaneous and ocular immunization routes significantly protected mice against Brucella ovis infection. Immune response: Immunization induced significantly higher IgG antibody levels with a mixed Th1/Th2 profile; IgA and IgG detected in sera and various mucosal secretions; opsonic antibodies enhanced uptake of labeled Brucella ovis by neutrophils and monocytes; subcutaneous immunization induced highest IFN-ɣ levels; ocular immunization induced significant IFN-ɣ and IL-4 levels compared to non-immunized controls. [Ref7356:Moran et al, 2022]
c_adjuvant: yes; class B CpG-ODN | yes; ISPA (modified ISCOMATRIX)
c_preparation:
BLSOmp31 formulated with class B CpG-ODN in a nanostructure called Coa-ASC16; compared with BLSOmp31 alone, BLSOmp31 with CpG-ODN, and BLSOmp31 emulsified in Incomplete Freund Adjuvant. [Ref7337:Moran et al, 2021]
Polymeric BLSOmp31 antigen formulated with ISPA adjuvant. [Ref7356:Moran et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 delta leuB recombinant FliC FSH beta vaccine
c_description: This vaccine candidate is a Brucella abortus strain RB51 with a leuB gene deletion expressing Salmonella typhimurium FliC protein conjugated to porcine follicle stimulating hormone beta subunit (FSHβ) DNA sequences, designed as an immunocontraceptive and protective vaccine. Efficacy: Significant reduction in fertility characteristics observed in both male and female mice. [Ref7338:Waldrop et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 ΔleuB genetically engineered to express Salmonella FliC conjugated to FSHβ DNA sequences. [Ref7338:Waldrop et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BLS recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) antigen to goats. Efficacy: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher interferon-γ production compared to vector control; reduced Brucella colonization in tissues; decreased Brucella antigen expression in spleen, kidney, and lymph nodes; amelioration of brucellosis-related histopathological lesions. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific immune response including increased interferon-γ production. [Ref7340:Leya et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain expressing BLS at 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL in 1 mL. [Ref7340:Leya et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella outer-membrane protein 19 (Omp19) antigen to goats. c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis IFITM3 exosome subunit vaccine
c_description: This study investigated the immune function of extracellular IFITM3 protein in the process of Brucella infection, focusing on exosomes secreted by macrophages infected with Brucella melitensis strain M5. Efficacy: Immunization with IFITM3-containing exosomes decreased mouse spleen tissue damage and spleen CFU, establishing an anti-Brucella state in mice. Immune response: Exosomes transmitted IFITM3 protein from cell to cell, effectively inhibiting intracellular survival of Brucella. [Ref7341:Yi et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Exosomes carrying IFITM3 protein derived from Brucella M5-infected macrophages. [Ref7341:Yi et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Omp16 PEDV vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A novel recombinant Lactobacillus casei strain expressing PEDVS protein of PEDV and OMP16 protein of Brucella abortus strain was constructed as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: The vaccine induced higher levels of humoral, cellular, and mucosal immunity compared to other recombinant protein controls. Immune response: Elevated serum IgG, neutralizing antibodies, IL-4, IL-10, INF-γ, and fecal IgA indicated strong humoral, cellular, and mucosal immune responses. [Ref7342:Li et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactobacillus casei expressing OMP16 and PEDVS proteins. [Ref7342:Li et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp22 Omp19 Omp28 multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: This study designed a safe and effective multi-epitope vaccine based on dominant T and B cell epitopes of Brucella outer membrane proteins Omp22, Omp19, and Omp28 using bioinformatics methods. [Ref7343:Chen et al, 2021]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct combined T/B dominant epitopes of Omp22, Omp19, and Omp28 linked by HEYGAALEREAG and GGGS linkers, with carrier sequences linked at the N- and C-termini via EAAAK linkers; the tertiary structure and physicochemical properties were analyzed in silico. [Ref7343:Chen et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella Omp25 FMDV VP1 sheeppox virus strain NISKHI vector vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate attenuated sheep pox virus strain NISKHI as a vector expressing foreign genes including Brucella spp. OMP25 and FMDV VP1. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the recombinant virus elicited specific antibodies against both sheep pox virus and the foreign antigens VP1 and OMP25. Immune response: Specific antibody responses to sheep pox virus and foreign proteins VP1 and OMP25 were induced in immunized mice. [Ref7344:Chervyakova et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Recombinant sheep pox viruses with deletions in ribonucleotide kinase (SPPV020) and thymidine kinase (SPPV066) genes were engineered to express enhanced green fluorescent protein, VP1, and OMP25 using integration plasmids and transient dominant selection. [Ref7344:Chervyakova et al, 2021]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; lamb testicles cells; bovine kidney cells; saiga kidney cells; porcine kidney cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HlyD subunit vaccine
c_description: HlyD was selected as a conserved antigen candidate from compositive reverse vaccinology screening Efficacy: HlyD substantially reduced the organ bacterial load of B. abortus S19 in mice and provided varying degrees of protection Immune response: Induced specific humoral and cellular immune responses [Ref7345:Zai et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus VirB8 subunit vaccine
c_description: VirB8 was selected as a conserved antigen candidate from compositive reverse vaccinology screening Efficacy: VirB8 substantially reduced the organ bacterial load of B. abortus S19 in mice and provided varying degrees of protection Immune response: Induced specific humoral and cellular immune responses [Ref7345:Zai et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain znBAZ vaccine
c_description: The live, double-mutant B. abortus (znBAZ) strain was used for mucosal vaccination to induce protection against pulmonary challenge with wild-type Brucella. Efficacy: The znBAZ strain resulted in nearly complete protection of mice against pulmonary challenge with wild-type Brucella, associated with a dominant CD8+ T cell response; NK cell depletion impaired dendritic cell activation and migration and reduced CD8+ T cell numbers threefold. Immune response: znBAZ induced up to a 5-fold increase in IFN-γ-producing NK cells in mouse lungs, with increased expression of CXCR3, Ki67, NKp46, and granzyme B, and decreased NKG2A; lung caspase-1+ inflammatory monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages secreted chemokines and cytokines recruiting and activating NK cells; IL-18 neutralization reduced early NK cell response; NK cells influenced lung dendritic cell activation and migration to lymph nodes, promoting protective CD8+ T cell development. [Ref7348:Bhagyaraj et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed by selecting 19 T and B cell epitopes from immunogenic antigens identified by 2D gel electrophoresis, MALDI-TOF, and literature; epitopes ligated with linkers and gene synthesized. Efficacy: Recombinant MEL protein induced immune responses equal to Rev. 1 vaccine in secretion of IFNγ, IL-2, and specific IgG; significant spleen cell proliferation compared to PBS control. Immune response: High IL-2 levels indicating cellular immunity activation; stimulation of both humoral and cellular-mediated immune responses against Brucella melitensis. [Ref7349:Saadat et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Recombinant polypeptide expressed in E. coli BL21, purified and mixed with chitin adjuvant for subcutaneous injection. [Ref7349:Saadat et al, 2021]
c_antigen: multi-epitope protein composed of 19 T and B cell epitopes

c_vaccine_name: 7α-HSDH protein vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated 7α-HSDH antigen as a safer vaccine candidate compared to commercial live vaccines. Efficacy: Protein with poly I:C induced higher protection than protein alone and similar protection to live attenuated vaccines. Immune response: Induced strong IgG with predominant IgG2a, high IgG2a/IgG1 ratio, splenocyte proliferation, and IL-2 and IFN-γ production indicating Th1 immune response. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Recombinant 7α-HSDH protein formulated with poly I:C adjuvant or as naked protein. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: BhuA protein vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safer and more effective vaccine alternative to commercial live vaccines by evaluating BhuA antigen with or without adjuvant. Efficacy: Immunization with BhuA protein plus poly I:C induced higher protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus than protein alone and comparable protection to live attenuated vaccines. Immune response: Induced vigorous IgG with predominant IgG2a, high IgG2a/IgG1 ratio, splenocyte proliferation, and production of IL-2 and IFN-γ indicating a Th1-oriented cellular immune response. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Recombinant BhuA protein formulated with poly I:C adjuvant or as naked protein. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: FliC protein vaccine
c_description: The study tested FliC antigen as a potential safer vaccine candidate against brucellosis. Efficacy: FliC protein plus poly I:C provided higher protection than protein alone and comparable to live attenuated vaccines. Immune response: Induced vigorous IgG with predominant IgG2a, high IgG2a/IgG1 ratio, splenocyte proliferation, and IL-2 and IFN-γ production indicating a Th1-biased immune response. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Recombinant FliC protein with or without poly I:C adjuvant. [Ref7350:Sadeghi et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 bacterial ghost vaccine
c_description: The study developed a Brucella abortus A19 bacterial ghost vaccine using a double inactivation strategy combining biological lysis and hydrogen peroxide treatment to ensure complete inactivation and safety. Efficacy: Immunization with A19BG conferred a similar level of protection as the existing A19 vaccine against Brucella melitensis M28 in both guinea pigs and cattle. Immune response: Vaccinated guinea pigs showed antibody levels, interferon-γ, interleukin-4, and CD4+ T cell responses comparable to those induced by the existing A19 vaccine; no adverse reactions were observed. [Ref7352:He et al, 2022]
c_preparation: The vaccine was prepared by sequential biological lysis and hydrogen peroxide treatment resulting in bacterial ghosts with typical morphology and genetic stability. [Ref7352:He et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was designed based on a putative immunogenic epitope of the apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase (Int), identified as the target of a highly expressed small RNA during early infection of bone marrow-derived macrophages. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed reduced viable bacterial counts in liver, spleen, and axillary lymph nodes compared to non-vaccinated controls; reduced number and size of granulomas in liver. Immune response: Increased production of IgG and its fractions; elevated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-6, followed by anti-inflammatory IL-10 and TGF-β in liver; BMDMs stimulated with splenocyte supernatants showed increased CD86 expression, higher iNOS levels, and increased nitric oxide production, indicating enhanced phagocytic and microbicidal activity. [Ref7354:Oliveira et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Epitope-based subunit vaccine selected by immunoinformatic analysis; details on formulation or adjuvant not reported. [Ref7354:Oliveira et al, 2021]
c_model_host: Mus musculus (C57BL/6 mice); bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase spike receptor binding domain subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was designed by covalently coupling the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein to the multimeric Lumazine Synthase protein from Brucella abortus to increase immunogenicity. Efficacy: Particles with a high RBD to BLS ratio (6-7 RBD molecules per BLS decamer) elicited significantly higher humoral immune responses and high titers of neutralizing IgGs compared to RBD alone or particles with lower RBD to BLS ratios. Immune response: High titer neutralizing IgG antibodies were induced by multimeric RBD-BLS particles with a high number of RBD copies, indicating enhanced antigen presentation and immunogenicity. [Ref7355:Argentinian, 2022]
c_preparation: Multimeric particles produced by transpeptidation reaction between RBD expressed in Pichia pastoris and Brucella abortus Lumazine Synthase (BLS), forming decameric 170 kDa particles with varying RBD to BLS ratios. [Ref7355:Argentinian, 2022]
c_antigen: Lumazine Synthase; Spike receptor binding domain (RBD)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 OMP22 OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Four recombinant proteins (L7/L12, OMP22, OMP25, OMP31) were cloned, expressed, purified, and combined as a subunit vaccine to evaluate protective efficiency against B. abortus infection. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccine induced significantly higher protection in mice against brucellosis compared to single subunit vaccines and showed protection comparable to the RB51 vaccine. Immune response: Immunization induced a T-helper-1-dominated immune response characterized by high IFN-γ and IL-2 production, low IL-10 levels, and elevated IgG2a titers relative to IgG1. The recombinant proteins reacted specifically with Brucella-positive serum. [Ref7357:Li et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Combined subunit vaccine composed of four recombinant Brucella abortus proteins. [Ref7357:Li et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis hdeA deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study also evaluated a hdeA deletion mutant and a double mucR and hdeA deletion mutant of Brucella ovis PA. Efficacy: Deletion of hdeA alone did not modify evaluated properties; however, the double mutant showed attenuation and persistence similar to mucR single mutant, supporting evaluation as attenuated vaccine candidates. [Ref7358:Tartilán-Choya et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis PA strain with hdeA gene deletion; also combined with mucR deletion. [Ref7358:Tartilán-Choya et al, 2021]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis mucR deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study constructed and characterized a mucR deletion mutant of virulent Brucella ovis PA, which affects surface properties and virulence. Efficacy: The mucR deletion mutants showed virulence attenuation but established persistent splenic infection in mice, suggesting potential as specific attenuated vaccines against Brucella ovis. [Ref7358:Tartilán-Choya et al, 2021]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis PA strain with mucR gene deletion; also studied a double mutant with hdeA deletion. [Ref7358:Tartilán-Choya et al, 2021]
c_antigen: mucR deletion mutant; hdeA deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Recombinant Brucella abortus RB51 vaccine expressing listeriolysin O, BAX, and SMAC
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The RB51 strain is a live attenuated vaccine with low side effects but insufficient protective efficacy. To enhance efficacy and safety, RB51 was genetically modified to express Listeria monocytogenes listeriolysin O (LLO), and apoptotic proteins BAX and SMAC. Efficacy: Recombinant RB51 strains expressing mLLO and BAX-SMAC showed higher cytotoxicity, reduced macrophage survival, and increased apoptosis and necrosis compared to parental RB51. Vaccination with RB51-mLLO-BAX-SMAC enhanced Th1 immune response in mice, indicating improved potency. Immune response: Enhanced T cell-mediated immunity, primarily through bacterial endosome escape and antigen cross-priming, leading to increased IFN-γ production and a stronger Th1 response, potentially improving safety and efficacy of the vaccine candidate. [Ref7359:Sarmadi et al, 2022]
c_preparation: RB51 was transformed with two broad-host-range plasmids: pbbr1ori-LLO containing LLO, and pBlu-mLLO-BAX-SMAC containing mutant LLO and BAX-SMAC fusion gene, generating recombinant RB51 strains. [Ref7359:Sarmadi et al, 2022]
c_antigen: listeriolysin O (LLO); mutant LLO (mLLO); BAX; SMAC
c_model_host: Mus musculus; J774A.1 murine macrophage-like cell line; BALB/c mice

c_vaccine_name: live B. abortus A19 strain vaccine
c_description: The live B. abortus A19 strain vaccine is a widespread vaccine in China but has residual virulence concerns. Efficacy: The combined low dose live vaccine plus inactivated vaccine group showed splenic bacterial burden and spleen weight equivalent to the high dose live vaccine group; both conferred protective immunity against B. abortus strain 2308 challenge. Immune response: The combined vaccine group elicited Brucella-specific serum IgG, IFN-γ, IL-4, and CD4+ and CD8+ T cell percentages similar to the high dose live vaccine group, indicating comparable cellular and humoral immune responses. [Ref7360:He et al, 2022a]
c_preparation: Live B. abortus A19 strain at 10^5 CFU/mL (low dose) or 10^6 CFU/mL (high dose) was used alone or combined with inactivated B. abortus A19 strain at 10^9 CFU/mL. [Ref7360:He et al, 2022a]

c_vaccine_name: oral S2-Ag85 DNA vaccine
c_description: The oral S2-Ag85 vaccine has been shown to protect the human body and effectively improve the titration of the vaccine by acting on intestinal mucosa cells and enhancing their immunogenicity. Efficacy: The S2-Ag85A vaccine was effective in activating dsDNA and RNA transduction pathways in intestinal cells and improving intestinal antigen presentation in mice. Immune response: Activation of dsDNA and RNA sensor pathways (RIG-1, Pol III, DAI, STING, AIM2, IRF3, IRF7) in intestinal cells leading to enhanced antigen presentation. [Ref7361:Sheng et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Recombinant S2-Ag85 DNA vaccine administered orally. [Ref7361:Sheng et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine was designed using reverse vaccinology from Omp10, Omp25, Omp31, and BtpB proteins to prevent Brucella infection, addressing the difficulty of eliminating Brucella with current medical treatments. Efficacy: Animal experiments demonstrated high immunogenicity of the MEV. Immune response: The MEV elicited a strong immune response as indicated by high immunogenicity in animal models. [Ref7362:Li et al, 2022a]
c_preparation: The vaccine peptide contains 806 amino acids, linking CTL, HTL, and B cell epitopes with AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers respectively; supplemented at the N-terminal with adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. [Ref7362:Li et al, 2022a]
c_antigen: Omp10, Omp25, Omp31, BtpB; 13 CTL epitopes, 17 HTL epitopes, 9 linear B cell epitopes, 2 conformational B cell epitopes

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 wzm deletion vaccine
c_description: The study constructed wzm/wzt single- and double-deletion mutants using the attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 as the parental strain to investigate the biological implications of the Wzm/Wzt system and its potential as a vaccine. Efficacy: Rev1Δwzm mutant was highly attenuated yet immunogenic and effective as a vaccine against Brucella melitensis and Brucella ovis in mice; it showed low persistence but maintained efficacy. Immune response: Rev1Δwzm induced protective immunity without causing infection in mouse placentas and was safe in pregnant ewes, with minimal serological interference in sheep. [Ref7363:Mena-Bueno et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with wzm gene deletion. [Ref7363:Mena-Bueno et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BtpA Omp16 Omp28 virB10 Omp25 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study designed a multiepitope peptide-based vaccine targeting IFN-γ epitopes, T cell cytotoxicity, and T lymphocytes using antigens BtpA, Omp16, Omp28, virB10, Omp25, and Omp31 from B. melitensis, B. abortus, and B. suis. Immune response: The vaccine is predicted to stimulate immune responses in B and T cells and potentially prevent infection by B. suis, B. abortus, and B. melitensis. [Ref7364:Tarrahimofrad et al, 2022]
c_adjuvant: yes; PADRE sequence as Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) and TLR4 agonist
c_preparation: The vaccine construct included 389 amino acids linked by AAY, GPGPG, and EAAAK peptides, incorporated the PADRE sequence as a TLR2 and TLR4 agonist, resulting in a soluble, nonallergenic, antigenic protein of 41.3 kDa. [Ref7364:Tarrahimofrad et al, 2022]
c_antigen: BtpA; Omp16; Omp28; virB10; Omp25; Omp31

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 brucellaphage-treated vaccine
c_description: The live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 organisms commonly used as a vaccine were employed to deliver a broad acting lytic brucellaphage inside phagocytes in vivo to reach virulent Brucella hiding intracellularly. Efficacy: The phage pulsed vaccine induced sustained and significantly high titers of anti-Brucella antibodies compared with untreated animals and animals vaccinated with S19 vaccine alone. Immune response: Induction of specific and sustained high titers of anti-Brucella antibodies measured by multiple serological assays. [Ref7365:Mohan et al, 2020]
c_preparation: Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine pulsed with lytic brucellaphage (phage pulsed vaccine preparation). [Ref7365:Mohan et al, 2020]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain znBM-mC vaccine
c_description: A novel live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain znBM-mC was developed and characterized for immunity. Efficacy: Vaccination conferred nearly complete protection in lungs and spleens from Brucella colonization; full protection observed in CD4-/-, CD8-/-, and wild-type mice; partial protection in IL-17-/- mice (lungs protected, spleen not). Immune response: Vaccination induced a strong IFN-γ+ CD8+ T-cell bias in lungs, with large increases in lung CD4+ and CD8+ effector memory and resident memory T cells producing IFN-γ; TNF-α and IL-17 also increased, with IL-17 mainly from CD4+ T cells; IFN-γ was essential for vaccine clearance. [Ref7366:Goodwin et al, 2022]
c_preparation: Administered via an oral prime followed by an intranasal boost. [Ref7366:Goodwin et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis BepC multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed a novel chimeric multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) construct based on immunoinformatic prediction of antigenic proteins from the whole proteome of Brucella suis using subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology approaches. Efficacy: Computational analyses suggest the MEV is highly antigenic, non-toxic, non-allergenic, flexible, stable, and soluble, with strong predicted interactions with TLR4 and HLAs, supporting its potential efficacy against Brucella suis infections. Immune response: Predicted to induce T-cell and B-cell immune responses through selected epitopes and enhanced by TLR4 agonist adjuvant; binding to human TLR4 and HLAs indicates potential to stimulate innate and adaptive immunity. [Ref7368:Jalal et al, 2023]
c_preparation: The MEV construct of 324 amino acids was created by linking six MHC I, ten MHC II, and four B-cell epitopes with appropriate linkers and combined with the TLR4 agonist HBHA protein as an adjuvant to boost immune response. [Ref7368:Jalal et al, 2023]
c_antigen: Multidrug efflux Resistance-nodulation-division (RND) transporter outer membrane subunit (gene BepC); T-cell and B-cell epitopes (six MHC I, ten MHC II, four B-cell epitopes)

c_vaccine_name: live-attenuated Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine (S2) adjuvanted with Ag85a
c_description:
A live-attenuated Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine (S2) was developed and adjuvanted with Ag85a to enhance immune responses and provide a candidate vaccine for preventing Brucella pathogens from livestock, potentially reducing dosage and toxicity compared to S2 alone. Efficacy: Ag85a-S2 triggered a stronger cellular immune response compared to S2 alone, with enhanced induction of interferon and other cytokines dependent on the cGAS-STING pathway. Immune response: Ag85a-S2 activated the cGAS-STING signaling pathway, leading to increased abundance of interferon and other cytokines; cGAS knockout significantly downregulated these responses, indicating partial dependence on this pathway for immune enhancement. [Ref7369:Dang et al, 2022]
This study used Antigen 85A (Ag85A) as a carrier fused with the Brucella S2 vaccine to reduce toxicity and enhance protective effect. Efficacy: The S2-Ag85A vaccine effectively reduced toxicity residue of the S2 vaccine and enhanced protective ability against Brucella infection in mice. Immune response: The vaccine stimulated higher immunogenic response with increased expression of Brucella heterozygous IgG1 and IgG2a; significantly increased IFN-γ expression in serum and spleen; significantly reduced IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, indicating induction of IFN-γ and downregulation of proinflammatory cytokines. [Ref7371:Zhang et al, 2022]
c_preparation:
Live-attenuated Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine combined with Ag85a as an adjuvant [Ref7369:Dang et al, 2022]
Oral live attenuated vaccine combining Brucella S2 strain with Ag85A as a carrier. [Ref7371:Zhang et al, 2022]
c_model_host: intestinal mucosal cells in vivo; bone marrow derived macrophages (BMDM); U937 cell line; Mus musculus

c_vaccine_name: Brucella AtpA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. Immune response: Expression of inflammatory cytokines IL1B and IFN-γ was significantly altered in infected mouse spleens; identified peptides could bind MHC molecules and potentially stimulate memory T cell activation and immune responses. [Ref7370:Pei et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella AtpD subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. Immune response: Expression of inflammatory cytokines IL1B and IFN-γ was significantly altered in infected mouse spleens; identified peptides could bind MHC molecules and potentially stimulate memory T cell activation and immune responses. [Ref7370:Pei et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BAbS19_II02030 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. Immune response: Expression of inflammatory cytokines IL1B and IFN-γ was significantly altered in infected mouse spleens; identified peptides could bind MHC molecules and potentially stimulate memory T cell activation and immune responses. [Ref7370:Pei et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella DnaK subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. Immune response: Expression of inflammatory cytokines IL1B and IFN-γ was significantly altered in infected mouse spleens; identified peptides could bind MHC molecules and potentially stimulate memory T cell activation and immune responses. [Ref7370:Pei et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope subunit vaccine associated with LPS loaded chitosan nanoparticle
c_description: The study evaluated multi-epitope antigens associated with LPS loaded chitosan (LLC) or mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle (MCN) as adjuvants and delivery systems to enhance immune responses against Brucella infection. Efficacy: Vaccine candidates containing mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles provided a high percentage of protection against Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus infection. Immune response: Formulations with mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles significantly elicited IFN-γ and IL-2 cytokines and antibody titers, inducing a Th1 immune response. Both LLC and MCN formulations induced Th1 responses. [Ref7372:Sadeghi et al, 2023]
c_adjuvant: yes; mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle; LPS loaded chitosan
c_preparation: Multi-epitope antigens were formulated with either LPS loaded chitosan nanoparticles or mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles. [Ref7372:Sadeghi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope subunit vaccine associated with mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle
c_description: Supporting publication [Ref7372:Sadeghi et al, 2023]
c_adjuvant: yes; mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle; LPS loaded chitosan

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis rBtuB Hia FlgK subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the goat Th1/Th2 immune response to a cocktail of three Brucella melitensis peptides (rBtuB-Hia-FlgK) previously shown to induce antigen-specific immune responses in rodent models. Efficacy: The peptide cocktail induced an increase in CD4+/CD8+ T cells starting at day 15 and persisting to day 80. IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2 mRNA expression were induced by day 15, with IFN-γ levels maintained at day 80. Although IFN-γ production was lower than that induced by Rev-1 at day 15, this may be due to sampling timing. Immune response: The vaccine induced a Th1-type cellular immune response characterized by increased CD4+/CD8+ T cell proliferation and production of Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2), similar to the response induced by the live attenuated Rev-1 vaccine. The results suggest the peptide cocktail can induce cellular immunity comparable to an attenuated vaccine. [Ref7373:De et al, 2023]
c_preparation: A cocktail of three peptides (rBtuB, Hia, FlgK) from Brucella melitensis was used; adjuvant was included but not specified. [Ref7373:De et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp19 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a potential recombinant vaccine candidate using the 19 kDa outer membrane protein (OMP19) of Brucella melitensis strain H38, targeting all Brucella infections, especially in humans and pregnant animals. Efficacy: The recombinant OMP19 antigen showed similar immunogenic power to the commercially available recombinant protein in the mouse model. [Ref7374:Uslu et al, 2022]
c_preparation: OMP19 gene was amplified and cloned into the pETSUMO vector system to produce purified recombinant OMP19 antigen. [Ref7374:Uslu et al, 2022]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16M delta wzm vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the biological properties and safety of a Brucella melitensis 16MΔwzm in-frame deletion mutant as a vaccine candidate, focusing on its use in pregnant mice and sheep. Efficacy: In mice, 16MΔwzm prevented placental and fetal infections and protected against Brucella melitensis and Brucella ovis infections. Efficacy in the natural host (sheep) remains to be confirmed. Immune response: Vaccination induced transient Rose Bengal serological reactions, stronger and earlier in pregnant ewes; seroconversion in smooth and rough LPS tests was observed at parturition in some ewes, especially after subcutaneous vaccination. [Ref7375:Zabalza-Baranguá et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16M strain with an in-frame deletion of the wzm gene, administered by subcutaneous or conjunctival routes. [Ref7375:Zabalza-Baranguá et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-antigen subunit vaccine via Escherichia coli
c_description: A bioconjugate vaccine against Brucella abortus was developed using engineered Escherichia coli as a safer chassis to produce the vaccine, overcoming pathogenicity issues of Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 used previously. Efficacy: The bioconjugate vaccine provided protective roles against both lethal and non-lethal challenges of Brucella abortus A19 strain.
