Immune response: The vaccine effectively evoked humoral immune responses and induced production of specific antibodies against Brucella abortus A19 lipopolysaccharide. [Ref7376:Li et al, 2023]
c_preparation: The vaccine was prepared by modularizing and reassembling the O-polysaccharide (OPS) gene cluster of Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 in E. coli, followed by protein glycosylation using the PglL system to create the bioconjugate vaccine. [Ref7376:Li et al, 2023]
c_antigen: O-antigen polysaccharide from Yersinia enterocolitica O:9; protein glycosylation system (PglL system)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp19 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify multi-epitope vaccine candidates based on the outer membrane protein Omp19 of Brucella, which is widely expressed, highly conserved, and immunogenic. Immune response: Potential B cell and T cell epitopes of Omp19 were identified as vaccine candidates, laying the foundation for further multi-epitope vaccine design. [Ref7378:Shi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25 multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify multi-epitope vaccine candidates based on the outer membrane protein Omp25 of Brucella, which is widely expressed, highly conserved, and immunogenic. Immune response: Potential B cell and T cell epitopes of Omp25 were identified as vaccine candidates, laying the foundation for further multi-epitope vaccine design. [Ref7378:Shi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Lactococcus lactis-pNZ8148-BLS-Usp45 vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to develop a recombinant Lactococcus lactis live vector secreting Brucella abortus lumazine synthase (BLS) protein as a potential oral vaccine against brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant BLS-specific IgG1 and IgG2a antibody responses compared to controls; increased levels of IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, and IL-10 cytokines were observed; vaccinated mice exhibited less severe spleen injuries and reduced inflammatory damage. Immune response: The vaccine induced both humoral (IgG1, IgG2a) and cellular immune responses (elevated IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, IL-10), indicating balanced Th1 and Th2 immunity and reduced inflammatory pathology in spleen tissue. [Ref7379:Fatehi et al, 2023]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing and secreting the BLS protein, delivered orally. [Ref7379:Fatehi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus smooth lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Quillaja saponin adjuvant
c_description: The vaccine candidate combines Brucella abortus S19 smooth lipopolysaccharide with Quillaja saponin to create a green vaccine aimed at mucosal brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccination conferred significant protection with a 130-fold reduction in lung bacterial burden and a 55.74-fold reduction in spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS controls. Immune response: Induced secretion of IgA and IgG1 in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid; systemic mixed IgG1/IgG2a response indicating both Th1 and Th2 activation, with predominance of IgG1. [Ref7380:Abushahba et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Two doses of sLPS combined with Quillaja saponin administered intranasally. [Ref7380:Abushahba et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus smooth lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Quillaja saponin-Xyloglucan mix adjuvant
c_description: The vaccine candidate combines Brucella abortus S19 smooth lipopolysaccharide with a Quillaja saponin and Xyloglucan mix to create a green vaccine aimed at mucosal brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccination resulted in the highest reduction in splenic Brucella loads with a 364.6-fold decrease in bacterial titer compared to non-vaccinated animals. Immune response: Induced secretion of IgA and IgG1 in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid; systemic mixed IgG1/IgG2a response indicating both Th1 and Th2 activation, with predominance of IgG1. [Ref7380:Abushahba et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Two doses of sLPS combined with Quillaja saponin-Xyloglucan mix administered intranasally. [Ref7380:Abushahba et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella outer-membrane vesicles and outer-membrane vesicle-associated proteins subunit vaccine
c_description: Existing Brucella vaccines are attenuated and can cause vaccine-associated brucellosis; subunit vaccines are safer but poorly immunogenic; LDH was added as an adjuvant to enhance immune response. Efficacy: LDH subunit vaccine induced higher specific antibody levels and Th1-type immune responses compared to Freund's adjuvant; mice had significantly lower splenic bacterial loads; LDH-OMV vaccine provided higher protection against Brucella infection. Immune response: Induced mainly T-helper 1 (Th1)-type immune responses with high levels of specific IgG antibodies and increased CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. [Ref7382:Deng et al, 2023]
c_preparation: LDH combined with Brucella outer-membrane vesicles and OMV-associated proteins to form a subunit vaccine. [Ref7382:Deng et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis pgm gene deletion vaccine
c_description: A novel highly attenuated vaccine strain constructed by clean deletion of the phosphoglucomutase (pgm) gene, which is involved in biosynthesis of polysaccharides including O-antigen and cyclic beta glucans. Efficacy: The vaccine confers excellent levels of protection against B. melitensis in mice and cross protection against B. abortus and B. suis. Immune response: Vaccination induces a robust memory cellular immune response but no antibody production against the O-antigen. [Ref7383:Czibener et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with pgm gene deletion. [Ref7383:Czibener et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 and OmpA subunit vaccine
c_description: Exosomes secreted by Brucella melitensis M5-infected macrophages (Exo-M5) were extracted and identified to study their role in immune activation and macrophage polarization. Efficacy: Exo-M5 promoted M1 macrophage polarization, induced secretion of M1 cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ), inhibited M2 cytokine (IL-10), reduced intracellular Brucella survival, increased IgG2a antibody release, protected mice from Brucella infection, and reduced spleen parasitaemia. Immune response: Activation of NF-κB signaling pathways, promotion of M1 macrophage polarization, increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IFN-γ, decreased IL-10 secretion, and enhanced IgG2a antibody production. [Ref7384:Wang et al, 2023a]
c_preparation: Exosomes carrying Brucella antigen components including Omp31 and OmpA derived from infected macrophages. [Ref7384:Wang et al, 2023a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description:
The study developed a novel oral antigen delivery system using Lactococcus lactis transformed with a plasmid encoding the Brucella abortus omp25 antigen to target mucosal immunity. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant omp25-specific IgG1 antibody production, increased IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-4, and IL-10 cytokine levels, and reduced spleen injury, alveolar edema, lymphocyte infiltration, and morphological damage compared to controls, indicating protective potential. Immune response: Induction of both humoral (serum IgG1 and mucosal sIgA) and cellular immune responses (elevated IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-4, IL-10) was observed, suggesting a balanced Th1/Th2 response following oral vaccination with the recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing omp25. [Ref7385:Gouran et al, 2023]
Brucellosis is a widespread zoonosis lacking safe and efficient vaccines; capripoxviruses have emerged as promising vaccine vectors for delivering foreign antigens. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed a significant reduction in bacterial load in the spleen after challenge, indicating partial protection. Immune response: Immunization elicited a robust Brucella-specific IgG response and stimulated a balanced Th1 (IFN-γ, IL-2) and Th2 (IL-4, IL-5) cytokine profile. [Ref7454:Wang et al, 2026]
c_preparation:
Oral vaccination with Lactococcus lactis transformed with pNZ8148 plasmid encoding omp25 (pNZ8148:omp25); control groups included free pNZ8148 and phosphate-buffered saline. [Ref7385:Gouran et al, 2023]
A recombinant goatpox virus expressing the Brucella outer membrane protein 25 (rGTPV-OMP25). [Ref7454:Wang et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b Omp31 CTLA-4 variable region fusion vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to improve safety and immune protection of Brucella vaccines by designing a fusion vaccine using bioinformatics approaches, linking Omp2b and Omp31 proteins and fusing the CTLA-4 variable region to the N-terminal of the epitope sequence. Efficacy: The designed fusion vaccine showed high potency against Brucella based on bioinformatics analyses. Immune response: The fusion protein vaccine had strong predicted affinity with B7-1 and B7-2, suggesting potential to enhance immune response via CTLA-4 interaction. [Ref7386:Guo et al, 2023]
c_preparation: A fusion protein vaccine was designed by sequentially linking Omp2b and Omp31 proteins and fusing the CTLA-4 variable region at the N-terminal; molecular docking showed strong affinity with B7-1 and B7-2. [Ref7386:Guo et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus mutant A19mut2 vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate A19mut2 was developed by replacing the formyltransferase gene wbkC in Brucella abortus A19 with the acetyltransferase gene wbdR from E. coli O157, resulting in a modified O-polysaccharide that does not induce antibodies against wild-type Brucella LPS, enabling DIVA (Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals) capability. Efficacy: A19mut2 showed decreased residual virulence compared to A19 but induced significant humoral and cellular immune responses similar to A19; protection efficacy against B. abortus S2308 NalR infection was comparable to A19 immunization. Immune response: Induced significant humoral immunity (IgG and subtypes) and cellular immunity (IFN-γ and IL10 cytokine release) in vaccinated mice; antibodies induced by A19mut2 did not cross-react with wild-type LPS, allowing serological differentiation. [Ref7387:Abdelgawad et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with modified lipopolysaccharide due to gene replacement. [Ref7387:Abdelgawad et al, 2023]
c_antigen: wbkC gene replaced by wbdR gene (modified O-polysaccharide)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB8 and VirB10 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine was designed targeting antigenic epitopes of the Brucella type IV secretion system proteins VirB8 and VirB10 to address the need for improved prevention and treatment of brucellosis, especially in humans where no vaccine currently exists. Efficacy: Not experimentally tested; in silico immune simulation suggested the vaccine construct may help initiate cellular and humoral immunity in brucellosis patients. Immune response: The vaccine construct showed potential to induce both cellular and humoral immune responses based on immune simulation results. [Ref7388:Yin et al, 2023]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct was composed of 2 cytotoxic T lymphocyte epitopes, 9 helper T lymphocyte epitopes, 6 linear B cell epitopes, and 6 conformational B cell epitopes spliced together with different linkers to form a multi-epitope vaccine. [Ref7388:Yin et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: L. lactis-pNZ8148-BAB1-0278-Usp45 vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A vector vaccine against brucellosis was developed using recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Brucella outer membrane protein BAB1-0278. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly higher total IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a levels compared to PBS controls; increased cytokine production (IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, IL-10); and reduced inflammatory response, morphological impairment, alveolar edema, and lymphocyte infiltration in spleen tissue. Immune response: The vaccine induced both humoral (IgG subclasses) and cellular immunity (increased cytokines IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, IL-10), along with enhanced lymphocyte proliferation and modulation of innate immune markers. [Ref7389:Kazemi et al, 2023]
c_preparation: The BAB1-0278 gene was cloned into the pNZ8148 vector, transformed into L. lactis, and the target protein was extracted and confirmed by SDS-PAGE and western blot. [Ref7389:Kazemi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multi-epitope subunit vaccine fused to IgG Fc
c_description: The vaccine was designed using an immunoinformatics approach to identify and analyze antigenic epitopes of Brucella abortus, including epitopes recognized by cytotoxic T cells, T helper cells, and B cells. Molecular adjuvants human β-defensins 3 and PADRE were added at the N-terminus, and a mouse IgG Fc fragment was fused at the C-terminus to enhance immunogenicity, creating the MEV-Fc vaccine. Efficacy: Immunosimulation predicted strong cellular and humoral immune responses induced by the MEV-Fc vaccine. Immune response: Predicted strong activation of both cellular immunity (cytotoxic T cells and T helper cells) and humoral immunity (B cells and antibody production). [Ref7390:Wu et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Chimeric peptide vaccine composed of multiple linked epitopes with molecular adjuvants (hBD-3 and PADRE) at the N-terminus and fused to mouse IgG Fc at the C-terminus. [Ref7390:Wu et al, 2023]
c_antigen: multiple epitopes recognized by cytotoxic T cells, T helper cells, and B cells; fused to IgG Fc fragment

c_vaccine_name: Brucella O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study developed a high-performance bioconjugate nanovaccine by introducing a self-assembly nanoparticle platform and an O-linked glycosylation system into Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9, which has an O-polysaccharide composed of the same unit as Brucella. Efficacy: The nanovaccine provided cross-protection against B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis lethal dose challenges and improved clearance of B. melitensis in non-lethal infection. Immune response: The vaccine greatly promoted antibody responses in mice, with a more pronounced increase in IgG2a than IgG1. [Ref7391:Huang et al, 2023]
c_preparation: A self-assembled bioconjugate nanovaccine coupling polysaccharide antigens with nano carriers was prepared and confirmed stable. [Ref7391:Huang et al, 2023]
c_antigen: O-polysaccharide from Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 Omp25 Omp28 recombinant subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to design a recombinant vaccine containing potential immunogenic epitopes against Brucella melitensis using immunoinformatics approaches. The vaccine candidate was designed to be expressed as recombinant antigens in E. coli, with in silico simulation indicating high expression levels. Efficacy: The designed vaccine showed high quality and acceptable physicochemical properties with predicted ability to induce humoral and cellular immune responses against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: High expression level of recombinant antigens predicted in E. coli host. Immune response: The vaccine is predicted to induce both humoral and cellular immune responses based on epitope analysis and immunoinformatics predictions. [Ref7392:Hashemzadeh et al, 2023]
c_preparation:
The vaccine was designed as a multi-epitope recombinant subunit vaccine combining epitopes from Omp31, Omp25, and Omp28 antigens joined by flexible linkers; codon optimization for expression in E. coli was performed in silico. [Ref7392:Hashemzadeh et al, 2023]
Multi-epitope recombinant subunit vaccine with codon optimization for E. coli expression. [Ref7392:Hashemzadeh et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Bp26 Omp31 subunit vaccine with aluminum hydroxide adjuvant
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate immune responses induced by a chimeric protein consisting of trigger factor, Bp26, and Omp31 loaded on aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles as an adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice with AH/TBO nanoparticles showed a higher reduction of bacterial culture after challenge compared to Se/TBO nanoparticles and TBO alone. Immune response: Significant IgG responses against the chimeric antigen were induced; IgG2a/IgG1 ratio indicated a T-helper type 1 immune response. [Ref7393:Goudarzi et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein (TBO) loaded onto aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles (~60 nm size) administered subcutaneously. [Ref7393:Goudarzi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Bp26 Omp31 subunit vaccine with selenium nanoparticle adjuvant
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate immune responses induced by a chimeric protein consisting of trigger factor, Bp26, and Omp31 loaded on selenium nanoparticles as an adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice with Se/TBO nanoparticles showed reduction of bacterial culture after challenge, but less than AH/TBO nanoparticles. Immune response: Significant IgG responses against the chimeric antigen were induced; IgG2a/IgG1 ratio indicated a T-helper type 1 immune response. [Ref7393:Goudarzi et al, 2023]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein (TBO) loaded onto selenium nanoparticles (~150 nm size) administered subcutaneously. [Ref7393:Goudarzi et al, 2023]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Cu/Zn-SOD Omp31 BP26 multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope subunit vaccine (MEVcob) was designed using reverse vaccinology, combining six CTL epitopes, seven HTL epitopes, and four linear B cell epitopes from CU/ZN-SOD, Omp31, and BP26 proteins, linked with CTB molecular adjuvant and PADRE universal T helper epitope. Efficacy: The vaccine induced statistically significant protection in BALB/c mice challenged with Brucella melitensis 043. Immune response: MEVcob induced elevated levels of IFN-γ, IgG, IgG2a, IgG1, IL-2, and TNF-α in BALB/c mice, indicating specific humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7394:Wang et al, 2024]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct is a 412-amino acid multi-epitope protein including CTL, HTL, and B cell epitopes linked by AAY, GPPGG, and KK linkers, with CTB as molecular adjuvant and PADRE epitope; codon adaptation and computer cloning were performed. [Ref7394:Wang et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus Omp10 recombinant vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to investigate the possibility of using recombinant Lactococcus lactis as a live vector to produce recombinant Brucella abortus Omp10 protein as an oral vaccine against brucellosis. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with L. lactis-pNZ8148-Omp10-Usp45 showed significantly higher Omp10-specific total IgG and IgG1 compared to PBS controls. Vaccinated mice had significantly elevated cytokine levels and reduced inflammatory response, morphological damage, alveolar edema, and lymphocyte infiltration after challenge. Immune response: The vaccine induced strong humoral immunity with increased Omp10-specific IgG and IgG1 antibodies and a mixed cytokine response including elevated IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, and IL-10, indicating activation of both Th1 and Th2 immune responses. [Ref7395:Kazemi-Roudsari et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Omp10 protein using the pNZ8148 vector with Usp45 signal peptide was constructed and administered orally. [Ref7395:Kazemi-Roudsari et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella rOmp25 rEipB subunit vaccine
c_description: The study selected two important vaccine candidate proteins for brucellosis, rOmp25 and rEipB, as models to evaluate recombinant protein production for vaccine purposes. [Ref7396:Akmayan et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins produced in Escherichia coli BL21 expression system. [Ref7396:Akmayan et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis znBM-lacZ vaccine
c_description: Two Brucella melitensis mutants, znBM-lacZ (znBMZ) and znBM-mCherry (znBM-mC), were developed to improve brucellosis vaccination and tested for systemic immunity against virulent B. melitensis challenge. Efficacy: znBMZ vaccination reduced splenic brucellae colonization by approximately 25,000-fold compared to PBS controls, outperforming B. abortus S19 vaccine which reduced colonization by 700-fold. Immune response: Both znBMZ and S19 induced IFN-γ+ CD4+ T cells and CD4+ effector memory T cells; only znBMZ induced IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells and CD8+ effector memory T cells, indicating a broader T cell immunity without booster. [Ref7397:Yang et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutants administered once by intraperitoneal route. [Ref7397:Yang et al, 2024]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; bone-marrow-derived macrophages; human TF-1 myeloid cells

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BP26 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study addresses the urgent need for a safe and effective human vaccine against brucellosis and explores recombinant protein-based subunit vaccines as promising candidates. Efficacy: The vaccine candidate induced strong cellular immune responses and high levels of specific antibodies, suggesting potential protective efficacy. Immune response: Induction of M1 macrophage polarization, stimulation of Th1 and CD8+ T cell responses, high titers of rBP26-specific antibodies, activation and proliferation of T lymphocytes, cytokine production, and maintenance of long-term immune memory. [Ref7398:Wen et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Recombinant BP26 protein expressed in prokaryotic systems combined with the CpG-ODN adjuvant. [Ref7398:Wen et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BtuB and LptD RNA vaccine
c_description: The study designed a novel multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting the extracellular proteins BtuB and LptD of Brucella, aiming to stimulate cellular and humoral immunity using immunoinformatics tools. Immune response: Computer simulations verified the vaccine's potential to stimulate cellular and humoral immune responses by targeting Brucella extracellular proteins. [Ref7399:Shi et al, 2024]
c_preparation: The vaccine was constructed from five cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes, ten helper T lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes, and eight B cell epitopes derived from BtuB and LptD proteins; codon optimization and in silico cloning indicated efficient transcription and translation in E. coli; secondary and tertiary structures were predicted and docked with TLR-4; molecular dynamics simulation confirmed vaccine stability. [Ref7399:Shi et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis gamma irradiated vaccine with Montanide ISA 61 adjuvant
c_description: The study evaluated reactogenicity, antibody responses, and protection of γ-irradiated Brucella ovis antigen formulated with Montanide ISA 61 adjuvant. Efficacy: Montanide ISA 61 formulation induced milder reactogenicity compared to alginate/chitosan and elicited higher levels of IgG2b, an important marker of cellular immune response; protection data not explicitly detailed. Immune response: Induced a high IgG2b/IgG1 ratio compatible with a Th1 profile response and milder local reactogenicity compared to alginate/chitosan formulation. [Ref7400:Silva et al, 2024]
c_preparation: γ-irradiated Brucella ovis antigen formulated with Montanide ISA 61 emulsion adjuvant. [Ref7400:Silva et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multi-epitope OMPs vaccine based on Lactococcus lactis live bacterial vectors
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study developed a novel vaccine strategy using genetically modified Lactococcus lactis to produce a multi-epitope outer membrane proteins (OMPs) peptide of Brucella abortus for oral administration. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed reduced spleen morphological damage, less inflammation, lymphocyte infiltration, and lesions compared to controls. Immune response: Vaccination induced significant IgG1 antibodies specific to OMPs, increased interferon lambda (IFN-λ) and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) levels, and enhanced transcription of interleukin 4 (IL-4) and interleukin 10 (IL-10). [Ref7401:Piri-Gharaghie et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Oral administration of genetically modified Lactococcus lactis expressing a 39 kDa multi-epitope OMPs protein encoded by a plasmid constructed via reverse vaccinology. [Ref7401:Piri-Gharaghie et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to design vaccines and drugs for brucellosis using protein modeling, epitope prediction, and molecular docking of the target proteins BvrR, OMP25, and OMP31. Immune response: Dominant B cell, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and T helper lymphocyte epitopes were predicted for the target proteins, indicating potential immunogenic regions for vaccine design. [Ref7402:Elrashedy et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Tertiary structure models of the three target proteins were constructed and analyzed for epitopes including B cell, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and T helper lymphocyte epitopes; no specific formulation was reported. [Ref7402:Elrashedy et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 delta wzm vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate Rev1Δwzm was developed as a derivative of B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 with a wzm gene deletion, aiming to improve safety and efficacy compared to the conventional Rev. 1 vaccine, especially for use in both young and adult sheep. Efficacy: Rev1Δwzm protected rams against Brucella ovis infection 25 weeks after vaccination, demonstrating effective protection in the target host. Immune response: The vaccine induced a transient serological response in the Rose Bengal test in up to 50% of sheep, confirmed partially by complement fixation test, and elicited a stronger, more persistent anti-rough-LPS antibody response; green fluorescent protein tagging allowed differentiation of vaccinated animals despite serological interference. [Ref7403:Mena-Bueno et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with wzm gene deletion; green fluorescent protein tagging was used to identify vaccinated sheep. [Ref7403:Mena-Bueno et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant EipB protein loaded PLGA nanovaccine
c_description: The study aimed to encapsulate recombinant EipB protein into PLGA nanoparticles to develop a new vaccine candidate addressing limitations of existing Brucellosis vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccine candidate conferred higher than 90% protection from Brucella infection in challenge experiments. Immune response: Both free antigen and nanoparticle formulations induced strong humoral immunity with a threefold increase in Brucella-specific IgG antibodies; stimulated Th1-mediated cellular immunity evidenced by significant increases in IFN-gamma and IL-12 cytokines rather than IL-4. [Ref7404:Akmayan et al, 2024a]
c_preparation: Recombinant EipB protein produced by recombinant DNA technology was encapsulated into PLGA nanoparticles using double emulsion solvent evaporation technique; nanoparticles characterized for size (~274 nm), morphology, zeta potential, polydispersity, release profile (56.1% release by day 14), and encapsulation efficiency. [Ref7404:Akmayan et al, 2024a]
c_model_host: J774 murine macrophage cells; murine splenocytes; mice (in vivo immunization and challenge)

c_vaccine_name: Plant-expressed chimeric core-like particle vaccine presenting Brucella melitensis T cell epitopes
c_description: The study aimed to develop a new-generation vaccine by presenting selected Brucella melitensis T cell epitopes on the surface of Orbivirus core-like particles (CLPs) transiently expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana plants. Efficacy: One of the three chimeric CLPs induced protection against virulent Brucella strain challenge equivalent to the commercial Rev. 1 vaccine; all three were safe at specific antigen doses. [Ref7405:Rutkowska et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Five chimeric CLPs were assembled in plants, each presenting a different T cell epitope; three highest-yielding CLPs were selected for further study. [Ref7405:Rutkowska et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella M epitope oligosaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study reports an efficient synthetic approach to oligosaccharides modeling the M epitope of the Brucella O-polysaccharide, which is unique to Brucella and characterized by α-(1→3)-linkage between d-perosamine units. [Ref7406:Tsvetkov et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Synthesized protected oligosaccharides including a disaccharide, two trisaccharides, and a tetrasaccharide assembled via five glycosylation steps using α-(1→3)-linked disaccharide thioglycoside as the key donor block. [Ref7406:Tsvetkov et al, 2024]
c_antigen: M epitope of the Brucella O-polysaccharide (α-(1→3)-linked d-perosamine oligosaccharides)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella trigger factor BP26 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description:
The study aimed to evaluate immunity induced by a mannosylated niosome containing a recombinant chimeric protein composed of Brucella trigger factor, BP26, and Omp31 in a mouse model. The study evaluated immunity induced by niosome nanoparticles loaded with a recombinant chimeric protein of Brucella trigger factor, BP26, and Omp31 in mice. The study assessed immunity induced by mannosylated niosome nanoparticles loaded with recombinant chimeric Brucella trigger factor/BP26/Omp31 protein in mice. Efficacy: Niosomal and mannosylated niosomal antigen formulations induced higher antibody levels compared to controls. The IgG2a/IgG1 ratio was greater than one for mannosylated niosome-rTBO, indicating a Th1-biased response. Cytokine production was significantly higher in vaccinated groups, especially with intraperitoneal administration, and immunization conferred protection against Brucella challenge. Efficacy: Niosomal antigen induced higher antibody levels and cytokine production than controls; intraperitoneal route showed stronger immune responses. Efficacy: Mannosylated niosomal antigen induced higher antibody titers and cytokine production than controls; IgG2a/IgG1 ratio >1 indicating Th1 response; intraperitoneal route more effective. Immune response: The vaccine stimulated both cellular and humoral immune responses, with increased production of cytokines (IFN-gamma, IL-4, IL-12) and antibodies. The intraperitoneal route elicited stronger cytokine responses than the intranasal route. Immune response: Induced both humoral and cellular immunity with elevated IgG, IgA, and cytokines IFN-gamma, IL-4, and IL-12. Immune response: Stimulated cellular and humoral immunity with increased IFN-gamma, IL-4, IL-12, and antibody levels. [Ref7407:Sharif et al, 2024]
A recombinant chimeric protein was designed by fusing three immunodominant Brucella antigens (trigger factor, Omp31, and Bp26) using EAAAK linkers, synthesized, cloned, and expressed in E. coli. Efficacy: Immunized mice sera contained high levels of IgG antibodies against the recombinant chimeric protein. Immune response: Induction of strong humoral immune response evidenced by high IgG antibody levels in immunized mice. [Ref7230:Abdollahi et al, 2016]
c_adjuvant: yes; niosome; mannosylated niosome | yes; Not reported | yes; niosome | yes; mannosylated niosome
c_preparation:
The recombinant chimeric protein (rTBO) was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified, and loaded onto niosome and mannosylated niosome nanoparticles used as immunoadjuvants. [Ref7407:Sharif et al, 2024]
Purified recombinant chimeric protein combined with an adjuvant (not specified). [Ref7230:Abdollahi et al, 2016]
Recombinant chimeric protein expressed and purified from E. coli was loaded onto niosome nanoparticles. [Ref7407:Sharif et al, 2024]
Recombinant chimeric protein loaded onto mannosylated niosome nanoparticles. [Ref7407:Sharif et al, 2024]
c_antigen: trigger factor; BP26; Omp31 (chimeric protein) | trigger factor (TF), Omp31, Bp26

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis plsC gene deletion vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon sequencing to identify genes essential for Brucella melitensis multiplication in mouse spleen and lungs, selecting genes whose deletion would attenuate the bacteria in the spleen, the main reservoir. Efficacy: The plsC deletion mutant showed protective efficacy similar to the reference Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine but with shorter persistence in the spleen. [Ref7408:Barbieux et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Deletion mutant of the plsC gene, which is involved in phospholipid biosynthesis. [Ref7408:Barbieux et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB9 VirB10 Omp19 Omp25 IgV CTLA-4 subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed to prevent human Brucella infection by combining multiple epitopes from four Brucella proteins with the immunoglobulin variable region of CTLA-4 (IgV_CTLA-4) to enhance immune activation. Efficacy: V_C4MEV demonstrated favorable immunogenicity and antigenicity, showing potential to activate defensive cells and immune responses against Brucella. Immune response: The vaccine showed potential to activate defensive immune cells and elicit immune responses, indicating promising immunogenic properties. [Ref7409:He et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Multiple epitopes including cytotoxic T lymphocyte, helper T lymphocyte, linear B-cell, and conformational B-cell epitopes from VirB9, VirB10, Omp19, and Omp25 were linked together to maintain correct protein folding; the MEV protein was fused with IgV_CTLA-4 to create the vaccine V_C4MEV. [Ref7409:He et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope mRNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to create a novel mRNA vaccine with multiple epitopes targeting Brucella melitensis using proteomics and immunoinformatic tools. Efficacy: The designed mRNA construct was predicted to be effective and promising as a vaccine. Immune response: The immune system's reaction to the novel vaccine was evaluated in silico, indicating potential effectiveness; laboratory and clinical trials are needed for confirmation. [Ref7410:Asadinezhad et al, 2024]
c_preparation: A multi-epitope protein was modeled from selected antigenic proteins and optimized; mRNA was analyzed for structure and stability. [Ref7410:Asadinezhad et al, 2024]
c_antigen: multiple epitopes from seventeen antigenic proteins

c_vaccine_name: Brucella TF BP26 omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: A trivalent candidate antigen formulation containing TF, BP26, and omp31 was designed and evaluated using bioinformatics, cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21, purified, and incorporated into a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS to stimulate selective immune responses. Efficacy: Recombinant protein and nanoparticle formulations induced significant immune responses compared to controls and showed good response upon subsequent injections with live bacterial strains. Immune response: Significant production of IgG1, IgG2a, IFN-γ, IL-12, and IL-4 cytokines indicating stimulation of both cellular and humoral immunity compared to positive and negative control groups. [Ref7411:Iranikhah et al, 2024]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins encapsulated inside a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS; nanoparticle properties such as size, zeta potential, retention rate, diffusion efficacy, and antigen binding were characterized for injection and inhalation delivery in mice. [Ref7411:Iranikhah et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 delta fba delta tal vaccine
c_description: The study proposes that deleting the genes encoding fructose-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba) and transaldolase (Tal) in the Brucella melitensis live-attenuated Rev. 1 vaccine strain blocks erythritol incorporation into central carbon metabolism, potentially reducing placental proliferation and adverse reproductive effects. Efficacy: The Rev1ΔfbaΔtal mutant provided comparable protection to the parental Rev. 1 vaccine in mice. Immune response: Not reported explicitly; however, the mutant showed reduced intracellular fitness and induced fewer adverse reproductive events, suggesting a safer immune profile in pregnant hosts. [Ref7412:Elizalde-Bielsa et al, 2024]
c_preparation: A double mutant of the Rev. 1 strain with deletions in fba and tal genes, unable to metabolize erythritol. [Ref7412:Elizalde-Bielsa et al, 2024]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; BeWo trophoblasts; THP-1 macrophages

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 Omp31 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT70 MPT83 RNA vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to develop a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting Brucella melitensis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis using immunoinformatics approaches, selecting proteins Omp25, Omp31, MPT70, and MPT83 to identify predominant T- and B-cell epitopes. Efficacy: The multi-epitope mRNA vaccine demonstrated increased antigenicity, non-allergenicity, solubility, high stability, and robust binding affinity to TLR4, suggesting potential efficacy. Immune response: Immune modeling predicted variations in innate and adaptive immune cell populations including helper T lymphocytes, cytotoxic T lymphocytes, regulatory T lymphocytes, natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and other immune cell subsets following vaccine administration. [Ref7413:Zhu et al, 2024]
c_preparation: The vaccine was constructed using helper T lymphocyte epitopes, cytotoxic T lymphocyte epitopes, linear B-cell epitopes, and conformational B-cell epitopes; nucleotide sequence optimization achieved a codon adaptation index of 1.0 and average GC content of 54.01%, indicating potential for efficient expression in Escherichia coli. [Ref7413:Zhu et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ABOR recombinant protein subunit vaccine
c_description: A designed recombinant polypeptide composed of five Brucella abortus proteins was produced and evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The ABOR recombinant protein induced a strong Th1 immune response with high levels of specific IgG2a and proinflammatory cytokines compared to control. Immune response: Induction of cellular and humoral immunity characterized by elevated IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-12, TNF-α, and IgG2a, indicating effective stimulation of Th1 immunity. [Ref7415:Saadat et al, 2024]
c_preparation: The recombinant ABOR protein (549 amino acids) combined with chitin as an adjuvant was administered subcutaneously. [Ref7415:Saadat et al, 2024]
c_antigen: MOXR family ATPase-α2, T9SS C-terminal target domain-containing protein, Cobyric acid synthase, Hypothetical protein, VirB11 type IV Secretion protein (combined in ABOR recombinant polypeptide)

c_vaccine_name: purE/purK gene-deletion mutant of Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5
c_description: A two-gene (purE and purK) deletion mutant was constructed in Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5 using homologous recombination to reduce cytotoxicity while maintaining protective efficacy. Efficacy: The mutant vaccine conferred protection against infection with virulent wild-type Brucella melitensis strain 16M comparable to parental strain M5. Immune response: Induced anti-Brucella-specific IgG, secretion of IFN-γ, low IL-6 levels, and mild histopathological changes with reduced cytotoxicity compared to parental strain. [Ref7416:Wang et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5 with purE and purK gene deletions. [Ref7416:Wang et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19 vaccine (conjunctival form, vaccine brand B)
c_description: The vaccine has been used safely for about 100 years; conjunctival form used to provide mucosal immunity and short-term antibody response. Efficacy: No antibody response detected; threshold of 30 ICFTUs observed in one animal. Immune response: No detectable antibody response; rapid decrease in antibody titers compared to subcutaneous vaccines. [Ref7417:Uslu et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Two-dose conjunctival vaccine from vaccine brand B. [Ref7417:Uslu et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multivalent DNA vaccine
c_description: Attenuated live Brucella strains cause side effects and are unsuitable for humans; a safer vaccine was developed by constructing plasmid DNA expressing six Brucella proteins. Efficacy: The single low-dose injection exerted a reliable protective effect against subsequent Brucella challenge. [Ref7418:Khodarovich et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA complexes with linear polyethylenimine to enhance DNA delivery. [Ref7418:Khodarovich et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis delta mapB outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Brucella suis ΔmapB outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) were characterized and evaluated as an acellular vaccine candidate to protect against systemic and mucosal B. suis infection, addressing the lack of available vaccines for swine brucellosis. Efficacy: Immunization with ΔmapB OMVs induced higher antigen-specific IgG titers than wild-type OMVs; antibodies reduced bacterial adherence and invasion and enhanced phagocytosis; ΔmapB OMVs induced stronger Th1 cellular responses; both OMVs conferred protection against intratracheal challenge, but ΔmapB OMVs provided superior protection against intraperitoneal infection. Immune response: ΔmapB OMVs elicited robust humoral immunity with high IgG titers and functional antibodies; cellular immunity was characterized by elevated secretion of interleukin-17 and gamma interferon, indicating a strong T helper 1 response. [Ref7419:González et al, 2024]
c_preparation: OMVs were isolated from B. suis ΔmapB mutant strain using ultracentrifugation and characterized by electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, SDS-PAGE, and proteomics; no adjuvant was reported. [Ref7419:González et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis wild type outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from wild-type B. suis 1330 strain were characterized and evaluated as an acellular vaccine candidate against systemic and mucosal B. suis infection. Efficacy: Immunization induced antigen-specific IgG and functional antibodies that reduced bacterial adherence and invasion and enhanced phagocytosis; conferred protection against intratracheal challenge but was less protective than ΔmapB OMVs against intraperitoneal infection. Immune response: Induced humoral immunity with antigen-specific IgG and functional antibodies; cellular immunity showed lower levels of interleukin-17 and gamma interferon compared to ΔmapB OMVs, indicating a less robust T helper 1 response. [Ref7419:González et al, 2024]
c_preparation: OMVs were isolated from wild-type B. suis using ultracentrifugation and characterized by electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, SDS-PAGE, and proteomics; no adjuvant was reported. [Ref7419:González et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: inactivated Brucella abortus vaccine with oil adjuvant
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an experimentally developed inactivated oil adjuvant Brucella abortus vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced spleen weight and bacterial load compared to unvaccinated controls after challenge (p < 0.001), indicating protective efficacy. Immune response: Vaccinated mice developed Brucella abortus-specific serum IgG from 2 weeks post-vaccination with peak titers at 5-6 weeks (p < 0.001); significant delayed-type hypersensitivity response was observed with increased skin thickness and cellular infiltration in the left footpad (p < 0.001), indicating both humoral and cellular immune responses. [Ref7421:Rahman et al, 2024]
c_preparation: The vaccine contained 1.5 × 10^7 inactivated Brucella abortus biovar 3 cells per 0.1 ml dose with an oil adjuvant. [Ref7421:Rahman et al, 2024]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis BacA gene deletion vaccine
c_description: This study investigated the role of BacA gene deletion in Brucella melitensis LPS to understand its effect on immune response modulation, aiming to advance bacterial vaccines and adjuvants by modifying lipid A. Efficacy: LPS from BacA gene deletion mutant disrupted immune suppression and promoted inflammatory factor production, contrasting with wild-type LPS which suppressed immune response. Immune response: Robust T cell immune response induced by BacA gene deletion LPS, including increased proliferation and differentiation of T cells and production of inflammatory factors. [Ref7423:Zhang et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Lipopolysaccharide extracted from Brucella melitensis BacA gene deletion mutant (Bm-ΔBacA) used to stimulate immune cells. [Ref7423:Zhang et al, 2025]
c_model_host: Bone Marrow-Derived Dendritic Cells; T cells; (in vivo immune response assays)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp19 Omp16 Omp25 L7/L12 multiepitope subunit vaccine
c_description: The study developed a novel IgG-Fc-fused multiepitope vaccine (MEV-Fc) based on immunodominant epitopes of Brucella antigens OMP19, OMP16, OMP25, and L7/L12, identified using an epitope- and structure-based vaccinology platform. Efficacy: MEV-Fc exerted a significant protective effect against Brucella infection compared to the PBS control group. Immune response: MEV-Fc enhanced both Th1 and Th2 immune responses and strongly induced production of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IFN-γ. [Ref7424:Wu et al, 2025]
c_preparation: MEV-Fc was expressed and purified via an Escherichia coli expression system. [Ref7424:Wu et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella inactivated vaccine (CF)
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safer and more effective candidate for brucellosis vaccination by evaluating the efficacy of the Brucella inactivated vaccine CF, addressing the limitations of current live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: CF demonstrated protective efficacy comparable to the S2 vaccine against B. melitensis biovar 3 infection in mice; CF-immunized guinea pigs resisted infection by B. melitensis M28 and B. melitensis biovar 3. Immune response: CF induced significant increases in specific IgG antibody levels against Brucella in early stages; markedly enhanced T cell immune response promoting a Th1-biased immune response in mice; induced both humoral and cellular immunity effectively. [Ref7425:Hu et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Inactivated Brucella melitensis vaccine designated CF; safety and immunogenicity evaluated with various doses and immunization methods. [Ref7425:Hu et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine
c_description: This study developed novel mRNA vaccines targeting the outer membrane protein BP26 of Brucella abortus using lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA (BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP). Efficacy: The BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine induced significantly stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines and markedly reduced splenic bacterial load after challenge. Immune response: The vaccine activated mixed Th1/Th2 immune responses, induced durable immune memory, and provided broader protective coverage compared to conventional alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines. [Ref7426:Liu et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA vaccine encoding BP26 fused with Fc (BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP). [Ref7426:Liu et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine
c_description: This study developed novel mRNA vaccines targeting the outer membrane protein Omp25 of Brucella abortus using lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA (Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP). Efficacy: The Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine induced significantly stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines and markedly reduced splenic bacterial load after challenge. Immune response: The vaccine activated mixed Th1/Th2 immune responses, induced durable immune memory, and provided broader protective coverage compared to conventional alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines. [Ref7426:Liu et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA vaccine encoding Omp25 fused with Fc (Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP). [Ref7426:Liu et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: detoxified lipopolysaccharide-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine
c_description: Detoxified lipopolysaccharide (d-LPS) from Brucella melitensis was prepared and conjugated to tetanus toxoid as a carrier protein to enhance immune responses. Efficacy: Mice immunized with d-LPS-TT showed the strongest protective immune responses against B. melitensis 16M challenge. Immune response: Induced significant IgG2a-specific serum responses targeting polysaccharide components; elevated IL-12 and IFN-γ levels indicating promotion of Th1 type cellular immunity. [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Conjugate of detoxified LPS and tetanus toxoid (d-LPS-TT). [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid conjugate subunit vaccine
c_description: Mixture of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid (OPS+TT) used for immunization. Efficacy: Not explicitly reported; implied less effective than conjugated vaccines. Immune response: Not explicitly detailed for this formulation. [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Non-conjugated mixture of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid. [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: hydrolytic O-polysaccharide-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine
c_description: Hydrolytic O-polysaccharide (OPS) from Brucella melitensis was prepared and conjugated to tetanus toxoid as a carrier protein to enhance immune responses. Efficacy: Mice immunized with OPS-TT demonstrated elevated protective immune responses, though less strong than d-LPS-TT. Immune response: Induced significant IgG2a-specific serum responses targeting polysaccharide components; elevated IL-12 and IFN-γ levels indicating promotion of Th1 type cellular immunity. [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Conjugate of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid (OPS-TT). [Ref7427:Khoramabadi et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: FcRn-targeted mucosal Brucella vaccine with multi-epitope fusion (h-tFc-MEV)
c_description: The study developed a recombinant antigen by fusing the human Fc domain with Brucella's multi-epitope protein to target FcRn for mucosal vaccine delivery. Efficacy: Oral delivery elicited enhanced systemic immunity with elevated serum IgG titers, increased CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratios, significant mucosal IgA upregulation, long-term immune memory lasting six months, and markedly reduced Brucella colonization in visceral organs after challenge. Immune response: The vaccine induced robust systemic and mucosal immunity, including elevated serum IgG, increased mucosal IgA, enhanced CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratios, and FcRn-mediated dendritic cell activation with increased MHC-II expression and antigen presentation efficiency. [Ref7428:Tian et al, 2025]
c_preparation: The vaccine was delivered orally via chitosan nanoparticles. [Ref7428:Tian et al, 2025]
c_antigen: multi-epitope protein (MEV) fused with human Fc domain

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 and D15 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed using reverse vaccinology methodology focusing on Omp19 and D15 antigens to prevent Brucella infection. Efficacy: The MEV exhibited a significant level of immunogenicity based on in silico analyses. Immune response: Identification of CTL, HTL, and B cell epitopes suggests potential to induce cellular and humoral immune responses; adjuvants added to enhance immunogenicity. [Ref7429:Gharazi et al, 2025]
c_adjuvant: yes; adjuvants added to N-terminal of vaccine peptide (specific adjuvant names not reported)
c_preparation: The MEV construct consists of 387 amino acids including 2 CTL epitopes, 2 HTL epitopes, and 2 linear B cell epitopes from Omp19 and D15, connected by GGGS and EAAAK linkers; adjuvants were added to the N-terminal to enhance immunogenicity. [Ref7429:Gharazi et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis UGPase deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study identifies UGPase as a critical determinant of Brucella virulence and immunogenicity, demonstrating that deletion of UGPase disrupts LPS synthesis, leading to a rough phenotype and reduced virulence. Efficacy: The UGPase deletion mutant showed impaired ability to infect host cells, diminished pathogenicity in mice, altered LPS structure with reduced binding to Brucella-positive serum, and induced a protective pro-inflammatory cytokine profile. Immune response: Infection with the mutant strain led to upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-ɑ, IFN-γ, and IL-2, and downregulation of anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-10 and IL-4 in mice; macrophages infected with the mutant exhibited decreased inflammatory response compared to wild-type infection. [Ref7430:Chen et al, 2025]
c_preparation: A Brucella melitensis 16M strain with UGPase gene deletion (16M-ΔUGPase) was used as the vaccine candidate. [Ref7430:Chen et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Lpp-OmpA BtaE subunit vaccine
c_description: This study examined the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the Lpp-OmpA-BtaE fusion protein co-administered with Freund's adjuvant in protecting against Brucella melitensis infection in a murine model. Efficacy: Vaccination with Lpp-OmpA-BtaE plus Freund's adjuvant conferred superior protection compared to Lpp-OmpA plus BtaE alone, significantly reducing bacterial burdens in spleens of infected mice. Immune response: Immunization elicited robust B-cell responses with a Th1-biased antibody profile (elevated IgG2a/IgG1 ratios), increased interferon-γ/interleukin-4 levels, and increased CD8+/CD4+ T-cell ratio, indicating strong cell-mediated immunity. [Ref7431:Nobari et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Fusion protein of lipoprotein outer membrane protein A (Lpp-OmpA) with Brucella trimeric autotransporter E (BtaE) combined with Freund's adjuvant. [Ref7431:Nobari et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB2 VirB3 VirB6 BtpA RNA vaccine
c_description: This study develops a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting the Brucella type IV secretion system using reverse vaccinology and bioinformatics tools. Efficacy: Computational results indicate the vaccine effectively stimulates an immune response with stable interaction to TLR4 (docking score -350.15); however, no wet lab validation yet. Immune response: Predicted robust antigenicity of selected proteins and stable vaccine-TLR4 binding suggest potential to stimulate immune response; experimental confirmation pending. [Ref7432:Luo et al, 2025]
c_preparation: The vaccine includes epitopes from VirB2, VirB3, VirB6, and BtpA proteins linked appropriately for mRNA vaccine design; molecular docking and dynamics simulations were used to optimize vaccine-TLR4 interactions. [Ref7432:Luo et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain G16 vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G16 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G16 showed immune protection levels matching the reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. Immune response: Immunized mice produced predominantly IgG2a-dominated Th1-type responses; macrophage activation was induced; LPS-ELISA differentiated vaccinated from infected animals. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G16 with semi-rough phenotype retaining partial O-antigen. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain G7 vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G7 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G7 showed immune protection levels matching the reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. Immune response: Immunized mice produced predominantly IgG2a-dominated Th1-type responses; macrophage activation was induced; LPS-ELISA differentiated vaccinated from infected animals. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G7 with complete rough phenotype. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain G8 vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G8 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G8 showed slightly lower immune protection efficacy compared to reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. Immune response: Immunized mice produced predominantly IgG2a-dominated Th1-type responses; macrophage activation was induced; LPS-ELISA differentiated vaccinated from infected animals. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G8 with complete rough phenotype. [Ref7433:Liu et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella-infected macrophage-derived Exosomes vaccine
c_description: This study explored the significance of exosomes derived from Brucella-infected macrophages in the context of Brucella infection and their influence on host immune responses, proposing their potential as innovative vaccines or immune adjuvants for brucellosis. Efficacy: Exosomes enhanced the host's anti-Brucella immune response and inhibited intracellular bacterial survival. Immune response: Exosomes played an important role in immune regulation during Brucella infection by transmitting antigens between immune cells to initiate an adaptive immune response against Brucella. [Ref7434:Zhang et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Exosomes derived from Brucella-infected macrophages. [Ref7434:Zhang et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp19 SodC recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aims to develop a new human brucellosis vaccine using recombinant capripoxvirus vectors expressing Brucella antigens. [Ref7435:Amanova et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Recombinant capripoxvirus SPPV (TK-) expressing OMP19 and SODC antigens cultivated in Vero cells using BelloStage™-3000 bioreactor with BioNOC II® macrocarriers. [Ref7435:Amanova et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25 recombinant capripoxvirus vector vaccine
c_description: The study aims to develop a new human brucellosis vaccine using recombinant capripoxvirus vectors expressing Brucella antigens. [Ref7435:Amanova et al, 2025]
c_preparation: Recombinant capripoxvirus SPPV (TK-) expressing OMP25 antigen cultivated in Vero cells using BelloStage™-3000 bioreactor with BioNOC II® macrocarriers. [Ref7435:Amanova et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: ferritin-based bioconjugate nanovaccine (Fn-OPS)
c_description: The study developed a bioconjugate nanovaccine by enzymatically coupling Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 O-specific polysaccharide, a structural analogue of Brucella antigens, to a self-assembled ferritin nanoparticle, creating a stable and monodisperse nanoparticle platform for targeted antigen delivery. Efficacy: The vaccine induced a robust immune response that provided strong protection against Brucella infection in mice. Immune response: Immunization activated T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and germinal center B cells, leading to high-titer IgG antibodies cross-reactive with Brucella lipopolysaccharide. [Ref7436:Li et al, 2025]
c_preparation: A ferritin nanoparticle platform conjugated with Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 O-specific polysaccharide via bacterial glycosylation-driven synthetic strategy, forming a bioconjugate nanovaccine (Fn-OPS) with stability at room temperature and confirmed in vivo safety. [Ref7436:Li et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: multi-epitope recombinant BCG vaccine targeting Brucella OMP31, LptE and VirB2
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed using reverse vaccinology targeting three immunogenic proteins of Brucella melitensis: OMP31, LptE, and VirB2. Molecular adjuvants cholera toxin B subunit and PADRE were incorporated to enhance immunogenicity, and TAT cell-penetrating peptides were added to improve intracellular delivery. Efficacy: Simulations showed potent immune activation with significant increases in cytotoxic T cells (1050 cells/mm³), memory helper T cells (1150 cells/mm³), and IFN-γ production (2 × 10^6 ng/ml), along with sustained IgG/IgM titers over 350 days (1 × 10^5 cells/mm³). Experimental validation of immunological efficacy is pending. Immune response: The vaccine induced strong cellular immune responses including cytotoxic and memory helper T cells, high IFN-γ production, and sustained humoral responses with IgG and IgM antibodies. [Ref7437:Li et al, 2025a]
c_adjuvant: yes; cholera toxin B subunit and PADRE
c_preparation: The MEV includes six CTL epitopes, nine HTL epitopes, seven linear B-cell epitopes, and five conformational B-cell epitopes. Structural optimization involved disulfide bond engineering to improve molecular stability. The codon-optimized MEV sequence was cloned in silico into the pMV261 shuttle vector to generate a recombinant BCG construct. [Ref7437:Li et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis vtlR mutant vaccine
c_description: The vtlR mutant strain of Brucella melitensis M5 was constructed and shown to be essential for virulence, with deletion impairing bacterial growth on certain sugars and increasing sensitivity to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Efficacy: The vtlR mutant strain showed reduced intracellular survival and triggered reactive oxygen species production; importantly, it elicited protective immunity in mice. Immune response: The mutant strain induced protective immunity in mice, associated with increased reactive oxygen species production in macrophages. [Ref7438:Wang et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vtlR deletion mutant strain of Brucella melitensis M5 [Ref7438:Wang et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: vaccine candidate consisting of recombinant antigens OMP19 and L7/L12 loaded in a nanoliposomal adjuvant system
c_description: A vaccine candidate was developed composed of two recombinant antigens, OMP19 and L7/L12 of Brucella melitensis, encapsulated in a nanoliposomal adjuvant system. Efficacy: The liposome-OMP19&L7/L12 formulation showed the highest reduction of Brucella melitensis in mouse spleens (2.43 and 1.44 log units of protection) after first and second protection assays, outperforming PBS, liposome alone, protein mixture alone, and Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. Immune response: The vaccine induced significant Th1 (IgG2a, IFN-γ, IL-2) and Th2 (IgG1, IL-4) responses, with a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio indicating a Th1 bias; subcutaneous administration did not significantly increase IgA compared to protein mixture alone, suggesting mucosal routes may be needed for IgA induction. [Ref7440:Pirhajati et al, 2026]
c_preparation: The antigens were encapsulated in a nanoliposomal adjuvant system forming monodisperse spherical nanoparticles approximately 123 nm in size with about 71% encapsulation efficacy and 65% antigen release rate. [Ref7440:Pirhajati et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BspH subunit vaccine
c_description: The secreted effector protein BspH was cloned, expressed, and purified as a recombinant protein (rBspH) to assess its immunocompetence. Efficacy: Immunization with rBspH conferred significant protection against subsequent challenge with B. abortus A19. Immune response: rBspH stimulation induced production of H+ and Ca2+ ions (not H2O2) in macrophages; triggered secretion of both Th1 and Th2-associated cytokines; immunized mice showed robust humoral response with specific IgG and elevated Th1 and Th2 cytokines. [Ref7441:Shi et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Recombinant BspH protein used for immunization; adjuvant use not reported. [Ref7441:Shi et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus OMVBru-M3 vaccine
c_description: Native OMVs from wild-type Brucella abortus were characterized and shown to enhance bacterial invasion and intracellular survival in macrophages and increase pathogenicity in mice. Efficacy: Native OMVs showed low yield and limited immunogenicity; no effective protection reported. Immune response: Native OMVs modulated macrophage polarization but elicited weaker immune responses compared to OMVBru-M3. [Ref7442:Huang et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Biological nanoparticles (outer-membrane vesicles) derived from wild-type Brucella abortus. [Ref7442:Huang et al, 2025a]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain delta eipB delta per delta wadC vaccine
c_description: The study engineered a recombinant Brucella abortus strain Bru-M3 by deleting eipB, per, and wadC genes to remodel noncanonical LPS and produce outer-membrane vesicles (OMVs) at higher yield and enhanced immunogenicity compared to wild-type OMVs. Efficacy: OMVBru-M3 vaccination conferred better protection against Brucella abortus challenge, improved bacterial clearance, and reduced tissue damage compared to wild-type OMVs. Immune response: Vaccination elicited stronger humoral responses and IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells, with elevated inflammatory cytokine production and modulation of macrophage polarization. [Ref7442:Huang et al, 2025a]
c_preparation: Biological nanoparticles (outer-membrane vesicles) derived from the recombinant Bru-M3 strain (OMVBru-M3). [Ref7442:Huang et al, 2025a]
c_antigen: eipB deletion; per deletion; wadC deletion; noncanonical lipopolysaccharide (LPS) remodeling

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with MONTANIDE ISA 61 VG adjuvant
c_description: The study evaluated immunologic responses and protection against experimental challenge in goats vaccinated with LPS combined with ISA 61 VG adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccination with LPS + ISA 61 VG did not confer protection against abortion, uterine, fetal, mammary, or maternal infection compared to controls. Immune response: LPS + ISA 61 VG induced significantly greater antibody responses and lymphocyte proliferative responses to LPS antigen than LPS alone; however, T cell proliferation and antigen-specific IFN-γ production were negligible and not different from controls. [Ref7443:Naseer et al, 2025]
c_preparation: LPS from B. melitensis strain 16M formulated with MONTANIDE™ ISA 61 VG adjuvant. [Ref7443:Naseer et al, 2025]
c_model_host: Capra hircus; peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella melitensis purD deletion vaccine
c_description: The study constructed a purD gene deletion mutant in Brucella melitensis M5 strain to investigate the role of de novo purine biosynthesis in virulence and intracellular survival. Efficacy: The purD mutant showed impaired growth, increased sensitivity to detergent, reduced membrane permeability, altered lipid biosynthesis, decreased ability to invade and survive in host cells, and reduced colonization and pathology in mice. [Ref7444:Yang et al, 2025]
c_preparation: A live attenuated strain with deletion of the purD gene, impairing purine biosynthesis. [Ref7444:Yang et al, 2025]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP2a OMP2b OMP1 OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study designed a multi-epitope vaccine targeting conserved regions of Brucella outer membrane proteins OMP2a, OMP2b, OMP1, OMP25, and OMP31 using immunoinformatics approaches, aiming to overcome drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: The vaccine construct demonstrated antigenicity, non-allergenicity, and stable binding to TLR2 and TLR4 receptors in silico, with immune simulations indicating potential to induce immune responses; however, efficacy requires validation in laboratory and animal models. Immune response: The multi-epitope vaccine candidate is predicted to elicit helper T-lymphocyte, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, and B-cell responses, with molecular docking and dynamics supporting stable interaction with toll-like receptors, suggesting activation of innate and adaptive immunity. [Ref7445:Doostmohammadi et al, 2026]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct consists of selected HTL, CTL, and B-cell epitopes connected by flexible linkers (GGSSGG), fused at the N-terminus to Cholera Toxin B subunit as an adjuvant, and includes a His-tag at the C-terminus for purification; the tertiary structure was modeled and refined in silico. [Ref7445:Doostmohammadi et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Hsp60 PEP1 peptide vaccine
c_description: A novel PrPC-binding peptide, PEP1, derived from Brucella abortus Hsp60 was identified through computational docking and structure-guided approaches to target receptor-mediated mucosal antigen uptake. Efficacy: Fusion of PEP1 to a model protein resulted in increased mucosal IgA and systemic IgG responses compared to the untargeted protein. Immune response: Enhanced mucosal IgA and systemic IgG responses were observed, indicating effective receptor-mediated antigen uptake through M cells. [Ref7446:Pham et al, 2026]
c_preparation: PEP1 was fused to a model protein to enable receptor-mediated targeting to intestinal M-cell-associated regions. [Ref7446:Pham et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5 macrophage microparticle subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigates microparticles (MPs) released from macrophages infected with the attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5, exploring their role in enhancing host defense and adaptive immunity against Brucella. Efficacy: MPs promoted bacterial clearance and restricted intracellular survival; elicited potent Th1-polarized immunity with elevated IgG2a and IFN-γ; activated NF-κB pathway in dendritic cells enhancing IL-12 and TNF-α secretion; primed cytotoxic T lymphocytes for specific lysis of Brucella-infected targets. Immune response: Th1-polarized immunity characterized by increased IgG2a titers and IFN-γ production; activation of NF-κB pathway in dendritic cells; increased IL-12 and TNF-α secretion; priming of cytotoxic T lymphocytes via direct and indirect pathways. [Ref7447:Zhang et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Microparticles derived from macrophages infected with Brucella melitensis strain M5. [Ref7447:Zhang et al, 2026]
c_model_host: Mus musculus; RAW264.7 macrophages; bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella abortus strain A19 btpB deletion vaccine
c_description: A btpB mutant strain of Brucella abortus strain A19 (ΔbtpB) was constructed by homologous recombination to investigate its biological characteristics, virulence, and immunogenicity. Efficacy: ΔbtpB showed reduced virulence with weaker splenic pathological damage and significantly lower splenic bacterial load compared to wild-type A19, indicating accelerated clearance in the host. Immune response: ΔbtpB induced stronger humoral and cellular immune responses including higher antibody levels, increased Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2), enhanced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activity, stronger early Th1 and Th2 responses with a later decline in Th2, and significantly enhanced NK cell cytotoxic activity compared to wild-type A19. [Ref7448:Yuan et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain A19 with btpB gene deletion. [Ref7448:Yuan et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: attenuated B. ovis ΔabcBA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is an attenuated live vaccine model with deletion of abcBA genes. Efficacy: β-glucan training did not enhance the efficacy of this attenuated vaccine; trained innate immunity exerted a detrimental influence on its efficacy. Immune response: Trained innate immunity induced by β-glucan or zymosan was evaluated; β-glucan reduced bacterial infection in vitro and in vivo but did not improve protection with this vaccine. [Ref7449:Oliveira et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vaccine based on Brucella ovis ΔabcBA mutant. [Ref7449:Oliveira et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: gamma-irradiated B. ovis vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is an inactivated formulation prepared by gamma irradiation of Brucella ovis. Efficacy: β-glucan training markedly reduced bacterial colonization in mice vaccinated with this inactivated vaccine. Immune response: Trained innate immunity induced by β-glucan enhanced the protective effect of this inactivated vaccine. [Ref7449:Oliveira et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Gamma-irradiated inactivated vaccine. [Ref7449:Oliveira et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella attenuated vaccine strain BA0711
c_description: The study aimed to elucidate the genetic basis of virulence attenuation in the Brucella attenuated vaccine strain BA0711 by whole-genome sequencing and comparison with the Brucella wild-type strain M28. Efficacy: The vaccine strain BA0711 maintains strong host adaptability, viability, and immunogenicity despite genetic mutations and deletions. [Ref7450:Xie et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis strain H38 delta wbkF delta wadB vaccine
c_description: Mutants of H38ΔwbkF vaccine with additional deletions in wadB or wadC genes, altering sugars of the rough LPS core tetrasaccharide branch, were constructed to minimize serological interference. Efficacy: These core-defective mutants were over-attenuated and failed to protect mice against infection. Immune response: Not reported beyond attenuation and protection failure. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutants with deletions in wbkF plus wadB or wadC genes; administered subcutaneously in mice. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_antigen: wbkF deletion; wadB deletion; wadC deletion

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella ovis strain H38 delta wbkF delta wadC vaccine
c_description: Mutants of H38ΔwbkF vaccine with additional deletions in wadB or wadC genes, altering sugars of the rough LPS core tetrasaccharide branch, were constructed to minimize serological interference. Efficacy: These core-defective mutants were over-attenuated and failed to protect mice against infection. Immune response: Not reported beyond attenuation and protection failure. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutants with deletions in wbkF plus wadB or wadC genes; administered subcutaneously in mice. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_antigen: wbkF deletion; wadB deletion; wadC deletion

c_vaccine_name: H38ΔwbkF rough vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a rough mutant of Brucella melitensis strain H38 with deletion of wbkF gene, previously shown to protect rams against B. ovis infection without interfering in S-LPS-based serological tests. Efficacy: H38ΔwbkF vaccine protected rams against B. ovis infection similarly to B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine; core-defective mutants (wadB and wadC deletions) were over-attenuated and failed to protect mice; conjunctival administration preserved efficacy in rams. Immune response: H38ΔwbkF induced antibodies to rough LPS that interfered with B. ovis serological tests; conjunctival administration significantly reduced this serological interference compared to subcutaneous route. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain H38ΔwbkF administered by subcutaneous or conjunctival routes; conjunctival administration explored to reduce serological interference. [Ref7451:Lopez et al, 2026]
c_antigen: wbkF deletion; wadB deletion; wadC deletion (mutants studied)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 and Omp19 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding omp16 and omp19 genes of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a novel vaccine candidate. Immune response: Expression of Omp16 and Omp19 proteins was confirmed; purified recombinant proteins showed good immunogenicity with specific binding to patient serum antibodies; Omp16 had stronger immunogenicity than Omp19; epitope prediction identified multiple epitopes; simulated immunization activated CD4+ and CD8+ T cells significantly. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmids pIVTRup-omp16 and pIVTRup-omp19 were used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA fragments encoding Omp16 and Omp19 proteins. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis omp16 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding the omp16 gene of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a vaccine candidate. Immune response: Omp16 protein expression confirmed; recombinant Omp16 showed strong immunogenicity with specific antibody binding; contained seven predicted epitopes; simulated immunization significantly activated CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pIVTRup-omp16 was used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA encoding Omp16 protein. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis omp19 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding the omp19 gene of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a vaccine candidate. Immune response: Omp19 protein expression confirmed; recombinant Omp19 showed good immunogenicity with specific antibody binding; contained six predicted epitopes; simulated immunization significantly activated CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pIVTRup-omp19 was used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA encoding Omp19 protein. [Ref7452:Zhang et al, 2026a]

c_vaccine_name: A19-∆VirB12 vaccine strain
c_description: The A19-∆VirB12 vaccine strain is a recently developed Brucella abortus vaccine strain carrying a deletion of the VirB12 gene, which complicates serological differentiation from wild-type infections. [Ref7453:Liang et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: rWbkC multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine was designed using immunoinformatics methods targeting the WbkC protein, a methyltransferase involved in O-antigen biosynthesis of Brucella lipopolysaccharide, known to stimulate strong immune responses in mice. Efficacy: Vaccination with rWbkC significantly reduced bacterial loads in spleen and liver compared to PBS control (p < 0.001); rWbkC showed superior clearance of bacterial burden in liver compared to WbkC protein alone (p < 0.01). Immune response: rWbkC induced significantly higher IgG and IgG1 antibody levels than WbkC protein; immune simulation predicted elevated IFN-γ, IL-2, and IgG/IgM levels, indicating strong cellular and humoral immune responses. [Ref7455:Lian et al, 2026]
c_preparation: Immunodominant linear B lymphocyte, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and helper T lymphocyte epitopes of WbkC were linked with short connectors to construct the recombinant protein rWbkC; bioinformatics predicted high antigenicity, solubility, and no allergenicity or toxicity; molecular docking showed stable binding to TLR2/4. [Ref7455:Lian et al, 2026]

c_vaccine_name: attenuated B. melitensis vaccine M5-90
c_description: The attenuated Brucella melitensis vaccine M5-90 is currently used to vaccinate animals in China. Efficacy: Specific T-cell response induced by the M5-90 vaccine was relatively weak and did not sustain long enough, possibly due to rapid activation of T-regulatory cells following vaccination. Immune response: Low levels of antibodies to BP26 and OMP31 detected; specific IFN-γ responses quantified; identification of multiple T-cell epitopes reactive in vaccinated sheep; some epitope reactivity associated with MHC-I B allele. [Ref7160:Wang et al, 2014a]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vaccine based on Brucella melitensis strain M5-90. [Ref7160:Wang et al, 2014a]

c_vaccine_name: recombinant Omp25 protein loaded PLGA nanovaccine
c_description: The study aimed to encapsulate recombinant Omp25 protein into PLGA nanoparticles to develop a new vaccine candidate addressing limitations of existing Brucellosis vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccine candidate conferred higher than 90% protection from Brucella infection in challenge experiments. Immune response: Both free antigen and nanoparticle formulations induced strong humoral immunity with a threefold increase in Brucella-specific IgG antibodies; stimulated Th1-mediated cellular immunity evidenced by significant increases in IFN-gamma and IL-12 cytokines rather than IL-4. [Ref7404:Akmayan et al, 2024a]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp25 protein produced by recombinant DNA technology was encapsulated into PLGA nanoparticles using double emulsion solvent evaporation technique; nanoparticles characterized for size (~221 nm), morphology, zeta potential, polydispersity, release profile (90.39% release by day 14), and encapsulation efficiency. [Ref7404:Akmayan et al, 2024a]
c_model_host: J774 murine macrophage cells; murine splenocytes; mice (in vivo immunization and challenge)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis high hydrophobic antigenic complex subunit vaccine encapsulated in microparticles
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the effect of excipients facilitating encapsulation of a hydrophobic antigenic complex from Brucella ovis on microparticle properties and to assess protective ability against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: The subcellular vaccine induced protection similar to that of the live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref691:Estevan et al., 2006]
c_preparation: Poly(epsilon-caprolactone) microparticles containing the hydrophobic antigenic complex (HS) were prepared by solvent extraction/evaporation using a total recirculation one-machine system; excipients beta-cyclodextrin and Pluronic F68 were used to enhance antigen loading and preserve bioactivity. [Ref691:Estevan et al., 2006]
c_antigen: high hydrophobic antigenic complex extracted from Brucella ovis (HS)

c_vaccine_name: live attenuated Brucella neotomae SOD gamma irradiated vaccine
c_description: Recombinant B. neotomae overexpressing superoxide dismutase was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent Brucella species. Immune response: Induction of antigen-specific antibody and T cell responses. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation. [Ref7114:Moustafa et al, 2011]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus virB10 Omp31 Omp16 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study designed a multi-epitope vaccine targeting B. melitensis and B. abortus using virB10, Omp31, and Omp16 antigens, incorporating predicted T lymphocyte, cytotoxic T cell, and IFN-γ epitopes. The 50S L7/L12 ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis was included as a bovine TLR4 and TLR9 agonist to enhance immune stimulation. Efficacy: The construct showed stable interaction with bovine TLR4 and TLR9 receptors, suggesting potential to induce immune responses. No in vivo efficacy data reported. Immune response: The vaccine is predicted to stimulate T- and B-cell responses by presenting multiple epitopes and activating innate immunity via TLR4 and TLR9 agonism, potentially inducing IFN-γ production. [Ref7377:Rahimnahal et al, 2023]
c_adjuvant: yes; 50S L7/L12 Ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (bovine TLR4 and TLR9 agonist)
c_preparation: The multi-epitope construct was linked with GPGPG, AAY, and KK linkers, cloned into the pET-32a shuttle vector using BamHI and HindIII restriction sites, and expressed as a soluble ∼82 kDa protein in Escherichia coli SHuffle host. [Ref7377:Rahimnahal et al, 2023]
c_antigen: virB10; Omp31; Omp16; 50S L7/L12 Ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis
c_model_host: Escherichia coli SHuffle; (in silico models for docking and simulation)
